knowledge_statements.title: Conic Representability Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD-based exact SOC representability test for an unrestricted convex quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+r\le0\), where \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). If \(Q\succeq0\), choose \(R\) such that \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) and introduce \(s=-2q^{\mathsf T}x-r\). The quadratic inequality is equivalent to \[\left\|\begin{pmatrix}2Rx\\s-1\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\le s+1,\qquad s=-2q^{\mathsf T}x-r.\] If \(Q\) has a negative eigenvalue, this unrestricted PSD-factorization test fails; representability under domain restrictions or other reformulations requires separate analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic inequality with a positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix has an exact SOC representation obtained from a matrix factorization and an affine bound variable. An indefinite matrix fails this particular unrestricted test.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+r\le0\), with \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\).
Representability is sought using continuous affine equations and standard second-order cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q\succeq0\), the displayed quadratic inequality has the stated exact second-order cone representation.

notation.meaning: affine upper bound on the squared norm

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric matrix \(Q\). Compute a spectral decomposition \(Q=V\Lambda V^{\mathsf T}\), or a symmetric pivoted \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization, and determine the inertia \((n_+,n_-,n_0)\). If \(n_-=0\), form \(R=\Lambda_+^{1/2}V_+^{\mathsf T}\), so \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\), and return \(R\) for conic modeling. Stop after returning either the factor or the negative-curvature witness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for exact formulations using only continuous convex-conic lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) and \(S=\{(x_1,x_2,t):t\ge x_1^2-x_2^2\}\). The points \((0,1,-1)\) and \((0,-1,-1)\) belong to \(S\), but their midpoint \((0,0,-1)\) does not; hence \(S\) is nonconvex. Any set described by affine equations and convex cone membership is convex, and every linear projection of such a set is convex. Therefore \(S\) cannot have an exact formulation using only continuous affine lifts and convex cones. Indefinite quadratic structure requires additional domain restrictions, discrete disjunctions, or a nonconvex representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite quadratic epigraph can be nonconvex, so no exact formulation using only continuous convex-conic lifts can represent it.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Quadratic Structure Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Big-M Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary activation of one nonlinear inequality over a bounded reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(g:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(y\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether \(g(x)\le 0\) is active. If \(M\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(M\ge\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\), then the implication \(y=1\Rightarrow g(x)\le 0\) is represented by
\[
x\in X,\qquad g(x)\le M(1-y),\qquad y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For \(y=1\), the inequality reduces to \(g(x)\le0\); for \(y=0\), it is valid for every \(x\in X\). Thus its integer feasible set equals the implication-defined set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid finite upper bound on the nonlinear expression converts a binary implication into one big-M inequality without changing integer feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(M\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(M\ge\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\).

notation.meaning: reference domain of the continuous variables
valid finite upper bound on g over X

children.title: Big-M Bound-Quality Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.title: Big-M Bound-Quality Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of valid big-M values on the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M_2\ge M_1\ge\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\), define
\[
P(M):=\{(x,y):x\in X,\ 0\le y\le1,\ g(x)\le M(1-y)\}.
\]
Then \(P(M_1)\subseteq P(M_2)\). Consequently, for any minimization objective \(f(x,y)\),
\[
\inf_{(x,y)\in P(M_2)}f(x,y)\le\inf_{(x,y)\in P(M_1)}f(x,y).
\]
Hence the smallest valid \(M\) gives the strongest member of this relaxation family, while enlarging \(M\) cannot improve its lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger valid big-M constants enlarge the continuous relaxation and cannot improve its minimization lower bound; the smallest valid constant is strongest.
assumptions_latex: \(M_2\ge M_1\ge\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\).
The binary variable is relaxed to \(0\le y\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(M_1)\subseteq P(M_2)\) and, for minimization, \(v(M_2)\le v(M_1)\).

notation.meaning: continuous big-M relaxation using constant M
infimum of the chosen objective over P(M)

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Disjunctive Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended convex-hull formulation for a finite union of compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets. The convex hull of their union is the projection onto \(x\) of
\[
x=\sum_{i=1}^k v_i,\qquad v_i\in\lambda_iS_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kS_i\right)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i s_i:\lambda\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ s_i\in S_i\right\}.
\]
If \(S_i\) has a convex nonlinear description, membership in \(\lambda_iS_i\) may be imposed through its closed perspective formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated copies and simplex weights give an extended formulation whose projection is exactly the convex hull of a finite union of compact convex sets.
assumptions_latex: \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex for every \(i\).
The union contains finitely many disjuncts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,v,\lambda):x=\sum_i v_i,\ v_i\in\lambda_iS_i,\ \lambda\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1\}=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iS_i).\)

notation.meaning: convex set associated with disjunct i
disaggregated scaled copy of the continuous vector

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical interface for finite alternatives containing nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized disjunctive program consists of continuous variables \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), Boolean indicators \(Y_{ik}\), global constraints \(r(x)\le0\), and disjunctions
\[
\bigvee_{i\in D_k}\left[Y_{ik}\ \wedge\ g_{ik}(x)\le0\right],\qquad k=1,\ldots,K,
\]
together with a Boolean formula \(\Omega(Y)\). Its feasible set contains precisely those \(x\in X\) for which a truth assignment satisfies \(\Omega\), the global constraints, and at least one selected alternative in every disjunction. Replacing \(Y_{ik}\) by binary variables permits big-M or convex-hull mixed-integer reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GDP models nonlinear alternatives with Boolean indicators, disjunctions, global constraints, and a logical formula, providing an interface to mixed-integer reformulations.
assumptions_latex: Each index set \(D_k\) is finite.
Every displayed nonlinear constraint is defined on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is GDP-feasible exactly when there exists \(Y\) satisfying \(\Omega(Y)\), \(r(x)\le0\), and every indexed disjunction.

notation.meaning: set of alternatives in disjunction k
Boolean indicator selecting alternative i in disjunction k

knowledge_statements.title: Primitive-Operator Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed acyclic representation of a factorable nonlinear expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primitive-operator graph for a factorable expression \(F(x)\) is a directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\). Its leaves represent variables or constants; every nonleaf \(v\) has ordered predecessors \(p_1(v),\ldots,p_{d_v}(v)\) and a primitive operator \(\phi_v\); and its value is recursively
\[
t_v=\phi_v\bigl(t_{p_1(v)},\ldots,t_{p_{d_v}(v)}\bigr).
\]
One or more designated roots return the components of \(F(x)\). Shared subexpressions may be represented by a single vertex with multiple outgoing arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primitive-operator graph is a DAG whose leaves are inputs and whose internal vertices recursively apply elementary operators to compute the nonlinear expression.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is factorable into finitely many supported primitive operators.
The dependency graph is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)\) equals the value at the designated root vertices obtained by a topological evaluation of \(G\).

notation.meaning: primitive operator assigned to vertex v

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports primitive-operator expression graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended formulation obtained by assigning variables to expression-graph vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a primitive-operator graph \(G=(V,E)\), introduce an auxiliary variable \(z_v\) for every noninput vertex. For each such vertex impose
\[
z_v=\phi_v\bigl(z_{p_1(v)},\ldots,z_{p_{d_v}(v)}\bigr),
\]
with input coordinates identified with \(x\). Replace every occurrence of the original expression by its root variable. If all graph equalities are enforced exactly, projection of the resulting extended feasible set onto the original variables equals the feasible set of the undecomposed nonlinear model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assigning one auxiliary variable and defining equality to each internal graph vertex yields an exact extended formulation of a factorable expression.
assumptions_latex: The primitive graph is finite and acyclic.
Every operator equality is imposed on its proper domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{graph}})=\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{original}}.\)

notation.meaning: auxiliary variable representing the value at vertex v
feasible set of the extended graph formulation

children.title: Expression-Graph Granularity
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing the size and resolution of extended expression graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal measure of how an expression is partitioned into graph operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an expression tree \(T\), an expression-graph granularity is a partition \(\mathcal{P}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) of its operator vertices into connected blocks such that contracting every block produces an acyclic quotient graph. Each block is treated as one composite graph operator. The granularity may be summarized by
\[
\gamma(\mathcal{P})=\left(m,\ \max_{B\in\mathcal{P}}|B|\right).
\]
A refinement splits blocks without merging vertices from different blocks; the finest partition has one operator vertex per block, while the coarsest admissible partition treats the complete expression as one block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression-graph granularity is the admissible partition of an expression tree into composite operators, ranging from one whole-expression block to individual primitive vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite expression tree.
Each block induces a connected operator subgraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{P}\) defines an acyclic quotient graph of composite operators and a refinement order on decompositions.
review_flags: The supplied inventory has no locator fixing a standard granularity definition or metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed partition convention and two-component granularity metric are not established as standard and have no supporting source. A source is needed to determine whether this is the intended mathematical notion for the leaf.

children.title: Relaxation Propagation Graph Coupling
children.top_down_role: Graph organization for distributing relaxations and domain information.

children.title: Relaxation Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph organization for assigning local relaxations to nonlinear expression nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph of local relaxations for a factorable nonlinear formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A relaxation graph associated with an auxiliary-variable expression graph replaces each exact relation
\[
z_v=\phi_v(z_{p_1(v)},\ldots,z_{p_{d_v}(v)})
\]
by a tractable set \(R_v\) containing its graph over specified predecessor bounds. The global relaxation is
\[
\mathcal{R}=\{(x,z):(z_{p_1(v)},\ldots,z_{p_{d_v}(v)},z_v)\in R_v\ \text{for every noninput }v\}.
\]
Because every exact operator tuple belongs to its corresponding \(R_v\), the projection of the exact graph feasible set is contained in \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\mathcal{R})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation graph replaces each exact operator relation by a tractable local superset; their intersection yields a valid relaxation of the original model.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_v\) contains the exact graph of \(\phi_v\) over the current bounds.
All shared auxiliary variables are consistently identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{graph}})\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(\mathcal{R}).\)

notation.meaning: local relaxation of the operator at vertex v

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports compositional relaxation graphs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compositional relaxation construction is plausible, but no cited source supports the precise definition or projection-validity formulation.

children.title: Bound-Propagation Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph organization for transmitting domain information through nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Propagation Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward interval tightening on an acyclic operator graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input an acyclic operator graph and initial intervals \(I_v\) for all vertices. In a forward topological sweep, replace each noninput interval by
\[
I_v\leftarrow I_v\cap\Phi_v(I_{p_1(v)},\ldots,I_{p_{d_v}(v)}),
\]
where \(\Phi_v\) is an inclusion-preserving interval extension of \(\phi_v\). In a reverse sweep, apply sound inverse contractors to intersect each predecessor interval with values consistent with \(I_v\). Repeat both sweeps until an interval is empty, no interval changes, or a prescribed tolerance or iteration limit is reached. Return infeasibility if an interval is empty; otherwise return the tightened intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward interval evaluation and backward inverse contraction are alternated on the operator graph until infeasibility, a fixed point, or a stopping limit.
assumptions_latex: Every forward extension and inverse contractor is sound.
Initial intervals contain every feasible graph value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output intervals retain every feasible graph assignment; an empty interval certifies infeasibility within the initial box.

notation.meaning: current interval bound for vertex v
sound interval extension of the vertex operator

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports forward-backward graph bound propagation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind and the stated soundness conditions are plausible, but no source supports the precise forward-backward propagation algorithm or its infeasibility certificate.

children.title: Coupled Graph Information Flow
children.top_down_role: Exchange of local relaxation information and propagated bounds across a shared graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Graph Information Flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating exchange between bound propagation and local relaxation construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize vertex bounds \(I^0\) and local relaxations \(R^0_v\). At iteration \(k\), first apply sound graph propagation to obtain \(I^{k+1}\subseteq I^k\). Reconstruct or strengthen each operator relaxation over the new bounds so that
\[
\operatorname{graph}(\phi_v)\cap(I^{k+1}_{p(v)}\times I^{k+1}_v)\subseteq R^{k+1}_v.
\]
Then use deductions from the global relaxation \(\bigcap_vR^{k+1}_v\) to tighten vertex bounds before the next propagation pass. Stop at infeasibility, a common fixed point, or a prescribed limit. All retained bounds and relaxations must remain valid for the exact graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds strengthen local relaxations, while relaxation deductions tighten bounds; alternating these sound updates preserves all exact feasible graph assignments.
assumptions_latex: Propagation and relaxation-based bound deductions are sound.
Every reconstructed local relaxation contains the bounded exact operator graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled iterations produce nested valid bounds and valid graph relaxations until the stopping rule is met.

notation.meaning: local relaxation at vertex v and iteration k

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the stated coupled graph update scheme.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the particular alternating scheme. In addition, sound reconstruction guarantees validity but does not by itself establish that successive relaxation sets are nested, so the intended conclusion cannot be settled without authoritative support.

children.title: Block-Separability Reformulation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Termwise, blockwise, and extended block-separable representations.

children.title: Separable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Extended representations exposing termwise separable nonlinear structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph decomposition of an additively separable nonlinear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), where \(x_i\in X_i\). The constraint \(f(x)\le b\) has the extended representation
\[
z_i\ge f_i(x_i)\quad(i=1,
\ldots,n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n z_i\le b.
\]
Projection onto \(x\) gives exactly \(\{x\in\prod_iX_i:\sum_i f_i(x_i)\le b\}\): feasible \(z\) implies the original inequality, and an original feasible point admits \(z_i=f_i(x_i)\). When every \(f_i\) is convex, all component epigraph constraints are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additively separable inequality is represented exactly by one epigraph variable per component and a single linear constraint summing those variables.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) on \(\prod_iX_i\).
Each \(f_i\) is finite at the represented feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,z):z_i\ge f_i(x_i),\ \sum_i z_i\le b\}=\{x:\sum_i f_i(x_i)\le b\}.\)

notation.meaning: nonlinear component depending only on coordinate i

children.title: Block-Separable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Extended representations exposing separability across variable or constraint blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended formulation for nonlinear terms separated across variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb{N}\), partition \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(B)})\), and let \(x^{(b)}\in X_b\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_b}\). Suppose that
\[
F(x)=\sum_{b=1}^B F_b(x^{(b)}),
\]
where \(F_b:X_b\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}\). Then \(F(x)\le c\) is represented exactly by
\[
t_b\ge F_b(x^{(b)})\quad(b=1,\ldots,B),\qquad \sum_{b=1}^B t_b\le c.
\]
For any \(q\in\mathbb{N}\), additional linear cross-block constraints with \(A_b\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n_b}\) and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^q\), such as \(\sum_{b=1}^B A_bx^{(b)}=d\), may be retained explicitly without changing the blockwise nonlinear representation. If every \(X_b\) is convex and every \(F_b\) is convex on \(X_b\), the extended formulation is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blockwise nonlinear epigraphs plus a linear aggregation constraint exactly represent an additively block-separable inequality, while explicit linear cross-block constraints can be retained.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x^{(b)}\in X_b\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_b}\), and \(F_b:X_b\to\mathbb{R}\) for every \(b\).
\(F(x)=\sum_{b=1}^B F_b(x^{(b)})\) and \(c\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,t):x^{(b)}\in X_b,\ t_b\ge F_b(x^{(b)})\ (b=1,\ldots,B),\ \sum_{b=1}^B t_b\le c\}=\{x\in\prod_{b=1}^B X_b:F(x)\le c\}.\)

notation.meaning: nonlinear function local to block b

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling Recovery
children.top_down_role: Representations retaining residual coupling among otherwise separable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-variable representation for recovering couplings removed by block separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb N\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and, for each \(b\in\{1,\ldots,B\}\), let \(I_b\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(f_b:\mathbb R^{I_b}\to\mathbb R\). Define
\[
F=\{x\in X:f_b(x_{I_b})\le 0\text{ for every }b=1,\ldots,B\}.
\]
Introduce \(x^b\in\mathbb R^{I_b}\) for each block. Then
\[
F=\operatorname{proj}_x\left\{(x,x^1,\ldots,x^B):x\in X,\ f_b(x^b)\le0\text{ for every }b,\ x^b_j=x_j\text{ for every }b\text{ and }j\in I_b\right\}.
\]
The copy-consistency equations exactly recover the dependence between each block-local copy and the corresponding master coordinates; omitting one generally produces a relaxation of this extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate the variables used by each block and equate every local copy to its corresponding master coordinate. Projection onto the master variables then reproduces the original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the original master-variable domain.
Each constraint function \(f_b\) is assigned an index set containing every variable on which it depends.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) equals the projection of the block-local formulation containing all required copy-consistency equations.

notation.meaning: block-local copy of the variables indexed by I_b

children.title: Structural Graph Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Graph structures supporting decomposition, convexification, branching, and symmetry handling.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Description of the Perfectly Matchable Subgraph Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard notation x(S)=\sum_{i\in S}x_i, N(S) for the neighborhood of S, and c(S) for the number of connected components of G[S].
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an arbitrary graph \(G=(V,E)\), the perfectly matchable subgraph polytope is
\[
P_{\mathrm{PMS}}(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{V}:0\le x_i\le1\ \forall i\in V,\quad x(S)-x(N(S))\le |S|-c(S)\ \forall S\subseteq V\text{ such that every component of }G[S]\text{ is either a singleton or a nonbipartite graph of odd order}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every graph G, its perfectly matchable subgraph polytope is exactly the set of vectors satisfying the unit-box bounds and, for every eligible vertex subset S, the inequality x(S) minus x(N(S)) at most |S| minus the number of components of G[S]. A subset is eligible when each component induced by S is either a singleton or a nonbipartite graph with an odd number of vertices.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is an arbitrary graph}
x(S)=\sum_{i\in S}x_i
S\subseteq V
\text{Every component of }G[S]\text{ is a singleton or is nonbipartite of odd order}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\mathrm{PMS}}(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{V}:0\le x_i\le1\ \forall i\in V,\ x(S)-x(N(S))\le |S|-c(S)\ \text{for every eligible }S\subseteq V\right\}

children.title: Sparsity Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations of variable, constraint, or matrix sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable sparsity graph of a differentiable mixed-integer nonlinear formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable functions \(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_m\) on an open set containing the continuous relaxation, the sparsity graph is the undirected graph \(G_s=(V,E_s)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Distinct vertices \(i,j\) satisfy \(\{i,j\}\in E_s\) when some function has structurally coupled derivatives, meaning \(\partial^2 f_k/\partial x_i\partial x_j\) is not identically zero. For merely factorized expressions, the analogous structural convention joins variables occurring together in one declared nonlinear factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparsity graph joins variables that have a structurally nonzero mixed derivative or occur together in a declared nonlinear factor.
assumptions_latex: The structural pattern is determined from the formulation, not from derivative values at one point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_s\) records pairwise nonlinear variable coupling in the formulation.

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.1 The sparsity graph p. 12

children.title: Interaction Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations of nonlinear or quadratic variable coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Interaction Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite incidence graph retaining nonlinear-factor identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a factorized formulation with variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) and declared nonlinear factors \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_q\), its interaction graph is the bipartite graph \(G_I=(V\mathbin{\dot\cup}F,E_I)\), where \(V=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), \(F=\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_q\}\), and
\[
(x_i,\phi_k)\in E_I\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \phi_k\text{ depends structurally on }x_i.
\]
Unlike a variable-only sparsity graph, \(G_I\) distinguishes different factors having the same variable support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interaction graph is the bipartite incidence graph connecting each nonlinear factor to every variable on which that factor structurally depends.
assumptions_latex: A particular factorization of the formulation is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_I\) preserves factor incidence and therefore determines each declared factor support.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: factor-variable incidence graphs are a standard representation of structured nonlinear expressions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factor-variable incidence definition is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source establishes that this is the intended meaning of Interaction Graphs in the local taxonomy.

children.title: Symmetry Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations used to expose structural equivalence under permutations.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Colored formulation graph whose automorphisms encode model symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A symmetry graph for a mixed-integer nonlinear formulation is a vertex- and edge-colored graph \(G_{\mathrm{sym}}\) constructed from variables, constraints, coefficients, and nonlinear operators so that every color-preserving automorphism induces permutations \((\pi_V,\pi_C)\) satisfying
\[
f_{\pi_C(k)}(\pi_V x)=f_k(x),\qquad \pi_V(X)=X,
\]
and preserving the objective, constraint senses, bounds, and integrality declarations. Such an automorphism certifies a formulation symmetry; the graph is symmetry-complete only if every formulation symmetry is represented by an automorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry graph encodes variables, constraints, coefficients, and operators so that its color-preserving automorphisms induce permutations preserving the entire optimization formulation.
assumptions_latex: Graph colors distinguish all formulation attributes that must remain invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every color-preserving automorphism of \(G_{\mathrm{sym}}\) induces a valid formulation symmetry.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: colored graph automorphisms are the standard certificate used in formulation-symmetry detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The role and content kind fit, but the soundness and symmetry-completeness claims depend on the precise colored-graph construction, for which no source or construction details are supplied.

children.title: Cross-Graph Coordination
children.top_down_role: Combined use of sparsity, interaction, and symmetry information in solver organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Graph Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency principle for simultaneous sparsity, interaction, and symmetry graph decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_s\), \(G_I\), and \(G_{\mathrm{sym}}\) describe one formulation. A coordinated partition \(\mathcal P\) must assign every factor vertex of \(G_I\) together with all variables in its neighborhood, or explicitly represent each crossing incidence by a linking variable and consistency equation. Its variable blocks must cover every edge of \(G_s\). If symmetry reduction is also imposed, \(\mathcal P\) and all linking constraints must be invariant under the selected subgroup of \(\operatorname{Aut}(G_{\mathrm{sym}})\). Under these requirements, graph-based decomposition preserves every declared nonlinear interaction and selected symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common partition must cover sparsity edges, preserve factor incidences through blocks or links, and remain invariant under any symmetries retained by the reformulation.
assumptions_latex: All three graphs encode the same formulation and variable indexing.
Every crossing interaction receives an explicit exact linkage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinated reformulation preserves the encoded nonlinear interactions and the selected symmetry subgroup.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact graph-based decompositions must preserve every crossing incidence by explicit linkage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordination principle is plausible, but no direct source supports the composite sufficiency claim. It also alternates between a partition and overlapping factor-containing blocks without defining which structure is intended.

children.title: Perspective Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Convexification of indicator-controlled convex nonlinear structure.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Perspective reformulation, applications, and algorithmic techniques

children.title: Perspective Reformulation Families
children.top_down_role: Separable, quadratic, and conic representations of perspective-strengthened sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Reformulation Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex perspective representation of an on-off epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be closed, proper, and convex with \(\phi(0)=0\). Define its closed perspective by
\[
\widetilde\phi(x,z)=
\begin{cases}
z\phi(x/z),&z>0,\\
\phi^\infty(x),&z=0,\\
+\infty,&z<0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\phi^\infty\) is the recession function. The closed convex hull of the union of the inactive epigraph \(\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\) and active epigraph \(\{(x,1,t):t\ge\phi(x)\}\) is \(\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge\widetilde\phi(x,z)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective gives the closed convex hull of a convex epigraph switched between an inactive origin and an active state.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is closed, proper, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S_0\cup S_1)=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge\widetilde\phi(x,z)\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the closed-perspective epigraph is the standard convex-hull representation for an on-off convex epigraph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-perspective hull representation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but it is a nontrivial convex-hull theorem with no authoritative locator.

children.title: Perspective Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Static, dynamic, and lifted linear outer approximations of perspective sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient linearizations whose intersection represents a closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be closed and convex. For every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\phi\) and \(g\in\partial\phi(\bar x)\), the perspective epigraph satisfies the linear inequality
\[
t\ge g^{\mathsf T}x+\bigl(\phi(\bar x)-g^{\mathsf T}\bar x\bigr)z.
\]
For \(z>0\), this is the supporting inequality for \(t\ge z\phi(x/z)\). The intersection of all such inequalities, together with \(z\ge0\) and the appropriate closed-domain and recession constraints at \(z=0\), equals the closed perspective epigraph. Finite subsets give static or dynamically separated outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradients of the base convex function generate linear perspective cuts; all such cuts plus domain and recession constraints recover the closed perspective epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is closed and convex.
\(g\in\partial\phi(\bar x)\) at a point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge g^{\mathsf T}x+(\phi(\bar x)-g^{\mathsf T}\bar x)z\) is valid for the perspective epigraph.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential at the linearization point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: perspective cuts follow directly from supporting hyperplanes of a convex function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed subgradient inequality is valid, but the stronger assertion that all such inequalities plus unspecified domain and recession constraints exactly recover the closed perspective epigraph requires a precise source and formulation.

children.title: Perspective Applicability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundaries involving activation linkage, nonconvex terms, and shared-variable coupling.

children.title: Activation-Linkage Validity
children.top_down_role: Perspective validity under discrete activation and variable-linkage structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Linkage Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary linkage condition for an on-off perspective term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an on-off term with indicator \(z\in\{0,1\}\), argument \(x\), and active cost \(\phi(x)\). A perspective reformulation is valid for the intended disjunction only when the original feasible set enforces
\[
z=0\ \Longrightarrow\ x=0
\]
for every component of \(x\) entering the perspective term, while \(z=1\) restores the intended active domain. Equivalently, the disjunctive domain must be \(\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in D\}\), possibly expressed by valid bounds such as \(z\ell\le x\le zu\). Without this linkage, the perspective formulation removes feasible inactive points with nonzero \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective strengthening is valid only when inactivity forces every argument of the switched term to its designated inactive value, normally zero.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\{0,1\}\) activates the term \(\phi(x)\).
Zero is the designated inactive value of the term argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity requires \(z=0\Rightarrow x=0\) and recovery of the intended active domain when \(z=1\).

notation.meaning: active domain of the term argument
valid componentwise bounds in the active state

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the perspective hull represents a disjunction whose inactive branch fixes the term argument at zero

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly describes the standard zero-inactive on-off disjunction, but the universal necessity claim needs an authoritative applicability source distinguishing this construction from translated or auxiliary-variable perspectives.

children.title: Nonconvex-Term Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of perspective strengthening when the activated nonlinear term is nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Term Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convex perspective strengthening for a nonconvex base term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Convexity of the base term is essential to the standard perspective strengthening. For the nonconvex function \(\phi(x)=-x^2\) on \([-1,1]\), its positive perspective is
\[
z\phi(x/z)=-x^2/z\qquad(z>0),
\]
which is concave rather than convex on its natural domain. Consequently, the inequality \(t\ge -x^2/z\) does not define a convex relaxation and is not the convex hull of the associated on-off epigraph. A valid convexification must instead use a convex envelope or a disjunctive relaxation of the nonconvex term before applying perspective machinery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual perspective is convex only for convex base terms; a concave quadratic produces a nonconvex epigraph and does not yield the on-off convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The standard epigraph perspective construction is applied without first convexifying the base term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\phi(x)=-x^2\), the constraint \(t\ge z\phi(x/z)\) is nonconvex and is not a perspective convex-hull formulation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convexity of the perspective is equivalent to convexity of the underlying proper function on positive scales

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The concave-quadratic example correctly demonstrates that the ordinary convex perspective machinery does not apply, but the boundary statement and prescribed remedy have no cited source.

children.title: Shared-Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Perspective behavior when multiple activated terms share continuous variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for separately perspectivizing terms sharing one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose terms \(\phi_i(x)\), \(i=1,\ldots,p\), share the same physical variable \(x\) but have distinct indicators \(z_i\). Replacing every term by its own perspective and imposing \(z_i=0\Rightarrow x=0\) is exact only if the original model itself requires
\[
\bigl(\exists i:z_i=0\bigr)\Longrightarrow x=0.
\]
If an inactive term is merely omitted while another active term may use nonzero \(x\), these individual linkages cut off feasible points. A valid extended formulation may instead use term-specific copies \(x^i\), impose the appropriate activation linkage on each copy, and represent the intended sharing through explicit coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate perspectives of terms sharing a variable may overconstrain the model; term-specific copies and exact coupling are needed unless every inactive indicator truly forces the shared variable to zero.
assumptions_latex: Multiple switched terms share one physical variable.
Their indicators may take different values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent zero-linkages on the shared variable are valid only when every inactive indicator truly implies \(x=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: applying an inactive-state implication to a shared physical variable can strengthen the underlying disjunction incorrectly

children.title: Perspective Strength-Loss Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where perspective formulations remain valid but lose hull strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Strength-Loss Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit relaxation gap caused by omitting the perspective quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the on-off quadratic epigraph
\[
S=\{(x,z,t):z\in\{0,1\},\ -z\le x\le z,\ t\ge x^2\}.
\]
Its perspective relaxation contains \(0\le z\le1\), \(-z\le x\le z\), and \(t\ge x^2/z\) for \(z>0\). The unstrengthened relaxation retaining only \(t\ge x^2\) is strictly weaker: at \((x,z)=(1/2,1/2)\), it permits \(t=1/4\), whereas the perspective inequality requires \(t\ge1/2\). Thus strength is lost whenever fractional activation is allowed but the nonlinear term is not scaled by its activation variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a switched quadratic, retaining the original quadratic after relaxing the indicator admits fractional points excluded by the perspective inequality, creating a strict relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: The binary activation variable is relaxed to \(0\le z\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \((x,z)=(1/2,1/2)\), the naive bound is \(t\ge1/4\), while the perspective bound is \(t\ge1/2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed point directly demonstrates the classical fractional-indicator gap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical counterexample and its arithmetic are correct, and counterexample is the appropriate content kind, but no inspectable citation supports its placement as perspective strength-loss knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Bilinear Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick convex-hull representation over a rectangular domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\), \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and \(w=xy\), with finite bounds. The convex hull of the bilinear graph over this rectangle is the polytope defined by the bounds and
\[
\begin{aligned}
w&\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y,\\
w&\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,\\
w&\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y,\\
w&\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.
\end{aligned}
\]
These four McCormick inequalities are simultaneously necessary and sufficient for membership in \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy):x\in[\ell_x,u_x],\ y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four McCormick inequalities exactly describe the convex hull of a continuous bilinear graph over a finite rectangle.
assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<\ell_x\le u_x<+\infty\) and \(-\infty<\ell_y\le u_y<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four displayed inequalities and variable bounds describe \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy)\}\) over the rectangle.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product xy

knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Quadratic Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex and concave envelopes of a quadratic on a compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=ax^2+bx+c\) on \([\ell,u]\), where \(\ell<u\), and let \(s(x)=q(\ell)+(q(u)-q(\ell))(x-\ell)/(u-\ell)\) be its endpoint secant. The convex envelope and concave envelope of \(q\) over this interval are
\[\operatorname{vex}_{[\ell,u]}q=\begin{cases}q,&a\ge 0,\\s,&a<0,\end{cases}\qquad \operatorname{cav}_{[\ell,u]}q=\begin{cases}s,&a>0,\\q,&a\le 0.\end{cases}\]
Thus the nonconvex side is replaced exactly by the affine endpoint secant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded interval, a quadratic supplies one envelope itself; its opposite envelope is the line joining the endpoint values.
assumptions_latex: \(q(x)=ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a,b,c\in\mathbb R\).
\(-\infty<\ell<u<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed functions are the exact convex and concave envelopes of \(q\) on \([\ell,u]\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of q on D
concave envelope of q on D

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Domain Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of box-domain product envelopes on finite coordinate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=[\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\) with finite, nondegenerate bounds, the convex hull of the graph \(w=xy\) is polyhedral and is determined by the four corner points \((x,y,xy)\) of \(D\). Under the affine substitutions \(x=\ell_x+(u_x-\ell_x)\xi\) and \(y=\ell_y+(u_y-\ell_y)\eta\), it is the affine image of the corresponding hull on \([0,1]^2\). Consequently, shrinking either coordinate interval cannot weaken the product envelope over the retained domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bilinear graph over a rectangle has a corner-generated polyhedral hull; affine scaling normalizes it, and tighter bounds strengthen its envelope.
assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<\ell_x<u_x<\infty\).
\(-\infty<\ell_y<u_y<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hull geometry is corner-generated, affinely invariant under box normalization, and monotone under bound tightening.

notation.meaning: coordinates normalized to the unit square

knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Continuous Product Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear hull for one bounded continuous variable multiplied by one binary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in[\ell,u]\), \(y\in\{0,1\}\), and \(z=xy\), where \(\ell\le u\) are finite. Then
\[\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,z):x\in[\ell,u],\ y\in\{0,1\},\ z=xy\}\]
is exactly the set satisfying \(0\le y\le1\), \(\ell\le x\le u\), and
\[\ell y\le z\le uy,\qquad x-u(1-y)\le z\le x-\ell(1-y).\]
For binary \(y\), these inequalities force \(z=0\) when \(y=0\) and \(z=x\) when \(y=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities give the exact convex hull of a bounded continuous variable multiplied by a binary variable.
assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<\ell\le u<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linear system is the exact convex-hull representation of \(z=xy\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex formulation of the exact graph hull for a single multilinear monomial on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\) on the box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), and let \(V\) be the \(2^n\) vertices of \(B\). The exact convex hull of the graph is
\[\operatorname{conv}\{(x,f(x)):x\in B\}=\left\{(x,w):x=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv,\ w=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vf(v),\ \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1,\ \lambda_v\ge0\right\}.\]
Dropping or aggregating vertex variables yields polyhedral outer relaxations but need not preserve this exact hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graph hull of one multilinear monomial over a box is the convex hull of its values at all box vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(-\infty<\ell_i<u_i<\infty\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(2^n\)-vertex extended formulation represents the exact convex hull of the multilinear graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive McCormick Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-based construction of a polyhedral relaxation for a bounded multilinear monomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a bounded box \(B\) and a binary factorization tree for \(w=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\). Associate each leaf with its factor and each internal node with a variable \(t=rs\). Starting at the leaves, compute valid bounds for \(r\) and \(s\), impose the four McCormick inequalities for \(t=rs\), and propagate valid bounds for \(t\) toward the root. Output the resulting extended polyhedron, identifying the root variable with \(w\). Stop after every internal node has been processed; the projection onto \((x,w)\) contains the original multilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively factor a multilinear term, introduce one variable per intermediate product, and impose a McCormick envelope at every tree node.
assumptions_latex: Every leaf variable has finite lower and upper bounds.
A binary factorization tree for \(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected extended polyhedron is a valid outer relaxation of \(w=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\) over \(B\).

notation.meaning: product represented at an internal tree node

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Grouping Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of recursive product relaxations on the chosen factorization tree and propagated bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each binary factorization tree \(T\) of \(w=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\), let \(R_T\) be the projection of its recursive McCormick formulation onto \((x,w)\). Every \(R_T\) contains the multilinear graph, but distinct trees may produce distinct projected polyhedra because their intermediate variables represent different subproducts and receive different propagated bounds. Hence associativity of exact multiplication does not imply equality of the relaxations. A grouping is stronger than another on the same box precisely when \(R_{T_1}\subseteq R_{T_2}\); such dominance is instance- and bound-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent algebraic groupings can yield different recursive McCormick relaxations because intermediate products and their bounds differ.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge3\) and every factor has finite bounds.
Each tree uses valid bounds and McCormick inequalities at every internal node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recursive McCormick strength may depend on grouping, with dominance characterized by projected-set inclusion.

notation.meaning: projected recursive relaxation generated by T

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive envelope obtained by partitioning a bounded product domain into finitely many cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), where the compact box \(D\) is covered by finitely many boxes \(D_1,\ldots,D_K\). For each \(k\), define \(G_k=\{(x,w):x\in D_k,\ w=f(x)\}\) and choose a convex local outer relaxation \(H_k\supseteq G_k\). The partitioned relaxation is
\[R_{\mathcal P}=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K H_k\right).\]
It admits a disjunctive extended formulation using cell weights and scaled copies of the local formulations. It contains the graph over \(D\), and if \(H_k=\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\) for every \(k\), then
\[R_{\mathcal P}=\operatorname{conv}\{(x,f(x)):x\in D\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the domain, choose a valid convex local envelope on each cell, and take the convex hull of their union. The result is exact when every local set is the exact restricted graph hull.
assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is defined on a compact box \(D\).
\(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^K D_k\), where each \(D_k\) is a box.
Each \(H_k\) is convex and satisfies \(G_k\subseteq H_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathcal P}\) is a valid outer relaxation and equals the full graph hull when \(H_k=\operatorname{conv}(G_k)\) for all \(k\).

notation.meaning: convex local outer relaxation on cell k

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Strengthened Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthening an extended envelope by valid inequalities expressed in the original product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\) be a product graph and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1+m}\) be an extended relaxation with \(G\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_{x,w}(Q)\). If \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\) is any convex set containing \(G\), define
\[Q^+=Q\cap\{(x,w,u):(x,w)\in C\}.\]
Then \(G\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_{x,w}(Q^+)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_{x,w}(Q)\). The inclusion is strict exactly when some projected point of \(Q\) violates \(C\); thus projected valid inequalities strengthen the envelope without excluding graph points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting an extended envelope with valid inequalities in original variables yields a no-weaker projected relaxation and may make it strictly tighter.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is an extended outer relaxation of \(G\).
\(C\) is convex and contains \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strengthened projection remains valid and is contained in the original projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition–Projection Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined relaxation applying projected valid inequalities within a domain-partition disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a partition \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^K D_k\), let \(Q_k\) be an extended local envelope and let \(C_k\) contain the graph restricted to \(D_k\). Define \(Q_k^+=Q_k\cap\{(x,w,u_k):(x,w)\in C_k\}\) and
\[R_{\mathcal P,C}=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K\operatorname{proj}_{x,w}(Q_k^+)\right).\]
This hybrid contains the full graph and is contained in the unstrengthened partitioned relaxation formed from the \(Q_k\). It is also contained in the convex hull obtained by applying the same cellwise projected restrictions before discarding the partition labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid strengthens every partition cell in projected space before taking the disjunctive hull of the cell relaxations.
assumptions_latex: The cells finitely cover \(D\).
Each \(Q_k\) contains its restricted graph.
Each \(C_k\) is valid on cell \(D_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathcal P,C}\) is a valid hybrid relaxation no weaker than its unstrengthened partitioned counterpart.

knowledge_statements.title: RLT Constraint-Product Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level reformulation–linearization constraints generated from linear constraints and bound factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given linear inequalities \(g_r(x)=a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r\ge0\) and bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\), select nonnegative factors \(x_j-\ell_j\) and \(u_j-x_j\). Form the valid quadratic inequalities
\[g_r(x)(x_j-\ell_j)\ge0,\qquad g_r(x)(u_j-x_j)\ge0.\]
Expand each product, replace every quadratic term \(x_ix_j\) by a lifted variable \(X_{ij}\), and retain the original constraints and bound-derived product relations. The output is a linear lifted relaxation containing every point with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) that satisfies the original system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RLT multiplies valid inequalities by nonnegative bound factors and linearizes the resulting quadratic terms in a lifted matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(g_r(x)\ge0\) is valid for the original feasible set.
Finite bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated lifted linear system is valid for all feasible rank-one pairs \((x,X)\) with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-MILP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral lifting of bounded quadratic terms into a mixed-integer linear outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a bounded mixed-integer quadratic minimization model. For every quadratic product \(x_ix_j\) occurring in its constraints or objective, introduce a variable \(X_{ij}\), replace each occurrence of \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\), and impose a polyhedral outer envelope \(P_{ij}\) for \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\) over the valid bounds of \(x_i\) and \(x_j\). Retaining the original integrality restrictions gives the MILP relaxation
\[\mathcal R=\{(x,X):(x_i,x_j,X_{ij})\in P_{ij}\ \text{for every lifted pair, and all lifted linear constraints hold}\}.\]
Every feasible solution of the quadratic model lifts to a point of \(\mathcal R\) with the same objective value. Therefore minimizing the lifted linear objective over \(\mathcal R\) gives a valid lower bound on the original minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift every quadratic product in a bounded mixed-integer minimization model and impose a polyhedral product envelope. The resulting MILP is an outer relaxation whose optimum is a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The original model is a minimization problem.
Every quadratic product in the constraints or objective is lifted.
All variables appearing in lifted products have finite valid bounds.
Each \(P_{ij}\) contains the graph of \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\) over those bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted MILP contains a value-preserving lift of every original feasible solution, so its minimum is a valid lower bound on the original minimum.

notation.meaning: polyhedral outer envelope for one product

knowledge_statements.title: Product Disaggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact additive decomposition of a product followed by componentwise envelope relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x=\sum_{k=1}^K x_k\), with valid bounds \(\ell_k\le x_k\le u_k\), and let \(w=xy\). Introduce component products \(w_k=x_ky\) and impose
\[x=\sum_{k=1}^Kx_k,\qquad w=\sum_{k=1}^Kw_k.\]
These equations together with \(w_k=x_ky\) are exactly equivalent to \(w=xy\). Replacing each component equality by a valid envelope over \([\ell_k,u_k]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\) gives a lifted outer relaxation. If disaggregation yields tighter component bounds, its projection can be strictly smaller than the envelope constructed only from aggregate bounds on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one factor into bounded components, distribute multiplication across them, and relax the smaller component products separately.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{k=1}^Kx_k\) holds exactly.
Finite valid bounds exist for every \(x_k\) and for \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise envelopes plus \(w=\sum_k w_k\) form a valid lifted relaxation of \(w=xy\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(H_J=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{J}}P_{J,\alpha}\bigr)\). If \(J\subseteq J'\subseteq I\), then \(H_{J'}\subseteq H_J\), and \(H_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^{I}\times\mathbb R^{n-|I|})\). The standard disjunctive extended formulation of \(H_J\) introduces one scaled copy of the continuous variables and one multiplier for each nonempty branch, so its raw size is \(O(2^{|J|}(n+m))\) when \(P\) has \(m\) inequalities. Thus strength increases with the split set, potentially at exponential lift cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting more binary variables yields nested, stronger projected relaxations and reaches the integer hull, but explicit branch lifts can grow exponentially.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift Size–Strength Tradeoffs

children.title: Boolean Quadric Polytope Interface
children.top_down_role: Lifted binary-product structure expressed through the Boolean quadric polytope.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linear optimization of a binary quadratic objective supported on \(E\) is equivalent to linear optimization over \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\).

notation.meaning: Boolean quadric polytope of the graph.
Lifted coordinate representing the binary product \(x_ix_j\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-indexed Boolean quadric polytope in node-and-edge coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Boolean quadric polytope associated with \(G\) is
\[\operatorname{BQP}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(x,w)\in\{0,1\}^{V}\times\{0,1\}^{E}:w_{ij}=x_ix_j\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}.\]
Consequently, for coefficients \(c_i\) and \(q_{ij}\),
\[\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^{V}}\left(\sum_{i\in V}c_ix_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}q_{ij}x_ix_j\right)=\min_{(x,w)\in\operatorname{BQP}(G)}\left(\sum_{i\in V}c_ix_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}q_{ij}w_{ij}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean quadric polytope is the convex hull of binary node variables together with edge variables equal to their pairwise products.
knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Quadric Polytope Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-indexed Boolean quadric polytope representation is mathematically standard and fits the interface leaf, but the record has no citation. A source with a definition, theorem, section, or page locator is required.

children.title: Correlation Polytope Interface
children.top_down_role: Lifted binary-product structure expressed through the correlation polytope.

assumptions_latex: \(n\ge 1\) and \(S^n\) denotes the real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A binary quadratic function becomes a linear functional of \(X\) over \(\operatorname{COR}(n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-coordinate definition of the correlation polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The correlation polytope of order \(n\) is
\[\operatorname{COR}(n)=\operatorname{conv}\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in\{0,1\}^{n}\}\subseteq S^n.\]
Every vertex \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(X_{ii}=x_i\) and \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\). Therefore, for every \(Q\in S^n\),
\[\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\min_{X\in\operatorname{COR}(n)}\langle Q,X\rangle,\]
where \(\langle Q,X\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(QX)\). Linear side constraints in the products become linear constraints on entries of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correlation polytope is the convex hull of binary rank-one matrices, converting binary quadratic objectives into linear matrix objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlation Polytope Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix-coordinate definition and objective linearization are standard and internally consistent, but no source is cited. The claimed interface, including the treatment of product side constraints, requires a specific authoritative locator.

children.title: Canonical Polyhedral Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Mappings between Boolean quadric and correlation polytope representations.

assumptions_latex: \(K_n\) is the complete graph on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete-graph Boolean quadric polytope and the correlation polytope are linearly isomorphic.

notation.meaning: Boolean quadric polytope in node-and-edge coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate identification between complete Boolean-product and correlation representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{E(K_n)}\to S^n\) by \(\Phi(x,w)_{ii}=x_i\) and \(\Phi(x,w)_{ij}=\Phi(x,w)_{ji}=w_{ij}\) for \(i<j\). Then
\[\Phi\bigl(\operatorname{BQP}(K_n)\bigr)=\operatorname{COR}(n).\]
The inverse map reads the diagonal of \(X\) as \(x\) and its strict upper triangle as \(w\). Hence \(\Phi\) is a linear bijection preserving vertices, faces, valid inequalities, and linear optimization values after the corresponding coefficient transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Placing Boolean node coordinates on a matrix diagonal and product coordinates off diagonal gives a linear bijection with the correlation polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Polyhedral Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate map is a linear bijection between the complete-graph Boolean quadric and correlation polytopes and fits the correspondence leaf. The record nevertheless lacks the required inspectable polyhedral source.

children.title: Cut-Polytope Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Affine and combinatorial connections between binary quadratic and cut representations.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph and \(\nabla G\) is obtained by adjoining a new node \(0\) adjacent to every node of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\) is affinely isomorphic to the cut polytope of the suspension graph \(\nabla G\).

notation.meaning: Suspension graph formed by adding universal node \(0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suspension-graph affine correspondence for graph-indexed Boolean products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Boolean vertex \((x,w)\) of \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\), define cut coordinates on \(\nabla G\) by
\[\delta_{0i}=x_i\quad(i\in V),\qquad \delta_{ij}=x_i+x_j-2w_{ij}\quad(\{i,j\}\in E).\]
These are the incidence coordinates of the cut whose side not containing \(0\) is \(\{i:x_i=1\}\). Conversely,
\[x_i=\delta_{0i},\qquad w_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{0i}+\delta_{0j}-\delta_{ij}}{2}.\]
The mutually inverse affine maps extend by convexity to an affine isomorphism between \(\operatorname{BQP}(G)\) and \(\operatorname{CUT}(\nabla G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean product point maps affinely to a cut of the suspension graph, with an explicit inverse recovering every product coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Polytope Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The suspension-graph formulas give the standard affine Boolean-quadric/cut-polytope correspondence and are mutually consistent, but the record supplies no authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Quadratic Binary Lift-Project Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive and hierarchy-based strengthening of lifted binary quadratic formulations.

children.title: Lift-Project Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive strengthening applied to lifted binary quadratic formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\subseteq[0,1]^n\) and coordinate \(x_j\) is required to be binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projecting the disjunctive hull gives a valid relaxation enforcing the split \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\).

notation.meaning: Two-term split hull for binary coordinate \(j\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-coordinate Balas disjunctive lift for a mixed-binary relaxation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The split hull is
\[D_j(P)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x_j=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x_j=1\})\bigr).\]
It is the projection onto \(x=x^0+x^1\) of the lifted system
\[Ax^k\le b\lambda_k\ (k=0,1),\quad x_j^0=0,\quad x_j^1=\lambda_1,\quad \lambda_0+\lambda_1=1,\quad \lambda_0,\lambda_1\ge0.\]
Thus every projected inequality valid for this lift is valid for all points of \(P\) satisfying the binary disjunction, and \(D_j(P)\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary split is convexified by two scaled branch copies; projecting their lifted formulation yields valid lift-and-project inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift-Project Disjunctions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

children.title: Quadratic Binary Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Successive lifted relaxation levels for binary quadratic models.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is a polytope and \(P_I=P\cap\{0,1\}^n\).
\(H^0(P)=P\), and each round applies every prescribed binary split before projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hierarchy is nested and, for standard finite binary lift-and-project operators, reaches \(\operatorname{conv}(P_I)\) after at most \(n\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-convergence property shared by standard full binary lift-and-project hierarchies.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 6. Lift-and-Project Cuts for Mixed 0-1 Programs p. 79

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a standard full binary lift-and-project hierarchy, the level sets satisfy
\[P=H^0(P)\supseteq H^1(P)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H^n(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P_I).\]
At level \(r\), the lifted constraints encode products or disjunctions involving at most \(r\) binary coordinates, and projection returns a relaxation in the original \(x\)-space. Every point of \(P_I\) has a consistent lift at every level, so \(\operatorname{conv}(P_I)\subseteq H^r(P)\); applying all \(n\) binary disjunctions leaves exactly the binary convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard binary lift-and-project hierarchies form nested relaxations, preserve all integer points, and attain the binary convex hull within finitely many levels.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Binary Hierarchies

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 6. Lift-and-Project Cuts for Mixed 0-1 Programs p. 79

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The notation \(H^r\) is not tied to a specific lift-and-project operator, while finite convergence within \(n\) rounds and the meaning of a level depend on the chosen hierarchy. The cited chapter is too broad to determine which operator supports the exact displayed chain. A precise operator definition and supporting theorem locator are required.

children.title: Projection Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-strength behavior after eliminating lifted variables.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is a polytope, and \(R\) is a lifted relaxation whose projection is \(\pi_x(R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lift strength must be assessed after projection: additional valid lifted constraints strengthen the original-space relaxation only when their projection removes an original-space point.

notation.meaning: Projection onto the original variable space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of lift-and-project relaxations in the original variable space.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be valid lifts of \(P_I=P\cap\{0,1\}^n\). If \(R_2\subseteq R_1\) in a common lifted space, then \(\pi_x(R_2)\subseteq\pi_x(R_1)\). The inclusion is strict exactly when there exists \(x\in\pi_x(R_1)\) having no extension in \(R_2\). Conversely, extra lifted variables or inequalities that do not change \(\pi_x(R)\) provide no stronger bound for objectives depending only on \(x\). Therefore formulations of different lifted dimensions are ordered by their projected feasible sets, not by dimension alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger or tighter lift is genuinely stronger only when its projection excludes additional original-space points and can improve an original-space objective bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Strength Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

children.title: Structured Semidefinite Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Basic and problem-structured semidefinite lifting families.

children.title: Shor Matrix Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Baseline semidefinite lifting for quadratic optimization structure.

assumptions_latex: \(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\in S^n\), \(q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping the rank-one equality yields the Shor semidefinite relaxation and a valid lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard first-order Shor relaxation for a quadratically constrained quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the quadratic program
\[\min_x\ x^{\mathsf T}Q_0x+2q_0^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2q_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\]
introduce \(X\) for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) and impose
\[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
The Shor relaxation replaces each quadratic expression by \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+2q_i^{\mathsf T}x\) and omits \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\). Since every feasible \(x\) lifts to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), the semidefinite optimum is a lower bound on the original minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shor relaxation linearizes quadratic terms in a matrix and replaces the exact rank-one condition by positive semidefiniteness, giving a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Shor Matrix Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

children.title: Combinatorial Matrix Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Matrix relaxations strengthened by problem-specific combinatorial structure.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and \(X\in S^n\) represents \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
All additional linear combinatorial constraints are valid for the binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting the basic semidefinite lift with valid combinatorial matrix constraints gives a relaxation at least as strong as the unstrengthened Shor relaxation.

notation.meaning: Feasible set defined by the valid combinatorial constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary combinatorial strengthening of a first-order semidefinite matrix lift.

source_refs.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization, p. 483

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every binary rank-one lift satisfies
\[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad X_{ii}=x_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\]
and, for all \(1\le i<j\le n\),
\[0\le X_{ij}\le x_i,\qquad 0\le X_{ij}\le x_j,\qquad X_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1.\]
Additional valid inequalities derived from the underlying combinatorial structure may be imposed linearly on \((x,X)\). If \(R_{\mathrm{Shor}}\) is the basic matrix relaxation and \(C\) is the feasible set defined by any such valid system, then \(R_{\mathrm{comb}}=R_{\mathrm{Shor}}\cap C\subseteq R_{\mathrm{Shor}}\), while every binary feasible rank-one lift remains in \(R_{\mathrm{comb}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary diagonal identities, product inequalities, and problem-specific valid inequalities can be added to a Shor matrix relaxation without excluding feasible binary solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Matrix Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization, p. 483

children.title: Structure-Aware Matrix Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Additional matrix restrictions derived from discrete model structure.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible set and every \(x\in F\) has the exact lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
\(\mathcal C\) is a family of linear or conic constraints satisfied by every exact lifted point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding \(\mathcal C\) preserves validity and can only strengthen the projected matrix relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and monotonicity of problem-specific matrix strengthening.

source_refs.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be a matrix relaxation containing \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) for every \(x\in F\), and suppose \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\in\mathcal C\) for every \(x\in F\). Define \(R^+=R\cap\mathcal C\). Then
\[F\subseteq\pi_x(R^+)\subseteq\pi_x(R).\]
Thus sparsity constraints, symmetry equations, assignment identities, cardinality-derived equations, or valid submatrix inequalities may strengthen the relaxation whenever they belong to \(\mathcal C\). For a minimization problem with an objective represented consistently in the lift, the optimal bound over \(R^+\) is no smaller than the bound over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any matrix constraints valid for every exact problem-specific lift may be intersected with the base relaxation, preserving feasibility while potentially improving its bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Aware Matrix Strengthening

source_witnesses.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

children.title: Lagrangian–Semidefinite Bound Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Dual-equivalence and bound-comparison relationships for selected quadratic relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–Semidefinite Bound Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between the Shor relaxation value and the quadratic Lagrangian bound under conic strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+c_i^\top x+r_i\) and consider minimizing \(q_0(x)\) subject to \(q_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Its Shor relaxation minimizes \(\langle Q_0,X\rangle+c_0^\top x+r_0\) subject to \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+c_i^\top x+r_i\leq0\) and \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). If this SDP has a finite optimum and satisfies Slater's condition, then its value equals \(\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\}\), and both values are lower bounds on the original minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under SDP strong duality, the Shor relaxation and the quadratic Lagrangian dual give the same lower bound on a quadratically constrained minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)
\exists(\bar x,\bar X):\ \begin{pmatrix}1&\bar x^\top\\\bar x&\bar X\end{pmatrix}\succ0,\ \langle Q_i,\bar X\rangle+c_i^\top\bar x+r_i<0
v_{\mathrm{SDP}}> -\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_x\left(q_0(x)+\sum_i\lambda_iq_i(x)\right)\le v_{\mathrm{QCQP}}

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal clique representation of a sparse positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), and let \(Z\) be a symmetric partial matrix whose specified entries are the diagonal and edges of \(G\). Then \(Z\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if every fully specified clique matrix \(Z[C_k,C_k]\) is positive semidefinite. Hence a sparse SDP may replace one completion constraint by the block constraints \(Z[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\), provided copies of entries shared by intersecting cliques are constrained to agree. The replacement preserves the feasible projections and objective value whenever the objective and other constraints use only specified entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, a global PSD-completion constraint is equivalent to PSD constraints on maximal clique blocks plus equality of shared entries.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is chordal}
C_1,\ldots,C_p\text{ are the maximal cliques of }G
\text{all model expressions use specified entries of }Z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z\text{ has a PSD completion}\iff Z[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\ \forall k\text{ with consistent overlaps}

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Cut Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separating a non-PSD lifted matrix by a linear eigenvector cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z(\xi)=Z_0+\sum_{j=1}^d\xi_jZ_j\) be an affine symmetric matrix required to satisfy \(Z(\xi)\succeq0\). If a relaxation solution \(\bar\xi\) has a vector \(v\) with \(v^\top Z(\bar\xi)v<0\), then positive semidefiniteness implies the globally valid linear inequality \(v^\top Z(\xi)v=v^\top Z_0v+\sum_{j=1}^d\xi_jv^\top Z_jv\geq0\). This inequality separates \(\bar\xi\). An eigenvector corresponding to \(\lambda_{\min}(Z(\bar\xi))<0\) supplies such a vector and a directly checkable violation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-eigenvalue eigenvector produces a valid linear inequality in lifted variables that separates the current non-PSD matrix.
