children.title: SDP–Cut Coordination
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces coordinating matrix bounds with linear cut pools.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP–Cut Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative coordination of a linear relaxation with PSD separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a polyhedral relaxation \(P\), an affine matrix \(Z(\xi)\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an objective, initialize \(P_0=P\). At iteration \(t\), optimize over \(P_t\) to obtain \(\xi^t\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(Z(\xi^t))\geq-\varepsilon\), return \(\xi^t\) as PSD-feasible to tolerance. Otherwise choose a unit eigenvector \(v^t\) for a negative eigenvalue and set \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\{\xi:(v^t)^\top Z(\xi)v^t\geq0\}\). If a prescribed iteration limit is reached, return the current relaxation bound and retained cuts, without claiming PSD feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a linear relaxation, detect a negative eigenvalue, add its linear PSD cut, and stop at spectral tolerance or a resource limit.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is polyhedral}
Z:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb S^n\text{ is affine}
\varepsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\min}(Z(\xi^t))\ge-\varepsilon\text{ at spectral termination; every added cut is PSD-valid}

knowledge_statements.title: QP-Based Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained by retaining the convex quadratic objective at a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) over a mixed-integer feasible set, where \(Q\succeq0\). At a branch-and-bound node \(u\), let \(F_u\) include the original convex constraints and node restrictions, and let \(R_u\) replace integrality by continuous bounds. Solving the convex quadratic program \(L_u=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_u\}\) gives \(L_u\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F_u\}\). Thus a node is safely pruned when its relaxation is infeasible or when \(L_u\) is no smaller than the incumbent objective value, subject to certified numerical tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous convex QP relaxation at a tree node supplies a valid lower bound and supports infeasibility or incumbent-based pruning.

F_u\subseteq R_u
\text{the problem is a minimization problem}

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started QP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reoptimization of a child-node convex QP from parent solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and let the child relaxation have feasible region \(R_{\mathrm{child}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{parent}}\). Given a certified solve of the parent QP, initialize the child solver from a compatible parent primal-dual iterate, active set, or factorization after updating the child bounds and dimensions. Repair or discard an initialization that violates the solver's requirements, then reoptimize the child QP using its ordinary optimality or infeasibility tests. Report a child bound only after those tests certify it to the declared tolerances; the warm start alone neither changes the child problem nor certifies a bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Parent-to-Child Bound Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic inheritance of valid minimization bounds under child-node restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_p\) be a parent-node relaxation and let every child relaxation satisfy \(R_c\subseteq R_p\). For the same minimization objective \(f\), define \(L_p=\inf_{x\in R_p}f(x)\) and \(L_c=\inf_{x\in R_c}f(x)\), with the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(L_p\leq L_c\). Consequently, any certified parent lower bound remains a valid, possibly weaker, lower bound for every child before reoptimization; after solving the child relaxation, the stored node bound may be strengthened to \(L_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a minimization relaxation cannot decrease its optimum, so a certified parent lower bound remains valid for each child.

knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which reused QP state does not constitute a valid node-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parent optimal solution reused at a child is only an initialization. If a new child bound excludes that point, it is not child-feasible; even when feasible, its objective is an upper bound for the child QP, not a certified lower bound. Likewise, parent multipliers need not satisfy child dual feasibility or complementarity. Therefore pruning from an inherited solver iterate is invalid unless either the certified parent lower bound alone suffices or child reoptimization produces a valid dual bound, infeasibility certificate, or residual-controlled optimality certificate for the modified QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reused iterate is not a child-node certificate; pruning requires an inherited valid lower bound or fresh dual, infeasibility, or optimality certification.

children.title: Branching Policies for Convex MIQP
children.top_down_role: Variable, constraint, and structure-aware branching choices for convex MIQP trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Policies for Convex MIQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-variable branching with QP-derived candidate scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node \(u\) with QP-relaxation region \(R_u\) and optimal relaxation solution \(x^*\), let \(J_f=\{j:j\text{ is integer-constrained and }x_j^*\notin\mathbb Z\}\). When \(J_f\neq\varnothing\), assign every candidate a defined score \(s_j\), such as a reliability-weighted estimate of its two child-bound increases, and choose \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in J_f}s_j\). Define the child relaxations \(R_u^-=R_u\cap\{x:x_{j^*}\leq\lfloor x_{j^*}^*\rfloor\}\) and \(R_u^+=R_u\cap\{x:x_{j^*}\geq\lceil x_{j^*}^*\rceil\}\). If \(J_f=\varnothing\), the relaxation solution satisfies the designated integrality restrictions and no integrality branch is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a fractional integer variable using a defined QP-informed score and split its node relaxation at the floor and ceiling of its relaxation value.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Selection for Convex MIQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-bound selection and global-gap accounting for convex-MIQP tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an open-node pool \(\mathcal N\), an incumbent value \(U\), and a certified lower bound \(L_u\) for every \(u\in\mathcal N\), with the invariant that the open nodes cover all feasible solutions not already pruned. Remove infeasible nodes and nodes satisfying \(L_u\geq U-\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal N\neq\varnothing\), best-bound selection chooses \(u^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathcal N}L_u\); after processing it, insert every surviving child with a valid bound. For a nonempty pool define \(L=\min_{u\in\mathcal N}L_u\). Under the absolute-gap convention, terminate with an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent if \(\mathcal N=\varnothing\), or if \(\mathcal N\neq\varnothing\) and \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the open node with the smallest certified QP bound and terminate when the exhaustive open-node pool is empty or its global bound is within the absolute tolerance of the incumbent.

\text{the open nodes cover all unpruned feasible solutions}
U\text{ is the value of a feasible incumbent}
\varepsilon\ge0

children.title: Classical Outer Approximation

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-tree outer approximation for differentiable convex MINLP with finitely many integer assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing a convex differentiable function \(f(x,y)\) subject to convex differentiable inequalities \(g_i(x,y)\leq0\), \(x\in X\), and \(y\in Y\subset\mathbb Z^p\), where \(X\) is convex and \(Y\) is finite. Maintain a MILP master whose objective and constraint linearizations are globally valid lower outer approximations. After the master selects \((x^k,y^k,\eta^k)\), fix \(y=y^k\) and solve the convex NLP globally. If it is feasible with solution \(z^k=(x^k_{\mathrm{NLP}},y^k)\), update the incumbent and add the supporting inequalities \(\eta\geq f(z^k)+\nabla f(z^k)^\top(z-z^k)\) and \(g_i(z^k)+\nabla g_i(z^k)^\top(z-z^k)\leq0\). If the fixed-integer NLP is infeasible, add a globally valid feasibility cut or a valid master constraint excluding \(y^k\). Repeat until the certified master lower bound is within \(\varepsilon\) of the incumbent or the master proves that no admissible assignment remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate a linear mixed-integer master with globally solved fixed-integer convex NLPs, adding supporting cuts for feasible assignments and valid feasibility or exclusion cuts for infeasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and }g_i\text{ are convex and differentiable on a convex domain containing the master points}
X\text{ is convex and }Y\subset\mathbb Z^p\text{ is finite}
\text{all master cuts are globally valid}
\text{each fixed-integer NLP and MILP master is solved globally}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U-L_{\mathrm{master}}\le\varepsilon\text{ at gap termination, or the master certifies that no admissible assignment remains}

notation.meaning: combined continuous and integer variable vector

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Master Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-tree processing of linear outer-approximation node masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize one branch-and-bound tree for a linear outer-approximation master containing globally valid supporting cuts. At each open node \(u\), solve its LP relaxation and prune it if infeasible or bounded by the incumbent. If the integer variables are fractional, branch and add the resulting node restrictions. If they are integral, solve the associated fixed-integer convex NLP; use a feasible solution to update the incumbent and add its globally valid objective and constraint linearizations to affected open nodes. Continue until the open-node pool is empty or its smallest certified LP bound closes the prescribed optimality gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex NLP Node Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-integer convex NLP used during LP–NLP tree-search coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x,y):g_j(x,y)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m,\ x\in X,\ y\in Y\}\). For an integer assignment \(\bar y\in Y\), its fixed-integer NLP is \[v(\bar y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,\bar y):g_j(x,\bar y)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] If the subproblem has an optimizer \(\bar x\), then \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a feasible incumbent candidate, and joint-convex supporting inequalities generated at that point are valid for the convex relaxation. If the subproblem is infeasible, it supplies no incumbent; a separately certified feasibility procedure may instead generate a valid feasibility cut or certify exclusion of \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing an integer assignment produces a convex continuous NLP. A feasible optimizer is an incumbent candidate and can generate globally valid supports under joint convexity; certified infeasibility can support a feasibility cut or exclusion of that assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\).
The functions \(f\) and \(g_j\), for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), are jointly convex on \(X\times\operatorname{conv}(Y)\).
Any supporting inequality asserted at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) uses a subgradient that exists there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(\bar y)\) is the continuous-subproblem value for \(\bar y\), and globally valid master supports require joint convexity on the relaxation domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Subproblem Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination rule for LP–NLP branch-and-cut outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a linear outer-approximation master with an objective variable \(\eta\), valid bounds, and available globally valid cuts. Repeatedly select an integer assignment \(\bar y\) encountered in the master tree and solve its fixed-integer convex NLP globally to the required tolerance. If it is feasible, use its optimizer \(\bar x\) to update the incumbent and add valid objective or constraint supporting cuts at \((\bar x,\bar y)\). If it is infeasible, add a valid feasibility cut or a certified exclusion of only \(\bar y\). Continue the same master tree, revisiting affected nodes as required. Stop when every open node has a valid lower bound at least \(U-\varepsilon\), where \(U\) is the incumbent value, or when exhaustive tree processing proves that no feasible assignment exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master tree proposes integer assignments, fixed-integer convex NLPs return incumbents or certified feasibility information, and globally valid cuts refine the continuing tree until exhaustive valid bounds close the prescribed gap or prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every generated inequality is valid for every retained feasible MINLP point.
Each fixed-integer NLP is solved globally to the accuracy required by \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The master solver maintains valid node lower bounds and exhaustively processes or validly prunes the tree.
The integer search is finite, or convergence of the specified tree-and-cut procedure is established separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon the stated stopping test, the incumbent is certified within \(\varepsilon\) of the global optimum, or exhaustive processing certifies infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Tree Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quesada–Grossmann dynamic OA within one branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Create one MILP branch-and-bound tree for a linear outer approximation of a convex MINLP. Whenever the tree produces an integer-feasible master point \((\hat x,\hat y,\hat\eta)\), solve the fixed-integer convex NLP with \(y=\hat y\). If that NLP is feasible, update the incumbent and add globally valid objective and constraint supporting cuts generated at an NLP solution. If it is infeasible, add a valid feasibility cut or a certified exclusion of \(\hat y\). Continue the existing tree, making every new cut effective at each node where it is valid and reprocessing affected nodes when necessary. Terminate when exhaustive tree processing leaves no open node with lower bound below \(U-\varepsilon\), or proves that no feasible integer assignment exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-tree outer approximation dynamically adds globally valid nonlinear supports to one continuing MILP branch-and-bound tree and terminates only when exhaustive valid bounds close the gap or prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The nonlinear functions are convex on the master relaxation domain and admit the supporting inequalities used by the algorithm.
Every feasibility cut or assignment exclusion is validly certified.
The tree solver maintains valid lower bounds and correctly propagates cuts or revisits affected nodes.
The integer search is finite, or convergence of the specified branch-and-cut procedure is established separately.
The fixed-integer NLPs and tree bounds are computed to accuracy consistent with \(\varepsilon\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Nonlinear Supporting Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting hyperplanes generated lazily during single-tree OA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z=(x,y)\) and let \(h:\mathbb R^{n+p}\to\mathbb R\) be convex. At a queried point \(\bar z\), choose \(s\in\partial h(\bar z)\). The dynamically generated cut is \[h(\bar z)+s^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0.\] Convexity implies that every point satisfying \(h(z)\le0\) satisfies this inequality. For a convex objective \(f\) represented by an epigraph variable \(\eta\), the analogous cut is \[\eta\ge f(\bar z)+q^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z),\qquad q\in\partial f(\bar z).\] These cuts may be inserted when a tree solution violates the nonlinear model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient at a queried point defines a global supporting inequality for each convex constraint or objective epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(f\) are proper convex functions and are subdifferentiable at \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities are valid outer-approximation cuts over the functions' common convex domain.

children.title: Cut-Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Locality, convexity, and numerical conditions affecting generated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between global convex supports and merely local linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable constraint \(h(z)\le0\), the linearization \(h(\bar z)+\nabla h(\bar z)^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0\) is globally valid on a convex domain \(D\) whenever \(h\) is convex on \(D\). Without convexity, validity can fail: for \(h(t)=1-t^2\) on \(D=[-2,2]\), linearization at \(\bar t=0\) gives \(1\le0\), which excludes every point, although \(t=2\) satisfies \(h(2)=-3\le0\). Thus a nonconvex linearization cannot be installed globally unless a separate argument establishes validity; it must be localized, replaced by a valid relaxation, or omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity makes supporting cuts globally valid; without it, a tangent may exclude feasible points and therefore requires localization or another validity argument.
assumptions_latex: The cut is intended for the domain \(D\) on which validity is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing convexity destroys the general implication \(h(z)\le0\Rightarrow h(\bar z)+\nabla h(\bar z)^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0\).

notation.meaning: domain over which a cut is asserted valid

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Cutting-Plane Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative cutting-plane scheme in a lifted separable formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a lifted convex MINLP with nonlinear inequalities \(h_k(w_k)\le0\), initialize a mixed-integer linear relaxation in variables \((x,y,w)\). At iteration \(r\), solve this relaxation and obtain \((x^r,y^r,w^r)\). For every violated block, select \(s_k^r\in\partial h_k(w_k^r)\) and add \[h_k(w_k^r)+(s_k^r)^{\mathsf T}(w_k-w_k^r)\le0.\] Reoptimize and repeat until all nonlinear inequalities are satisfied within tolerance. Return the current solution when it is feasible and its master lower bound meets the incumbent bound; otherwise report infeasibility when the relaxation becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended cutting-plane methods solve lifted MILP relaxations and iteratively add blockwise convex subgradient cuts until feasibility and the objective gap are certified.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_k\) is convex on the projected domain of \(w_k\).
The lifted linear linking constraints exactly relate \(w\) to \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every added inequality is valid for the lifted feasible set, so master objective values remain valid lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Outer-Approximation Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise OA representation for separable convex nonlinearities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a convex nonlinear expression is separable: \(H(z)=\sum_{i=1}^q h_i(z_i)\), where every \(h_i\) is convex. Introduce epigraph variables \(t_i\) and impose \(\sum_{i=1}^q t_i\le0\) together with \(t_i\ge h_i(z_i)\). Given sampled points \(\xi_i^r\) and subgradients \(s_i^r\in\partial h_i(\xi_i^r)\), a separable polyhedral outer approximation is \[t_i\ge h_i(\xi_i^r)+(s_i^r)^{\mathsf T}(z_i-\xi_i^r),\qquad i=1,\ldots,q.\] Each component can receive cuts independently, preserving validity while exploiting block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable convex constraint can be lifted into component epigraphs and approximated by independent supporting cuts for each nonlinear block.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_i\) is proper convex and subdifferentiable at every sampled point \(\xi_i^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted inequalities form a valid polyhedral relaxation of \(H(z)\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Master Designs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted master formulation exposing blockwise convex epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), and let \(r\in\{1,\ldots,R\}\) index separable convex constraints \[H_r(x,y)=\sum_{k=1}^{q_r}h_{rk}(C_{rk}x+D_{rk}y)\le0,\] where \(C_{rk}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{d_{rk}}\), \(D_{rk}:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^{d_{rk}}\), and \(h_{rk}:\mathbb R^{d_{rk}}\to\mathbb R\) is convex. Introduce \(w_{rk}=C_{rk}x+D_{rk}y\) and epigraph variables \(t_{rk}\in\mathbb R\). For each stored point \(\xi_{rk}^a\) and subgradient \(s_{rk}^a\in\partial h_{rk}(\xi_{rk}^a)\), an extended outer-approximation master retains the linking equations and imposes \[\sum_{k=1}^{q_r}t_{rk}\le0,\qquad t_{rk}\ge h_{rk}(\xi_{rk}^a)+(s_{rk}^a)^{\mathsf T}(w_{rk}-\xi_{rk}^a).\] These inequalities are imposed for the stored sample indices \(a\) and applicable pairs \((r,k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extended master introduces each nonlinear block argument and an epigraph variable, retains exact linear linking equations, and adds stored supporting inequalities independently for the convex components.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_{rk}\) is proper convex and subdifferentiable at every stored point \(\xi_{rk}^a\).
The equations \(w_{rk}=C_{rk}x+D_{rk}y\) define every component argument exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection of the extended outer-approximation master onto \((x,y)\) contains every feasible solution of the original separable convex constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex NLP Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous convex relaxation attached to a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex MINLP \(\min\{f(x,y):g_j(x,y)\le0,\ x\in X,\ y\in Y\}\), let a node impose bounds \(\ell^N\le y\le u^N\). Its NLP relaxation is \[L_N=\inf\{f(x,y):g_j(x,y)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m,\ x\in X,\ y\in\operatorname{conv}(Y),\ \ell^N\le y\le u^N\}.\] Every integer-feasible descendant point is feasible for this relaxation. Consequently, infeasibility of the relaxation proves node infeasibility, while any finite optimal value \(L_N\) is a valid lower bound for minimization over the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each node, integrality is relaxed within the node bounds; the resulting convex NLP supplies a valid lower bound or proves node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(Y)\) are convex.
The objective and constraint functions are convex on the node relaxation domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\le v_N\), where \(v_N\) is the optimal value over integer-feasible points in node \(N\).

children.title: Nonlinear Branching Policies
children.top_down_role: Branching choices informed by nonlinear variables, expressions, or relaxation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Branching Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching rule driven by a fractional convex-NLP relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the convex NLP relaxation at node \(N\) and obtain \((x^N,y^N)\). If every required component of \(y^N\) is integral, process it as an integer-feasible candidate. Otherwise select an index \(i\) with \(y_i^N\notin\mathbb Z\), optionally using reliability, pseudocost, or strong-branching scores computed from child NLP bounds. Create children \[N^-:\ y_i\le\lfloor y_i^N\rfloor,\qquad N^+:\ y_i\ge\lceil y_i^N\rceil.\] Each integer-feasible point of \(N\) belongs to at least one child. Continue by a prescribed node-selection rule until all nodes are processed or pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional integer variable, optionally selected using nonlinear relaxation bound predictions, and partition the node into floor and ceiling children.
assumptions_latex: The branched component \(y_i\) is required to be integer.
Both child node constraints are retained in subsequent NLP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children cover all integer-feasible points of \(N\) and exclude the fractional value \(y_i^N\).

children.title: NLP Node-Pruning Certificates
children.top_down_role: Optimality, infeasibility, and cutoff evidence supporting node pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: NLP Node-Pruning Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable fathoming conditions derived from convex node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent for a minimization problem, let \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and let \(L_N\) be a certified lower bound from the convex NLP relaxation of node \(N\). The node may be pruned if the relaxation is certified infeasible or if \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\). It may also be fathomed if an optimal relaxation solution satisfies every required integrality condition and is feasible for the original node formulation, because its objective then equals the node's integer optimum. A pruning certificate is, respectively, a verifiable convex-infeasibility certificate, a verified relaxation bound satisfying the displayed inequality, or an optimal relaxation solution accompanied by integrality and original-feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is prunable when its convex relaxation is certified infeasible, its lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond tolerance, or an optimal relaxation point is both integral and feasible for the original node problem.
assumptions_latex: The NLP relaxation contains every integer-feasible point of node \(N\).
The reported infeasibility, optimality, and bound information is certified to the algorithm's numerical tolerance.
Any integral relaxation optimizer used for fathoming is checked against all constraints of the original node formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning under any stated condition cannot discard an integer-feasible solution that improves \(U\) by more than \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Convex-MINLP Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master cuts derived from feasible convex continuous subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-MINLP Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Benders optimality cut from a feasible convex continuous subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed integer vector \(\bar y\), consider \(v(\bar y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,\bar y):g(x,\bar y)\le0\}\). Let \(\bar x\) solve this subproblem and let \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) be an optimal multiplier. Define the Lagrangian value function \[\phi_{\bar\lambda}(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x,y)+\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,y)\bigr).\] Weak duality gives \(\phi_{\bar\lambda}(y)\le v(y)\) for every feasible integer assignment \(y\). Hence the generalized Benders master inequality \[\eta\ge\phi_{\bar\lambda}(y)\] is a valid optimality cut and is tight at \(\bar y\) under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal multipliers from a feasible fixed-integer convex subproblem define a Lagrangian lower-bound function and hence a valid generalized Benders optimality cut.
assumptions_latex: For each relevant \(y\), the continuous subproblem is convex in \(x\).
The subproblem at \(\bar y\) satisfies strong duality and attains primal and dual optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\ge\phi_{\bar\lambda}(y)\) is valid for the value-function epigraph and satisfies \(\phi_{\bar\lambda}(\bar y)=v(\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: master approximation of the value function

children.title: Convex-MINLP Feasibility Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master exclusions derived from infeasible convex continuous subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-MINLP Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Benders cut obtained from a convex feasibility-value subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer parameter \(y\in Y\), define \(\phi(y)=\inf_{x,t}\{t:g_i(x,y)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Assume \(\phi\) is finite and convex on \(\operatorname{conv}(Y)\). If a tested assignment \(\bar y\) satisfies \(\phi(\bar y)>0\) and \(s\in\partial\phi(\bar y)\), then every assignment admitting some \(x\) with \(g_i(x,y)\le0\) satisfies \[\phi(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\le0.\] Hence this inequality is a valid master feasibility cut and excludes \(\bar y\). A subgradient obtained from optimal multipliers of the convex feasibility subproblem is a checkable certificate of the cut coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive convex feasibility value and one of its subgradients yield a valid master cut excluding the infeasible integer assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\) and each \(g_i\) is jointly convex on the relevant convex domain.
\(\phi\) is finite at \(\bar y\), and the feasibility-value subproblem attains its optimum.
\(s\in\partial\phi(\bar y)\) is certified by valid convex-subproblem multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\le0\) is valid for every feasible assignment and is violated by \(\bar y\).

notation.meaning: minimum uniform constraint violation at assignment y
subgradient of the feasibility-value function at the tested assignment

children.title: Convex MIQCP Supporting-Cut Certificates
children.top_down_role: Supporting approximations certifying valid bounds for convex quadratic constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex MIQCP Supporting-Cut Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order supporting inequalities for differentiable convex quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(z)=\tfrac12 z^{\mathsf T}Qz+a^{\mathsf T}z-b\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(\bar z\) be any linearization point. Convexity gives \[q(z)\ge q(\bar z)+\nabla q(\bar z)^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z),\qquad \nabla q(\bar z)=Q\bar z+a.\] Consequently every point satisfying \(q(z)\le0\) also satisfies the supporting cut \[q(\bar z)+(Q\bar z+a)^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0.\] The data \((Q,a,b,\bar z)\), together with a certificate that \(Q\succeq0\), therefore certify validity of this linear outer-approximation inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic constraint lies above each tangent plane, so its tangent inequality is a verifiable linear outer approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(\bar z\) belongs to the domain of the quadratic constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(z)\le0\Rightarrow q(\bar z)+(Q\bar z+a)^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0\).

children.title: Fixed-Integer Optimality Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Integer Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT primal-dual certificate for a fixed-integer convex nonlinear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(y=\bar y\) and consider \(v(\bar y)=\inf_x\{f(x,\bar y):g_i(x,\bar y)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Suppose the functions in \(x\) are convex and Slater's condition holds. A tuple \((\bar x,\lambda)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\) is an optimality certificate when \(g_i(\bar x,\bar y)\le0\), \(0\in\partial_x f(\bar x,\bar y)+\sum_i\lambda_i\partial_xg_i(\bar x,\bar y)\), and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x,\bar y)=0\) for every \(i\). These conditions certify \(v(\bar y)=f(\bar x,\bar y)=\inf_x\{f(x,\bar y)+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x,\bar y)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under convexity and Slater regularity, primal feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, stationarity, and complementarity certify global optimality at the fixed integer assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\cdot,\bar y)\) and \(g_i(\cdot,\bar y)\) are proper closed convex functions.
The fixed-assignment subproblem satisfies Slater's condition.
The displayed infimum and certificate point are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is globally optimal and \(v(\bar y)=f(\bar x,\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of the continuous subproblem at the fixed assignment
convex subdifferential with respect to continuous variables

children.title: Fixed-Integer Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility evidence from convex subproblems with fixed integer assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Integer Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex alternative certificate derived from a strictly positive violation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(y=\bar y\) and define \(\phi(\bar y)=\inf_{x,t}\{t:g_i(x,\bar y)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). If the convex problem attains \((\bar x,\bar t)\) with \(\bar t>0\), and multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), stationarity \(0\in\sum_i\lambda_i\partial_xg_i(\bar x,\bar y)\), and complementarity \(\lambda_i(g_i(\bar x,\bar y)-\bar t)=0\), then \(\bar t=\phi(\bar y)>0\). Thus no \(x\) can satisfy all inequalities \(g_i(x,\bar y)\le0\), and \((\bar x,\bar t,\lambda)\) certifies infeasibility of the fixed-integer subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT data proving that the minimum uniform constraint violation is positive certify infeasibility of the continuous subproblem at the fixed assignment.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i(\cdot,\bar y)\) is proper closed convex.
The violation-minimization problem satisfies a convex constraint qualification.
The displayed primal and multiplier solutions are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(\bar y)=\bar t>0\), so \(\{x:g_i(x,\bar y)\le0\ \forall i\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: minimum uniform violation at the fixed assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Master Feedback from Fixed Assignments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of fixed-assignment certificates into valid master constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex MINLP value function \(v(y)=\inf_x\{f(x,y):g_i(x,y)\le0\}\), let \(\bar y\) be tested. If an optimality certificate supplies \(v(\bar y)\) and \(s\in\partial v(\bar y)\), then the master epigraph variable \(\eta\) may receive \[\eta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y).\] If instead an infeasibility certificate supplies a convex feasibility function \(\phi\), with \(\phi(\bar y)>0\) and \(r\in\partial\phi(\bar y)\), then the master may receive \[\phi(\bar y)+r^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\le0.\] Convex subgradient inequalities certify both constraints for all feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-assignment optimality produces an epigraph lower cut; fixed-assignment infeasibility produces a feasibility cut excluding the tested assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) and the chosen feasibility function \(\phi\) are convex on \(\operatorname{conv}(Y)\).
The fixed-assignment certificates establish the stated values and subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed optimality or feasibility inequality is valid master feedback for every globally feasible assignment.

children.title: Master Lower-Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Global lower-bound evidence supplied by master relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Lower-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified global lower bound furnished by a valid master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization MINLP with optimal value \(z^*\). Let a master problem minimize \(\eta\) over integer assignments and constraints that are valid for every feasible original solution, with \(\eta\) constrained by certified underestimators of the fixed-assignment value function. If the master is solved globally and returns value \(L\), then each original feasible pair maps to a master-feasible pair having \(\eta\) no larger than its objective value. Therefore \[L\le z^*.\] A master solution certificate, together with validity certificates for all retained cuts and a complete certificate of the master optimum, constitutes a verifiable lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally solved master relaxation made only of valid constraints and objective underestimators certifies a lower bound on the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem with value \(z^*\).
Every original feasible solution has a corresponding feasible master representation.
The master is solved globally with certified value \(L\).

notation.meaning: certified optimal value of the master relaxation
global optimal value of the original MINLP

children.title: Incumbent Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Relative or absolute gap evidence based on incumbent comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute or relative optimality guarantee from certified primal and dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U\) be the objective value of a certified feasible incumbent and let \(L\le z^*\) be a certified global lower bound. Then \[0\le U-z^*\le U-L.\] Thus \(U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\)-optimality. Under the convention \(\operatorname{gap}_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\), the inequality \(\operatorname{gap}_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) certifies the corresponding relative tolerance. The certificate consists of the feasible incumbent, its evaluated objective, the lower-bound certificate, and the stated arithmetic comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and certified lower bound bound suboptimality by their difference and provide absolute or convention-specific relative gap certificates.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is feasible and has finite objective value \(U\).
\(L\) is a valid lower bound on the finite optimum \(z^*\).
The relative-gap normalization is fixed as displayed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-z^*\le U-L\), with the displayed absolute and relative tolerance guarantees.

notation.meaning: objective value of the certified incumbent

children.title: Exact Termination Evidence
children.top_down_role: Combined evidence supporting exact completion of convex mixed-integer nonlinear search.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Termination Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-gap certificate for exact global termination of a minimization algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\hat x,\hat y)\) be a certified feasible solution with objective \(U=f(\hat x,\hat y)\), and let \(L\) be a certified global lower bound obtained from a complete master relaxation or an exhausted search tree. If exact arithmetic establishes \(L=U\), then weak bounding gives \(L\le z^*\le U\), hence \[z^*=L=U.\] The feasible-solution certificate, all lower-bound and cut-validity certificates, the certificate of complete master or tree processing, and the exact equality \(L=U\) together constitute exact termination evidence. A merely numerical equality within tolerance certifies only approximate termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact equality of a certified global lower bound and a certified feasible incumbent value proves global optimality; tolerance-based equality does not prove exact termination.
assumptions_latex: \((\hat x,\hat y)\) is exactly feasible and its objective value is exactly \(U\).
\(L\) is an exact certified lower bound covering the entire remaining search region.
The equality \(L=U\) is established without tolerance ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\hat x,\hat y)\) is globally optimal and \(z^*=L=U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Native Conic Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound node relaxation retaining the original closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:Ax+By-b\in K,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\). At a search node imposing bounds \(\ell\le y\le u\), its native conic relaxation is \[L_{\ell,u}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:Ax+By-b\in K,\ \ell\le y\le u,\ y\in\operatorname{conv}(Y)\}.\] Every integer-feasible solution in the node is feasible for this relaxation, so \(L_{\ell,u}\) is a valid node lower bound. The conic constraint is retained rather than replaced by finitely many linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing integrality while preserving the cone gives a conic node problem whose optimum lower-bounds every integer-feasible solution in that node.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The continuous relaxation of the node is solved globally.
The original objective is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\ell,u}\) is a valid lower bound for the node's mixed-integer conic problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Outer Approximation of Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite dual-cone cuts replacing conic membership by a polyhedral relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), membership satisfies \[w\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lambda^{\mathsf T}w\ge0\ \text{for every }\lambda\in K^*.\] Given a finite set \(D\subseteq K^*\), define \(P_D=\{w:\lambda^{\mathsf T}w\ge0\ \forall\lambda\in D\}\). Then \(K\subseteq P_D\), so replacing \(Ax+By-b\in K\) by \(Ax+By-b\in P_D\) yields a polyhedral outer relaxation suitable for mixed-integer linear search. If a relaxation point \(\bar w\notin K\), any \(\lambda\in K^*\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\bar w<0\) supplies a valid separating cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite collection of dual-cone inequalities contains the cone and gives a linear outer relaxation; a violated dual-cone inequality separates any detected nonconic point.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(D\) is a finite subset of the dual cone \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\subseteq P_D\), and every \(\lambda\in K^*\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\bar w<0\) gives a valid cut excluding \(\bar w\).

notation.meaning: dual cone consisting of vectors nonnegative on K
finite set of dual-cone cut normals
polyhedral outer approximation induced by D

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Dual Cut Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible vectors certifying affine lower cuts for conic value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\), consider \(v(y)=\inf_x\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+By-b\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. If \(\lambda\in K^*\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c\), then weak conic duality gives \[v(y)\ge\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-By).\] Hence the master inequality \(\eta\ge\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\) is valid for every feasible assignment, independently of dual attainment. Membership \(\lambda\in K^*\) and the equality \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c\) form a directly checkable certificate of cut validity; dual optimality at a tested assignment makes the cut tight there under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any conic-dual feasible vector yields a valid affine objective lower cut; strong duality makes an optimal dual vector's cut tight at the tested assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\).
\(\lambda\in K^*\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c\).
Strong duality is required only for the asserted tightness at a tested assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\ge\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\) is a valid master cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Dual Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic alternative ray proving fixed-assignment infeasibility and defining a master cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(y=\bar y\) in the conic system \(Ax+By-b\in K\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. If a vector \(\lambda\in K^*\) satisfies \[A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0,\qquad \lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-B\bar y)>0,\] then the fixed system is infeasible: any feasible \(x\) would imply \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax+B\bar y-b)\ge0\), contradicting the strict inequality. Moreover every assignment admitting a feasible \(x\) must satisfy \[\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\le0.\] Thus the dual ray certifies both fixed-assignment infeasibility and validity of a master feasibility cut excluding \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-cone ray orthogonal to continuous columns and strictly separating the fixed right-hand side proves infeasibility and supplies a valid feasibility cut.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(\lambda\in K^*\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\).
\(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-B\bar y)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed system is infeasible, and \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\le0\) is valid for every feasible assignment.

children.title: Dual-Ray Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regularity and numerical regimes affecting conic dual-ray evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Ray Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and numerical limits of conic dual rays used during mixed-integer conic search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic system \(Ax-b\in K\), any \(y\in K^*\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\) is an exact infeasibility certificate. A computed vector \(\widehat y\) is not an exact certificate when tolerance tests do not establish cone membership, orthogonality, and a strictly positive separating margin. Weak infeasibility or nonclosed cone images may preclude a certificate having these strict conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact dual ray certifies conic infeasibility only when cone membership, orthogonality, and strict separation hold; numerical residuals and weak infeasibility delimit its reliability.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^m:\langle y,z\rangle\ge0\ \forall z\in K\}\).
The conic system is \(Ax-b\in K\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any \(y\in K^*\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\) certifies infeasibility. Tolerance-level satisfaction of these conditions does not by itself provide an exact certificate, and weakly infeasible systems may have no such strict ray.

children.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure
children.top_down_role: Regularity failures affecting convex subproblem multipliers or supporting information.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of KKT-based subproblem evidence when an applicable constraint qualification is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without an applicable constraint qualification, an optimal differentiable nonlinear subproblem can lack KKT multipliers. For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}}x\) subject to \(x^2\le0\), the unique feasible and globally optimal point is \(x=0\), but no \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies KKT stationarity there. Consequently, failure to obtain multipliers does not establish nonoptimality or infeasibility, and a multiplier-dependent outer-approximation cut is unavailable for this subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a constraint qualification, an optimal differentiable subproblem may have no KKT multipliers, leaving multiplier-based outer-approximation evidence unavailable.
assumptions_latex: The continuous subproblem is differentiable, and no constraint qualification guaranteeing KKT multipliers is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}}x\) subject to \(x^2\le0\), the optimizer \(x=0\) has no multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying KKT stationarity. Thus missing multipliers do not imply nonoptimality or infeasibility.

children.title: Dual-Certificate Failure
children.top_down_role: Missing or invalid dual evidence returned by convex subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Conic infeasibility is tested through strict separation by a finite dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consider the semidefinite system \(X\succeq0\), \(X_{11}=0\), and \(X_{12}=1\), with \(X\in\mathbb{S}^2\). It is infeasible because positive semidefiniteness and \(X_{11}=0\) force \(X_{12}=0\). Yet the matrices \(X_{\varepsilon}=\begin{pmatrix}\varepsilon&1\\1&1/\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) approach the affine constraints as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Hence the two closed convex sets have zero distance and admit no strict separating hyperplane. An infeasibility routine restricted to strict dual certificates can therefore fail to certify this weakly infeasible system.

children.title: Numerical Dual-Evidence Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes producing weak or unreliable certificate information.

assumptions_latex: The exact certificate conditions are \(y\in K^*\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle>0\).
A solver reports a floating-point vector \(\widehat y\) using absolute feasibility tolerance \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported ray is numerically inconclusive whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat y,K^*)\le\tau\), \(\|A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\|\le\tau\), and \(0<\langle b,\widehat y\rangle\le\tau\), because admissible perturbations can eliminate the strict separating margin. More generally, scaling may make small absolute residuals large relative residuals. Before a cut or node-pruning decision uses \(\widehat y\), the implementation must validate cone membership, stationarity, and a scale-aware positive margin; otherwise the purported evidence does not certify exact infeasibility.

children.title: Convexity-Interface Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure of smooth convex-method interfaces under nonsmooth or misclassified nonlinear structure.

children.title: Nonsmooth Interface Failure
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns of smooth supporting-cut or derivative-based interfaces.

assumptions_latex: The outer-approximation interface accepts only classical gradients for nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the convex constraint \(f(x)=|x|\le 0\), the sole feasible point is \(x=0\), where \(\nabla f(0)\) does not exist. Consequently, a gradient-only interface cannot construct its prescribed linearization there. Convexity itself has not failed: every \(g\in\partial f(0)=[-1,1]\) yields the valid support inequality \(f(x)\ge f(0)+gx\). The failure boundary is therefore the interface requirement of differentiability; accepting certified subgradients restores valid outer-approximation cuts, whereas an arbitrary replacement slope outside \(\partial f(0)\) need not be valid.

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of the constraint function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability-dependent outer approximation at a nonsmooth convex constraint.

children.title: Hidden Nonconvexity
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex structure concealed by modeling form or incorrect classification.

assumptions_latex: A modeling interface classifies a nonlinear expression as convex and generates tangent underestimators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\) on \([-1,1]^2\). Its Hessian has eigenvalues \(1\) and \(-1\), so \(f\) is neither convex nor concave. At \((0,0)\), the tangent expression is identically \(0\), but \(f(1,-1)=-1<0\). Thus the asserted convex support inequality \(f(x)\ge0\) is false. Hidden bilinear or indefinite-quadratic structure therefore invalidates tangent cuts unless the relevant domain restriction or reformulation independently establishes convexity.

children.title: Convexity-Misclassification Consequences
children.top_down_role: Validity and certification consequences of applying convex methods to misclassified structure.

assumptions_latex: A minimization algorithm treats \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\) on \([-1,1]^2\) as convex.
It uses the tangent at \((0,0)\) as a global lower estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated estimator is \(f(x_1,x_2)\ge0\), although the feasible point \((1,-1)\) has value \(-1\). Hence the relaxation reports the invalid lower bound \(0\), exceeding the true optimum \(-1\). Any pruning decision based on this bound may discard a node containing a global optimizer. Thus convexity misclassification can destroy both lower-bound validity and global-optimality certification; subsequent convergence claims based on valid supporting hyperplanes no longer apply.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalid bounds and unsafe pruning caused by treating a nonconvex function as convex.

children.title: Weak Outer-Approximation Geometry
children.top_down_role: Poorly scaled or highly curved regions requiring extensive supporting approximations.

assumptions_latex: The convex function is \(f_M(x)=Mx^2\) on \([-1,1]\), where \(M>0\).
An outer approximation uses tangents at \(m\ge1\) points \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\in[-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangent at \(t_i\) is \(\ell_i(x)=M(2t_i x-t_i^2)\), and its error is \(f_M(x)-\ell_i(x)=M(x-t_i)^2\). Therefore the polyhedral underestimator \(L_m(x)=\max_i\ell_i(x)\) satisfies \(\max_{x\in[-1,1]}(f_M(x)-L_m(x))\ge M/m^2\), because \(m\) points cannot cover an interval of length \(2\) with radius below \(1/m\). Thus curvature or scaling can force many supporting cuts to achieve a prescribed uniform error.

children.title: Quadratic Relaxation Routing
children.top_down_role: Selection among envelope, linear, conic, semidefinite, and specialized quadratic bounds.

assumptions_latex: A quadratic expression is \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on a node box \([\ell,u]\).
The symmetric matrix \(Q\) and finite-variable bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Route the relaxation as follows. If \(Q\succeq0\) in an epigraph or convex inequality orientation, retain the convex quadratic or an equivalent second-order-cone representation. If the expression is separable or sparse bilinear over finite bounds, introduce product variables and their convex envelopes. Otherwise introduce \(X\) for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\), replace \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) by \(\langle Q,X\rangle\), and impose either selected envelope constraints or the semidefinite condition \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). Output the cheapest routed model meeting the required bound strength; every route must relax, rather than exclude, the node's feasible set.

children.title: Quadratic Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Detection and generation of violated cuts from quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvector separation for a violated semidefinite quadratic lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(\bar Y=Y(\bar x,\bar X)\) from a solution of a relaxation that does not yet enforce the full condition \(Y(x,X)\succeq0\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(\bar Y)<0\), choose a unit eigenvector \(v\) for that eigenvalue and add \(v^{\mathsf T}Y(x,X)v\ge0\). This inequality is linear in \((x,X)\), is valid for every positive-semidefinite lifting, and is violated by \((\bar x,\bar X)\). If no eigenvalue is below the separation tolerance, this oracle returns no cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a point from a relaxation that does not fully enforce positive semidefiniteness, a negative eigenvector of its lifted matrix defines a valid linear separating cut.
assumptions_latex: The target lifted relaxation requires \(Y(x,X):=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).
A solution \((\bar x,\bar X)\) is available from a relaxation that may violate this semidefinite condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_{\min}(Y(\bar x,\bar X))<0\), a corresponding unit eigenvector \(v\) defines the valid violated inequality \(v^{\mathsf T}Y(x,X)v\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

children.title: Quadratic Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Variable-domain contraction derived from quadratic constraints or expressions.

assumptions_latex: A quadratic constraint is decomposed as \(a x_j^2+b x_j+r(x_{-j})\le0\) on the current box.
A valid lower bound \(L\le r(x_{-j})\) is available throughout that box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compute the univariate necessary condition \(a x_j^2+b x_j+L\le0\). Let \(S:=\{t\in[\ell_j,u_j]:at^2+bt+L\le0\}\). If \(S=\varnothing\), declare the node infeasible. Otherwise replace the domain of \(x_j\) by \(S\), or by its interval hull when only interval bounds are stored. Repeat over variables and constraints until no bound changes beyond tolerance. Because every feasible point satisfies the necessary univariate inequality, each update preserves all feasible points while possibly tightening the node domain.

children.title: Separation–Propagation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between quadratic cut generation and domain contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation–Propagation Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating valid cut generation, bound propagation, and envelope rebuilding while retaining all earlier valid restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be the original node feasible set in the common lifted space, with \(\mathcal F\subseteq R_0\cap B_0\). At iteration \(k\), intersect \(R_k\) with valid separated cuts to form \(R_k'\). Propagate the quadratic constraints to obtain \(B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k\) while preserving \(\mathcal F\subseteq B_{k+1}\). Let \(E(B_{k+1})\) be valid bound-dependent envelope constraints on the tightened box, and set \(R_{k+1}:=R_k'\cap E(B_{k+1})\). Stop when no cut or bound changes beyond tolerance or when a resource limit is reached. Then every iteration preserves \(\mathcal F\), retains earlier cuts, and permits tighter bounds and stronger relaxations to reinforce one another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate valid separation and propagation while retaining previous cuts: intersect the relaxation with new cuts, tighten bounds without removing feasible points, and add envelopes valid on the tightened box.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is the original node feasible set represented in the same lifted space as the relaxations.
Every separated cut contains \(\mathcal F\), every propagation update retains \(\mathcal F\), and every rebuilt envelope is valid for \(\mathcal F\) on the updated box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updates satisfy \(\mathcal F\subseteq R_k'\cap B_{k+1}\) and \(R_{k+1}=R_k'\cap E(B_{k+1})\subseteq R_k'\), so separation, propagation, and envelope rebuilding preserve the original node feasible set while monotonically strengthening retained relaxation information.

children.title: Quadratic Spatial-Branching Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of unresolved quadratic relaxation gaps to the spatial search layer.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation supplies a valid lower bound \(L(C)\) for every child box \(C\subseteq B=[\ell,u]\), where \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\ell_i<u_i\) for each \(i\).
A finite incumbent value \(U\) is available for the minimization problem, and the pruning tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branching operation preserves valid lower bounding on the child boxes and transfers the unresolved relaxation gap to the spatial search layer.

notation.meaning: Valid relaxation lower bound on a box

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node box \(B=[\ell,u]\), compute its valid relaxation bound \(L(B)\). If \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\), prune the node. Otherwise, select an index \(j\) whose variable participates in an unresolved nonconvex quadratic term, choose \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\), and form \(B^-:=B\cap\{x:x_j\le s\}\) and \(B^+:=B\cap\{x:x_j\ge s\}\). Rebuild valid quadratic relaxations on the children, compute \(L(B^-)\) and \(L(B^+)\), and retain exactly those children \(C\in\{B^-,B^+\}\) satisfying \(L(C)<U-\varepsilon\). The output is the resulting set of active child nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a variable involved in an unresolved nonconvex quadratic term, rebuild valid lower-bounding relaxations on both child boxes, and retain only children whose bounds do not meet the incumbent pruning threshold.

children.title: Local-Solution–Global-Certificate Gap
children.top_down_role: Boundary between locally feasible solutions and globally valid lower-bound evidence.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite global optimum value \(v^*\).
A feasible point \(\hat x\), a valid global relaxation lower bound \(L\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility gives \(v^*\le f(\hat x)\), while the independent global bound gives \(L\le v^*\); consequently, \(f(\hat x)-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.

notation.meaning: Objective value of a feasible local solution

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility of \(\hat x\) gives \(v^*\le f(\hat x)\). First- or second-order local optimality conditions, when applicable, do not in general imply \(f(\hat x)=v^*\) for a nonconvex problem. A globally valid relaxation supplies the independent inequality \(L\le v^*\), and hence \(0\le f(\hat x)-v^*\le f(\hat x)-L\). Therefore, \(f(\hat x)-L\le\varepsilon\) is a verifiable global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate, whereas a local solver's termination test alone is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible local solution gives an upper bound but not a global certificate. A valid global lower bound closes that gap, and a sufficiently small upper-minus-lower bound certifies global approximate optimality.

children.title: Alpha Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Curvature-corrected convex lower models based on alpha constructions.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\), and set \(B=[\ell,u]\).
The function \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open set containing \(B\).
The vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfies \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(f_\alpha\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-based diagonal curvature correction in the alphaBB sense.

source_refs.locator: 6.4 CGU-underestimators p. 78
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[f_\alpha(x):=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i).\] For every \(x\in B\), each product satisfies \((\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\le0\), so \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\). Moreover, \(\nabla^2 f_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\). The assumed positive-semidefinite Hessian condition therefore makes \(f_\alpha\) convex on \(B\), so it is a convex underestimator of \(f\) there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The alpha construction adds nonpositive separable box terms to the target, using coefficients large enough to remove negative curvature and produce a convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.title: Alpha Underestimators

children.title: Curvature-Correction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing curvature-correction suitability and strength.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open set containing a convex box \(B\).
The symmetric matrix field \(H_-:B\to\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(H_-(x)\preceq\nabla^2 f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
The correction \(q\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open set containing \(B\) and satisfies \(q(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(H_-(x)+\nabla^2q(x)\succeq0\) on \(B\) is sufficient for \(f+q\) to be a convex underestimator; failure of convexity is established by a negative-curvature direction of the actual corrected Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion separating unnecessary, sufficient, and insufficient curvature correction.

source_refs.locator: 6.4 CGU-underestimators p. 78
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(g:=f+q\). Since \(q(x)\le0\) on \(B\), one has \(g(x)\le f(x)\) there. If \(H_-(x)+
abla^2q(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\), then \(
abla^2g(x)\succeq0\) throughout \(B\), so \(g\) is convex. If \(f\) is already convex, the zero correction is sufficient. Conversely, if some \(x\in B\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfy \(d^	op(
abla^2f(x)+
abla^2q(x))d<0\), then \(g\) is not convex on \(B\), and the correction is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpositive correction is sufficient when a certified Hessian lower bound shows that it removes all negative curvature. No correction is needed when the target is already convex, while a negative-curvature direction of the corrected Hessian proves insufficiency.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Correction Regimes

children.title: Convexified Polynomial Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Convex lower models obtained from polynomial convexification.

assumptions_latex: The polynomial \(p:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is evaluated on a convex box \(B\).
A polynomial correction \(r\) is nonpositive on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected polynomial \(g=p+r\) is a convex underestimator whenever its Hessian is positive semidefinite throughout \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial correction characterized by global dominance and convexity on a box.

source_refs.locator: 6.5 Convexified polynomial underestimators p. 78

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(g(x):=p(x)+r(x)\). If \(r(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in B\), then \(g(x)\le p(x)\) on \(B\). If additionally \(
abla^2p(x)+
abla^2r(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\), then \(g\) is convex on \(B\). Hence the two verifiable conditions \(r\le0\) and \(
abla^2g\succeq0\) on \(B\) make \(g\) a convexified polynomial underestimator of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial correction produces a convex underestimator when it never raises the target and makes the corrected Hessian positive semidefinite over the entire box.

children.title: Interval-Sampling Underestimation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Certified interval constructions and restricted-sampling alternatives.

children.title: Rigorous Interval Underestimation
children.top_down_role: Certified lower models derived from interval enclosures.

assumptions_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a compact interval box and let \(f:B\to\mathbb R\).
For every interval subbox \(X\subseteq B\), the outward-rounded interval extension \(F\) returns an interval \(F(X)\) satisfying \(\{f(x):x\in X\}\subseteq F(X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower endpoint of \(F(B)\), or the minimum lower endpoint over a finite box cover of \(B\), is a rigorous global lower bound for \(f\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded interval enclosure as a global underestimation certificate.

source_refs.locator: 6.5.1 Rigorous underestimators p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(F(B)=[\underline{F(B)},\overline{F(B)}]\). The enclosure property gives \(f(x)\ge\underline{F(B)}\) for every \(x\in B\). More generally, let \(m\in\mathbb N\) and let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subseteq B\) be interval boxes satisfying \(B\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^mB_k\). Then \[L:=\min_{1\le k\le m}\underline{F(B_k)}\] satisfies \(L\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\), and hence \(L\le\min_{x\in B}f(x)\). The cover together with the outward-rounded enclosures constitutes the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded interval evaluation encloses every function value on a box. Its lower endpoint, or the smallest lower endpoint over a finite cover, is therefore a rigorous global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Rigorous Interval Underestimation

children.title: Sampled Underestimation
children.top_down_role: Lower-model construction based on restricted function or derivative samples.

assumptions_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:B\to\mathbb R\), and let \(S\subset B\) be finite.
The prescribed model class \(\mathcal G\) consists of real-valued functions on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(g(s)\le f(s)\) for \(s\in S\) certify underestimation only on \(S\), unless an additional global certificate controls \(f-g\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample fitting without an automatic global-validity claim.

source_refs.locator: 6.5 Convexified polynomial underestimators p. 78
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sampled underestimator is a function \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfying \(g(s)\le f(s)\) for every \(s\in S\). These finitely many inequalities establish underestimation on \(S\) only. To conclude \(g(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\), one must additionally certify that \(f-g\) is nonnegative on \(B\), for example through an interval enclosure, an exact positivity certificate, or a regularity bound combined with a covering-radius estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model fitted below finitely many observed values is an underestimator only at those samples. Global validity requires an additional certificate controlling the unsampled domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampled Underestimation

children.title: Sampling-Certification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating rigorous sampled bounds from heuristic sampled approximations.

assumptions_latex: The sample set \(S\subset[0,1]\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite sampled inequalities do not certify global underestimation, even for smooth polynomial functions.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-sampling failure for unrestricted polynomial candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x):=0\) on \([0,1]\), and for any finite \(S\subset[0,1]\) define \(g(x):=\prod_{s\in S}(x-s)^2\). Then \(g(s)=0=f(s)\) for every \(s\in S\), so all sampled underestimation inequalities hold. However, \(g(x)>0=f(x)\) for every \(x\in[0,1]\setminus S\). Therefore no finite sampling test, without a degree restriction and a certified interpolation-error, Lipschitz, interval, or positivity bound, establishes \(g\le f\) on the complete interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial can agree with a zero target at every finite sample yet be positive everywhere else, so sampling alone cannot certify global underestimation.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Certification Boundaries

children.title: Univariate Piecewise-Linear Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Segmented approximations for isolated scalar nonlinearities.

assumptions_latex: The scalar function \(f:[\ell,u]\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
A partition \(\ell=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=u\), with \(m\in\mathbb N\), is fixed.
For every selected knot \(t_j\), a slope \(a_j\in\mathbb R\) is available such that \(f(x)\ge f(t_j)+a_j(x-t_j)\) for every \(x\in[\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On each activated segment, the endpoint secant supplies a valid upper inequality and the selected supporting lines supply valid lower inequalities for an outer relaxation of \(y=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Segmentwise linear graph relaxation for a convex univariate nonlinearity.

source_refs.locator: Linear programming relaxations of quadratically constrained quadratic programs p. 407

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(x\in[t_{k-1},t_k]\), define \[s_k(x):=\frac{t_k-x}{t_k-t_{k-1}}f(t_{k-1})+\frac{x-t_{k-1}}{t_k-t_{k-1}}f(t_k).\] Convexity gives \(f(x)\le s_k(x)\) on that segment. Each selected supporting slope gives \(f(x)\ge f(t_j)+a_j(x-t_j)\) on \([\ell,u]\). Consequently, when segment \(k\) is activated, the inequalities \[f(t_j)+a_j(x-t_j)\le y\quad\text{for every selected }j,\qquad y\le s_k(x)\] form an outer relaxation of \(y=f(x)\) over \([t_{k-1},t_k]\). Segment activation can be represented using SOS2 or binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex scalar function, the endpoint secant on the active interval lies above the graph, while valid supporting lines lie below it. Together with segment activation, these inequalities give a piecewise-linear outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Piecewise-Linear Relaxations

children.title: Multivariate Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Domain partitions for coupled multivariate nonlinear expressions.

assumptions_latex: \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) is bounded and \(f:B\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
For each \(i\), \(\mathcal P_i\) is a finite interval partition of \([\ell_i,u_i]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convexified union is a valid relaxation of \(w=f(x)\) on \(B\). If every child-cell relaxation is contained in its parent-cell relaxation, partition refinement cannot weaken the relaxation.

notation.meaning: Cartesian cells induced by the coordinate partitions
A valid cellwise relaxation of the graph of f

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian multivariate partitioning with arbitrary valid cellwise graph relaxations; refinement monotonicity requires child-to-parent containment.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C=\{C_k:k\in K\}\) be the Cartesian cells generated by \(\mathcal P_1,\ldots,\mathcal P_n\). For every \(k\in K\), let \(R_k\subseteq C_k\times\mathbb R\) contain \(\{(x,f(x)):x\in C_k\}\). The multivariate partition relaxation is \[R(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{k\in K}R_k\right).\] It contains the graph of \(f\) over \(B\). If \(\mathcal C'\) refines \(\mathcal C\) and every child relaxation is contained in the relaxation of its parent cell, then \[R(\mathcal C')\subseteq R(\mathcal C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the variable box into Cartesian cells, relax the nonlinear graph on each cell, and convexify their union. Refinement strengthens or preserves the relaxation when every child relaxation is contained in its parent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Partitioning

children.title: Bilinear Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Domain partitions specialized to bilinear terms.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\), \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and \(w=xy\).
\(\mathcal P_x\) and \(\mathcal P_y\) are finite interval partitions of the two domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convexified union of the bounded cellwise McCormick polytopes is valid for \(w=xy\), and nested refinement produces a nonincreasing sequence of relaxation sets.

notation.meaning: McCormick polytope on a rectangle, including the rectangle bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise McCormick relaxation obtained by partitioning one or both factor domains.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every partition rectangle \(Q_{pq}=[a_p,b_p]\times[c_q,d_q]\), let \(M_{pq}\) be the set of triples \((x,y,w)\) satisfying \((x,y)\in Q_{pq}\) and \[w\ge a_py+c_qx-a_pc_q,\qquad w\ge b_py+d_qx-b_pd_q,\] \[w\le b_py+c_qx-b_pc_q,\qquad w\le a_py+d_qx-a_pd_q.\] Then \(M_{pq}\) contains \(\{(x,y,xy):(x,y)\in Q_{pq}\}\), and \[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{p,q}M_{pq}\right)\] is a valid relaxation over the original box. Under nested partition refinement, every child McCormick polytope is contained in its parent polytope, so the convexified union cannot enlarge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the four McCormick inequalities together with the local variable bounds on every partition rectangle, then convexify the union. Nested refinement strengthens or preserves the bilinear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Partitioning

children.title: Coupled-Term Partition Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of partitions shared across interacting nonlinear terms.

assumptions_latex: A vector \(x\in B\subset\mathbb R^n\) appears in coupled terms \(w_t=f_t(x_{I_t})\), indexed by \(t\in T\).
Every shared variable uses one common finite interval partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordinated cell selectors preserve a common assignment of every shared variable and yield a valid joint relaxation contained in the uncoordinated termwise relaxation.

notation.meaning: Variables occurring in coupled term t
Binary selector for interval r of variable i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for partition selectors shared by several nonlinear terms.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition coordination requires
\[\sum_{r\in R_i}z_{ir}=1\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad z^t_{ir}=z_{ir}\quad(t\in T,\ i\in I_t,\ r\in R_i).\]
Each termwise disjunction is activated using the corresponding \(z^t_{ir}\). Consequently, two terms sharing \(x_i\) cannot select different intervals for that variable. Any point satisfying the original coupled equations admits consistent selectors, while dropping the equalities permits incompatible termwise cells; therefore the coordinated relaxation is valid and is contained in its uncoordinated counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use common interval selectors for variables shared across nonlinear terms. Linking every term-local selector to the common selector prevents incompatible cell choices and strengthens the joint relaxation.
