children.title: Adaptive Partition Refinement
children.top_down_role: Selective refinement of regions dominating the current relaxation gap.

assumptions_latex: A finite partition \(\mathcal C_k\) and valid relaxation \(R_k\) are available at iteration \(k\).
A computable nonnegative cell score \(\Delta_k(C)\) bounds or estimates the relaxation gap contribution of each active cell.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a valid relaxation at every iteration; with nested consistent cell relaxations, its relaxation bound is monotone under refinement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic selective refinement scheme; the score and splitting rule remain implementation dependent.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a finite partition \(\mathcal C_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the relaxation \(R_k\), compute \(\Delta_k(C)\) for active cells, and choose a nonempty set \(S_k\subseteq\{C\in\mathcal C_k:\Delta_k(C)>0\}\), for example cells attaining the largest scores. Replace each \(C\in S_k\) by finitely many children and construct child relaxations contained in the parent relaxation. Stop when the global bound gap is at most \(\varepsilon\), no positive score remains, or a resource limit is reached; output the relaxation bound and any incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the relaxation, score active cells by gap contribution, split selected high-score cells, and stop at the requested gap or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Partition Refinement

children.title: Partition-Growth Boundary
children.top_down_role: Formulation growth and dimensionality limits of partition-based strengthening.

assumptions_latex: Each of \(d\) coordinates is divided into \(m_i\ge1\) intervals.
The formulation explicitly represents every Cartesian cell or every combination of active coordinate intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of cells is \(\prod_{i=1}^d m_i\), which is exponential in \(d\) when \(m_i=m\ge2\) for all \(i\).

notation.meaning: Number of intervals for coordinate i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Cartesian-product counting gives the stated growth exactly
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Cartesian-cell count and the resulting lower bound for formulations with at least one cell-specific object per cell; not a universal lower bound for all extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Cartesian product of the coordinate partitions contains exactly \[N_{\mathrm{cell}}=\prod_{i=1}^d m_i\] cells. If \(m_i=m\ge2\) for every \(i\), then \[N_{\mathrm{cell}}=m^d.\] Consequently, a formulation containing at least one cell-specific object for every Cartesian cell has \[\Omega\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^d m_i\right)\] such objects. This bound does not apply to formulations that avoid explicit cell enumeration by exploiting additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full Cartesian partition has the product of the per-coordinate interval counts. A formulation with at least one object for every cell therefore grows exponentially in the number of jointly partitioned coordinates when each coordinate has the same fixed number of at least two intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Growth Boundary

children.title: Global Linearization Cuts
children.top_down_role: Globally valid linear cuts derived from nonlinear underestimators.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
The epigraph constraint is \(\eta\ge f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\bar x\in C\), the affine inequality \(\eta\ge f(\bar x)+\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) is globally valid on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global epigraph cut for a differentiable convex function.

source_refs.locator: 7.1.1 Linearization cuts p. 84
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every linearization point \(\bar x\in C\), the affine inequality \[\eta\ge f(\bar x)+\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\] is valid for every \((x,\eta)\) satisfying \(x\in C\) and \(\eta\ge f(x)\). This global validity requires convexity of \(f\), unless the affine expression is independently certified as a global underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any point of a differentiable convex function, the tangent affine function yields a globally valid epigraph cut. For a nonconvex function, separate certification of global underestimation is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Linearization Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1.1 Linearization cuts p. 84
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Interval-Gradient Cuts
children.top_down_role: Globally valid cuts derived from interval derivative enclosures.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box, \(\bar x\in B\), and \(f\) is continuously differentiable on \(B\).
For every \(z\in B\), \(\underline g_i\le \partial_i f(z)\le\overline g_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interval-gradient expression is a globally valid lower bound for \(f(x)\) on \(B\).

notation.meaning: Lower derivative bound for coordinate i
Upper derivative bound for coordinate i
Interval-gradient lower estimator based at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boxwise lower estimator derived from componentwise enclosures of the gradient.

source_refs.locator: 7.1.3 Interval-gradient cuts p. 85
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in B\), define \[L_{\bar x}(x)=f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\min\!\left\{\underline g_i(x_i-\bar x_i),\overline g_i(x_i-\bar x_i)\right\}.\] The bound \[f(x)\ge L_{\bar x}(x)\] is valid throughout \(B\). In each summand, the lower derivative endpoint applies when \(x_i\ge\bar x_i\), and the upper derivative endpoint applies when \(x_i\le\bar x_i\). Therefore \[\eta\ge L_{\bar x}(x)\] is a valid piecewise-affine relaxation of the epigraph constraint \(\eta\ge f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise derivative bounds yield a piecewise-affine global underestimator on a box, using the lower or upper derivative endpoint according to the sign of the coordinate displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Gradient Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1.3 Interval-gradient cuts p. 85
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Derivative-Enclosure Validity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interval and regularity regimes governing derivative-based cut validity.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a box and \(f\) is continuously differentiable on an open set containing \(B\).
Finite bounds \(\underline g_i\le \partial_i f(z)\le\overline g_i\) hold for every \(z\in B\) and \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\bar x,x\in B\), the interval-gradient lower estimator is valid. Bounds that do not cover the coordinate paths between \(\bar x\) and \(x\) do not certify this global conclusion.

notation.meaning: Box on which derivative bounds are certified

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient differentiability and enclosure regime for boxwise interval-gradient validity; weaker sufficient regimes may also exist.

source_refs.locator: 7.1.3 Interval-gradient cuts p. 85
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sufficient validity regime is that \(B\) is a box, \(f\) is continuously differentiable on an open set containing \(B\), and \[\partial_i f(z)\in[\underline g_i,\overline g_i]\] for every \(z\in B\) and \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Under these conditions, every \(\bar x,x\in B\) satisfies \[f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\min\!\left\{\underline g_i(x_i-\bar x_i),\overline g_i(x_i-\bar x_i)\right\}.\] Derivative bounds certified only on a subset that does not cover the coordinate paths between \(\bar x\) and \(x\) do not certify this global inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval-gradient cuts are valid under continuous differentiability when finite componentwise derivative enclosures cover the full box. Bounds that fail to cover the coordinate paths between the reference and evaluation points do not certify global validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Enclosure Validity Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1.3 Interval-gradient cuts p. 85
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Dual-Level-Contour Cut Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from dual bounds, objective levels, and nonlinear contours.

children.title: Lagrangian Cuts
children.top_down_role: Globally valid cuts derived from Lagrangian bounds or multipliers.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^m\).
The feasible epigraph points satisfy \(x\in X\), \(g(x)\le0\), and \(\eta\ge f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\ge0\) with finite \(L(\lambda)\), the inequality \(\eta+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\ge L(\lambda)\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on the Lagrangian subproblem value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-epigraph validity certificate obtained from a finite Lagrangian subproblem value.

source_refs.locator: 7.1.4 Lagrangian cuts p. 86
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \[L(\lambda)=\inf_{y\in X}\left\{f(y)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(y)\right\}.\] If \(L(\lambda)>-\infty\), then the Lagrangian cut \[\eta+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\ge L(\lambda)\] is valid for every feasible epigraph point \((x,\eta)\). More generally, any certified value \(\underline L(\lambda)\le L(\lambda)\) may replace \(L(\lambda)\) while preserving validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier and a finite Lagrangian subproblem value give an inequality valid for every feasible objective-epigraph point. A certified lower bound on that subproblem value also gives a valid, possibly weaker, cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1.4 Lagrangian cuts p. 86
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Level Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts associated with objective or feasibility level sets.

assumptions_latex: \(S_\alpha=\{x\in D:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A point \(\hat x\in D\setminus S_\alpha\) is to be separated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any separating inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) valid for \(S_\alpha\) and violated by \(\hat x\) is a level cut at level \(\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Normal and right-hand side of the cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation-based sense of a cut valid for a convex sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a prescribed \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), let \(S_\alpha=\{x\in D:f(x)\le\alpha\}\). A level cut separating \(\hat x\notin S_\alpha\) is an affine inequality
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\]
such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in S_\alpha\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}\hat x>\beta\). Closed convexity of \(S_\alpha\) ensures existence of such a strict separator for every exterior point. The cut certifies exclusion from the selected sublevel set, not necessarily infeasibility for the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level cut is an affine separator valid for a chosen convex sublevel set and violated by the current point outside that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Level Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separation statement is mathematically coherent, but no source is supplied for the field-specific use of 'level cut' in this taxonomy. Because that term has method-dependent meanings, the exact definition cannot be accepted without a specific locator.

children.title: Contour Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from nonlinear contour geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and quasiconvex on an open convex set \(D\).
\(\bar x\in D\), and the target region is \(S=\{x\in D:f(x)\le f(\bar x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le0\) is valid for the lower contour set \(S\).

notation.meaning: Lower contour set through the reference point
Gradient normal at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient halfspace valid for a differentiable quasiconvex lower contour set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Quasiconvexity makes every lower contour set convex. For \(S=\{x\in D:f(x)\le f(\bar x)\}\), differentiability implies
\[\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le0\qquad(x\in S).\]
Accordingly, the displayed halfspace is a contour cut supporting the lower contour through \(\bar x\). If \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\), the inequality is vacuous; if quasiconvexity is absent, the gradient halfspace need not contain the entire lower contour set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a differentiable quasiconvex contour point, the gradient defines a halfspace containing the entire lower contour set; a zero gradient gives no separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Contour Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gradient halfspace property is a standard differentiable-quasiconvex characterization, but no source is supplied for calling this inequality a 'contour cut' in the intended MINLP taxonomy. A specific source locator is required to resolve the terminology.

children.title: Convex-Free-Region Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Cuts obtained from disjunctions and nonlinear-free convex regions.

children.title: Nonconvex Disjunctive Cuts
children.top_down_role: Globally valid cuts derived from nonconvex disjunctions.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K D_k\), where the branch sets \(D_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) need not be convex.
The inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is valid on every branch set \(F\cap D_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality is valid for \(F\) and for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K(F\cap D_k))\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the disjunctive feasible union
Relaxation point separated by the cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise validity certificate for a cut derived from a finite disjunction whose branch sets may be nonconvex.

source_refs.locator: Disjunctive cuts for nonconvex MINLP p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[H=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K(F\cap D_k)\right).\] If \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) holds for every \(x\in F\cap D_k\) and every \(k=1,\ldots,K\), then the inequality is valid for both \(H\) and \(F\). If a relaxation point \(\hat x\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\hat x>\beta\), the inequality is a nonconvex disjunctive cut separating \(\hat x\) without excluding a point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality valid on every branch of a finite disjunction is valid for the feasible set and the convex hull of the feasible branch union. If a relaxation point violates it, the inequality is a nonconvex disjunctive cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Disjunctive Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: Disjunctive cuts for nonconvex MINLP p. 117

children.title: Nonconvex Intersection Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from intersections with nonlinear-free convex regions.

assumptions_latex: \(R=\{\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^m r_j\lambda_j:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\}\) is a simplicial relaxation cone.
\(F\subseteq R\) contains \(\bar x\), its interior contains no feasible point, and every segment \(\{\bar x+t r_j:0\le t<\tau_j\}\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}F\), where \(0<\tau_j\le+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_{j:\tau_j<+\infty}\frac{\lambda_j}{\tau_j}\ge 1\]

notation.meaning: Apex and extreme-ray directions of the relaxation cone.
First certified exit distance from the feasible-free region along ray j.
Nonnegative ray coordinates of a point in the cone.

review_flags: Exact literature source for the star-shaped nonconvex extension is missing.
Clarify whether the local taxonomy uses a stronger definition of nonconvex intersection cut.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ray intersection cut for a possibly nonconvex but apex-star-shaped feasible-free region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^m r_j\lambda_j\in R\). If \(x\) violates the displayed inequality, then \(s=\sum_{j:\tau_j<+\infty}\lambda_j/\tau_j<1\). For every finite \(\tau_j\), the corresponding ray contribution remains before its certified exit from \(F\); the stated radial-segment hypothesis therefore places \(x\) in \(\operatorname{int}F\). Since that interior is feasible-free, every feasible point of \(R\) satisfies the intersection inequality. Convexity of \(F\) is not required, but the certified radial containment is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified exit distances along the cone rays yield a valid intersection inequality even when the feasible-free region is nonconvex, provided its relevant radial segments remain inside.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Intersection Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Containment of each individual ray segment in F does not imply that a point formed from a combination of ray directions lies in F when F is nonconvex. The validity argument therefore fails under the stated hypotheses, and statement_latex improperly contains proof text. A sourced nonconvex intersection-cut theorem with an adequate radial-gauge or star-shaped containment hypothesis is required.

children.title: Convex-Free-Region Construction
children.top_down_role: Geometric regions supporting nonconvex intersection-cut generation.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the current relaxation domain and \(S\subseteq X\) is the feasible set.
\(\bar x\in X\setminus S\) is the relaxation point to be separated.
For each direction \(r_j\), infeasibility is certified on \(\{\bar x+t r_j:0\le t<\tau_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{int}F\cap S=\varnothing\) and each certified radial segment is contained in \(F\).

notation.meaning: Current feasible set within the relaxation domain.
Infeasible relaxation point used as the construction center.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this construction.
The intended meaning of convex-free region requires source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radial construction sufficient for subsequent intersection-cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X,S,\bar x\) and directions \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\). For each \(j\), use a valid infeasibility certificate to choose the largest available certified distance \(\tau_j>0\) such that \(\bar x+t r_j\notin S\) for every \(0\le t<\tau_j\). Form a region \(F\subseteq X\) containing all these radial segments, but include a point only when the same certificates establish that it lies outside \(S\). Stop when no certificate enlarges \(F\), and output \(F\) together with the distances \(\tau_j\). The required invariant is \(\operatorname{int}F\cap S=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an infeasible relaxation point, extend certified infeasible segments along selected rays and combine only regions whose interiors are proved feasible-free.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Free-Region Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the proposed construction or the intended meaning of a convex-free region. Terms such as “largest available certified distance,” certificate-based inclusion, and the stopping rule are not mathematically specified well enough to identify a reproducible algorithm.

children.title: Global Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cut families used to exclude regions inconsistent with global optimality criteria.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8, Local and Global Optimality Criteria
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in S\}\), and an incumbent supplies \(U=f(\hat x)\) with \(\hat x\in S\).
A function \(\ell:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\cap X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)\le U\) is valid for every feasible point capable of improving the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Feasible set and current relaxation domain.
Valid lower estimator of the objective on feasible points.

review_flags: The supplied source inventory has no precise locator for this cut family.
Local usage may include additional globally valid optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-underestimator cuts for a minimization problem with a known incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every improving feasible point satisfies \(f(x)<U\). Because \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) on \(S\cap X\), it also satisfies \(\ell(x)<U\), and the closed inequality \(\ell(x)\le U\) is valid for retaining all points no worse than the incumbent. Thus the region \(\{x\in X:\ell(x)>U\}\) may be excluded. If \(\ell\) is affine or convex-representable, this condition can be installed directly as a relaxation cut; otherwise it remains a globally valid nonlinear cutoff condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid objective underestimator may be bounded by the incumbent value, excluding every region whose certified objective lower bound already exceeds that value.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimality Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The underestimator cutoff is mathematically plausible, but no cited source establishes it as the intended Global Optimality Cuts family. A precise source must also clarify when the generally nonlinear condition is properly classified as a cut.

children.title: Nonlinear Domain-Reduction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Preprocessing and in-tree mechanisms that tighten nonlinear variable domains and simplify expression structure.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Nonlinear Propagation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction propagated through nonlinear constraints and expression graphs.

children.title: Interval Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using interval evaluations of nonlinear expressions.

assumptions_latex: Each variable initially has an interval \(X_i=[l_i,u_i]\).
Every expression operator has an inclusion-monotone interval extension.
All interval operations use outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, every feasible point in the original box belongs to the contracted box, or an empty interval certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Interval extension of an expression f.

review_flags: A precise interval-analysis source locator is not supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound interval evaluation and contraction with outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a box \(X=\prod_iX_i\) and expression constraints. Evaluate every expression by its interval extension. For a relation \(f(x)\in T\), replace its range by \([f](X)\cap T\), then apply sound inverse interval operators to intersect the operand intervals with preimages of that range. Repeat affected evaluations until no endpoint changes, a prescribed tolerance is reached, or some interval becomes empty. Output the final box. Inclusion monotonicity and outward rounding ensure that no feasible point from the input box is removed; an empty interval therefore certifies box infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate constraints over variable intervals, intersect their ranges with required values, propagate inverse interval restrictions, and repeat until stable or infeasibility is detected.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm describes standard interval propagation, but no inspectable citation is supplied. Soundness also depends on precisely defined solution-preserving inverse interval contractors, not merely inclusion-monotone forward extensions.

children.title: Feasibility-Based Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using constraint-feasibility implications.

assumptions_latex: \(S=\{x\in X:g_k(x)\in T_k,\ k=1,\ldots,q\}\) is the local feasible set.
Each contractor \(C_k\) is contracting and solution-preserving: \(S_k\cap B\subseteq C_k(B)\subseteq B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\cap X\subseteq X^{\star}\subseteq X\), where \(X^{\star}\) is the propagated box.
review_flags: A source distinguishing this method from general interval propagation is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-wise fixed-point propagation by solution-preserving contractors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B\leftarrow X\) and place all constraints in a queue. Remove an index \(k\), compute \(B'\leftarrow C_k(B)\), and set \(B\leftarrow B'\). If an interval changed, requeue every constraint sharing an affected variable. Stop when the queue is empty, contraction falls below tolerance, or an interval is empty. Return \(B\), or declare the input box infeasible in the empty case. Since every update contains \(S_k\cap B\), their composition preserves every point satisfying all constraints while monotonically contracting the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply solution-preserving constraint contractors and revisit neighboring constraints whenever a bound changes, reaching a fixed point or proving box infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Based Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contractor-queue scheme is plausible and its invariant is stated, but no source distinguishes this leaf from general interval or expression-graph propagation or supports the exact algorithmic formulation.

children.title: Expression-Graph Contraction
children.top_down_role: Propagation of tightened domains through nonlinear expression graphs.

assumptions_latex: The nonlinear system is represented by a directed acyclic expression graph.
Every node operator has sound forward and inverse interval extensions.
Leaf nodes carry the current variable intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned leaf intervals contain every assignment satisfying the root constraints within the original box.

notation.meaning: Interval attached to expression-graph node v.

review_flags: A precise expression-graph contractor source locator is absent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward contraction on an acyclic factorable expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize leaf intervals from the variable box. In topological order, assign each internal node \(v\) the interval \(I_v\leftarrow[\phi_v]((I_w)_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)})\). Intersect each constrained root interval with its permitted range. In reverse topological order, apply sound inverse extensions of \(\phi_v\) to contract its children, intersecting shared-node intervals whenever multiple parents contribute. Repeat forward and backward sweeps until stable, tolerance-limited, or empty. Return the contracted leaf intervals; emptiness certifies infeasibility of the original box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate intervals forward through an expression graph, intersect constrained outputs, and propagate inverse restrictions backward until the variable intervals stabilize or become empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Contraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward-backward contractor description is plausible, but no precise source is cited. A source is needed for the inverse operators and for correct treatment of repeated variables or shared graph nodes.

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary optimization models used to contract nonlinear variable domains.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq X=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i,u_i]\) is the feasible set in the current node.
Each auxiliary optimization problem is solved globally or replaced by a certified valid bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n[L_i,U_i]\subseteq X\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper bounds for variable i.

review_flags: The supplied locator inventory does not identify an OBBT section.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or certified optimization-based tightening over the current feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every selected variable \(i\), solve or validly bound the auxiliary problems \(L_i=\inf\{x_i:x\in S\}\) and \(U_i=\sup\{x_i:x\in S\}\). Replace \([l_i,u_i]\) by \([l_i,u_i]\cap[L_i,U_i]\), using conservative certified bounds when an auxiliary solve is incomplete. Optionally rebuild the auxiliary models and repeat after material contractions. Stop at a fixed point, a resource limit, or an empty interval. The output box contains \(S\); emptiness from certified auxiliary bounds proves local infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize and maximize selected variables over the current feasible region, then intersect their domains with the resulting certified bounds and repeat as useful.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is recognizably an OBBT algorithm, but it has no supporting locator. The source must specify which conservative bound directions are safe for incomplete minimization and maximization solves and support the infeasibility claim.

children.title: Objective-Guided Domain Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using relaxation dual information and objective cutoffs.

children.title: Dual-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using relaxation multipliers or reduced-cost information.

assumptions_latex: A minimization relaxation has certified lower bound \(L\) and a feasible incumbent value \(U\ge L\).
Variable \(x_j\) is at its lower bound \(l_j\) in an optimal LP relaxation solution and has reduced cost \(\bar c_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\le l_j+(U-L)/\bar c_j\) for every relaxation-feasible point with objective at most \(U\).

notation.meaning: Certified relaxation lower bound and incumbent upper bound.
Positive reduced cost of variable j at its lower bound.

review_flags: The formula requires a source locator for the exact LP reduced-cost convention.
Extension to nonlinear Lagrangian dual bounds is not stated.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP reduced-cost tightening under an incumbent objective cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any relaxation-feasible point, the dual reduced-cost bound implies that increasing \(x_j\) from \(l_j\) by \(d\ge0\) raises the certified objective lower bound by at least \(\bar c_jd\). A point capable of matching the incumbent must therefore satisfy \(L+\bar c_j(x_j-l_j)\le U\). Hence its domain may be intersected with \(( -\infty,l_j+(U-L)/\bar c_j]\). If \(U=L\), the variable is fixed at \(l_j\). The symmetric statement applies to a variable at its upper bound with the corresponding reduced-cost sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive reduced cost limits how far a lower-bound variable can move before its certified objective contribution exceeds the incumbent gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Based Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost formula requires an optimal dual solution whose objective value and reduced cost are jointly associated with the same LP relaxation. Merely assuming an arbitrary certified lower bound L and a reduced cost at an optimal solution is insufficient. A source and corrected dual-consistency hypotheses are required.

children.title: Incumbent-Based Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction using incumbent objective values.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in S\cap X\}\).
A feasible incumbent \(\hat x\) gives \(U=f(\hat x)\).
Auxiliary bounds are certified over \(S_U=\{x\in S\cap X:f(x)\le U\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_U\subseteq\prod_i[L_i^U,U_i^U]\), so the tightened box preserves every point no worse than the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Feasible points no worse than the incumbent.

review_flags: No precise source locator for incumbent-restricted OBBT is supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OBBT restricted to points capable of matching the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Add the valid objective cutoff \(f(x)\le U\) to the current feasible-region description. For each selected variable \(i\), compute certified bounds \(L_i^U=\inf\{x_i:x\in S_U\}\) and \(U_i^U=\sup\{x_i:x\in S_U\}\), then intersect its domain with \([L_i^U,U_i^U]\). Repeat after substantial contractions or incumbent improvements. Stop at a fixed point or resource limit. If \(S_U\) is certified empty, the current node contains no solution capable of matching the incumbent and may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add the incumbent objective cutoff, optimize variable bounds over the remaining competitive points, and prune the node if that restricted set is empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Based Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incumbent-restricted auxiliary optimization scheme is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports its formulation or establishes that it is the intended meaning of Incumbent-Based Tightening rather than objective-cutoff OBBT.

children.title: Objective-Cutoff Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation of objective cutoff information through nonlinear structure.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with feasible incumbent value \(U\).
The objective is represented by a factorable expression graph with sound interval contractors.
Only solutions satisfying \(f(x)\le U\) need be retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated box contains every feasible point whose objective is at most \(U\).
review_flags: A source specifically treating objective-cutoff propagation is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward interval propagation from an incumbent objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate the objective graph over \(X\) to obtain its root interval \(I_f\). Replace that interval by \(I_f\cap(-\infty,U]\), and apply sound inverse contractors backward through the objective graph to contract intermediate and variable intervals. Propagate changed variable bounds through all constraints and repeat until stable, tolerance-limited, or empty. Output the contracted box. If the root intersection or any descendant interval is empty, then every point in the input box has certified objective greater than \(U\), so the node may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the objective range with the incumbent cutoff and propagate that restriction backward through the objective expression and the remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Cutoff Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The propagation algorithm is plausible but unsupported by a specific source. The source should also resolve whether points equal to the incumbent are retained and when emptiness justifies pruning under the solver's strict-improvement convention.

children.title: Nonlinear Structure Presolve
children.top_down_role: Presolve mechanisms exposing simpler, tighter, or convex nonlinear representations.

children.title: Nonlinear Expression Simplification
children.top_down_role: Presolve transformations that reduce nonlinear expression complexity.

assumptions_latex: An expression \(e(x)\) is considered only on a current domain \(X\).
Every rewrite \(e\mapsto\tilde e\) is certified to preserve values or the relevant constraint relation on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in X:e(x)\in T\}=\{x\in X:\tilde e(x)\in T\}\) for every rewritten constraint range \(T\).

notation.meaning: Permitted range in the associated constraint.

review_flags: No supplied source locator states domain-qualified nonlinear rewrite rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-aware, feasibility-preserving simplification of nonlinear expression graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid nonlinear simplification replaces \(e\) by \(\tilde e\) only after establishing equivalence on \(X\), including all domain conditions of division, roots, logarithms, powers, and inverse functions. Constant folding, elimination of neutral elements, common-subexpression reuse, and algebraic cancellation are admissible under this invariant. For example, replacing \(x/x\) by \(1\) requires \(0\notin X_x\). The simplified model must preserve the feasible set on \(X\); preserving merely a formal identity outside the operators' domains is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplify nonlinear expressions only with domain-aware rewrites that preserve the represented constraint set, including exceptional points of division and nonlinear functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Expression Simplification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The domain-qualified equivalence invariant is sound, but the record supplies no source for the claimed nonlinear presolve rules or their exact exceptional-domain conditions.

children.title: Convexity-Structure Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of convex subexpressions, constraints, or reformulations during presolve.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and convex.
\(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is convex on \(D\) if and only if \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in D\).

notation.meaning: Hessian matrix of f at x.

review_flags: A standard convex-analysis theorem locator is not present in the supplied inventory.
Operational composition-rule detection is only summarized, not fully axiomatized.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable Hessian test, supplemented by sound expression composition rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stated smooth finite-dimensional setting, convexity is exactly characterized by positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian throughout \(D\). A presolver may certify this condition directly, by interval bounds proving \(d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)d\ge0\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), or indirectly through valid curvature composition rules on certified argument ranges. Failure of these sufficient computational tests means that curvature is unknown; it does not by itself certify nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A twice continuously differentiable function on an open convex domain is convex exactly when its Hessian is positive semidefinite everywhere on that domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity-Structure Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The smooth Hessian characterization is standard and precisely scoped, but no authoritative theorem locator is cited. The additional claims about interval-Hessian and composition-rule detection likewise need a specific source.

children.title: Presolve Reformulation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity and effectiveness limits of nonlinear presolve transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Reformulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact presolve reformulations and transformations that can alter feasibility or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve reformulation is exact when \(R(\widehat F)=F\) and \(\widehat f(y)=f(R(y))\) for every \(y\in\widehat F\). Variable elimination, expression replacement, or constraint deletion lies within this boundary only when these conditions follow from identities valid on the current domains. Exactness implies \[\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{y\in\widehat F}\widehat f(y).\] Moreover, every optimizer \(y^*\) of the presolved problem recovers to an optimizer \(R(y^*)\) of the original problem. In a common variable space with the same objective, a transformed feasible set \(G\supsetneq F\) defines a relaxation, not an exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact presolve formulation maps onto the original feasible set and preserves objective values. A genuine enlargement of a common feasible region is a relaxation rather than an equivalent reformulation.
assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(F\subseteq X\), with objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
The presolved formulation has feasible set \(\widehat F\subseteq\widehat X\), objective \(\widehat f:\widehat X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and recovery map \(R:\widehat F\to X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under exactness, \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{y\in\widehat F}\widehat f(y)\), and every attained presolved optimum recovers to an original optimum.

notation.meaning: Recovery map from presolved variables to the original variable space
Transformed feasible set in a common variable space

children.title: Unsafe or Ineffective Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by invalid bounds, tolerances, or weak propagation.

assumptions_latex: A sound propagation operator must return a box \(B'\) satisfying \(F\cap B\subseteq B'\subseteq B\).
Floating-point outward rounding is required when computed interval endpoints are used as rigorous bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invalid exclusion occurs when \(F\cap B\nsubseteq B'\); ineffective reduction occurs when \(B'=B\) despite a strictly tighter sound box being derivable.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the nonlinear model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes loss of valid solutions from merely weak nonlinear propagation.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current box \(B\), domain reduction is sound precisely when \(F\cap B\subseteq B'\). It is unsafe if an invalid input bound, inward-rounded interval endpoint, or feasibility tolerance produces some \(x\in F\cap B\) with \(x\notin B'\). For example, replacing the rigorous implication \(x^2\le 2\Rightarrow x\le\sqrt 2\) by \(x\le 1.414\) excludes feasible points. A sound step is ineffective when \(B'=B\), although another available propagation or optimization step can derive a strict box \(B''\) satisfying \(F\cap B\subseteq B''\subsetneq B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduction is unsafe if it removes a feasible point. It is ineffective if it leaves the box unchanged although a sound tighter box is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe or Ineffective Domain Reduction

children.title: Quadratic Relaxation-Bound Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Comparison and routing of lower bounds used in mixed-integer quadratic search.

children.title: Quadratic-Conic Bound Pair
children.top_down_role: Bounds retaining convex quadratic, quadratically constrained, or conic structure.

children.title: Continuous Quadratic Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds retaining convex quadratic objective or constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Quadratic Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous QCQP relaxation bound for a mixed-integer quadratic or quadratically constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x+a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\), and let \(X_Q\) be a continuous domain obtained by relaxing the required integer restrictions. Define \[R_Q:=\{x\in X_Q:q_i(x)\le 0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}\] and \[L_Q:=\inf_{x\in R_Q}q_0(x).\] If \(F\subseteq R_Q\), then \(L_Q\le\inf_{x\in F}q_0(x)\). When \(X_Q\) is convex and the symmetric matrices \(Q_i\) are positive semidefinite for \(i=0,\ldots,m\), this relaxation is a convex QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous quadratic bound is the optimum of a quadratic relaxation obtained by relaxing integrality while retaining selected quadratic constraints. It is a valid lower bound, and it is a convex QCQP when both its objective and constraints are convex.
assumptions_latex: The original problem minimizes \(q_0\) over a feasible set \(F\).
The continuous relaxation set \(R_Q\) contains \(F\).
The functions \(q_i\) are indexed by \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(L_Q=\inf_{x\in R_Q}q_0(x)\) satisfies \(L_Q\le\inf_{x\in F}q_0(x)\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic objective or constraint function indexed by i
Continuous variable domain after relaxing integrality

children.title: Continuous Conic Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds retaining native conic structure.

assumptions_latex: The original minimization feasible set \(F\) maps into a conic relaxation \(R_K\).
The cone \(K\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conic value \(L_K=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}z:Az=b,\ z\in K\}\) is a lower bound on the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous SOCP or SDP bound obtained from an exact conic representation or a conic relaxation.

source_refs.locator: Part VI. Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Optimization
5.1 Semidefinite and Lagrangian relaxations p. 55
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous conic bound is the value \[L_K:=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}z:Az=b,\ z\in K\},\] where \(K\) is a closed convex cone and every original feasible point \(x\in F\) admits a lifted vector \(z(x)\in R_K:=\{z:Az=b,\ z\in K\}\) with \(c^{\mathsf T}z(x)\le f(x)\). Second-order, rotated second-order, and positive-semidefinite cones yield common instances. The embedding condition implies \(L_K\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\); equality with a continuous quadratic bound requires an exact, objective-preserving conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic bound minimizes a linear lifted objective over a convex cone containing images of all feasible points, thereby furnishing a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Conic Bounds

children.title: Quadratic-to-Conic Routing
children.top_down_role: Selection between quadratic and conic relaxation representations.

assumptions_latex: A continuous quadratic relaxation and candidate conic representations are available.
Each accepted reformulation has a verified feasible-point embedding and objective correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The routed formulation returns a valid lower bound; it preserves the quadratic bound exactly when the selected conic representation is exact.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural routing between direct convex QCQP solution and equivalent or relaxed conic formulations.

source_refs.locator: Part VI. Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a continuous quadratic relaxation \(R_Q\). For each convex quadratic inequality, test whether it has an objective-preserving second-order-cone representation; route such constraints to SOCP form. If quadratic terms require a matrix lift, route them to an SDP relaxation. Retain direct QCQP form when it is convex and no supported conic form improves solution access. Reject any route lacking a verified embedding of every point of \(R_Q\). Solve the selected relaxation \(R_K\), output \(L:=\inf_{z\in R_K}c^{\mathsf T}z\), and record whether the route is exact or relaxation-producing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Route convex quadratic constraints to exact SOCP form when possible, use SDP lifts when needed, and retain direct QCQP form otherwise; report whether strength is preserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-Conic Routing

children.title: MILP-Compatible Bound Family
children.top_down_role: MILP-compatible bounds obtained from quadratic linearization and lifting.

children.title: Linearized Quadratic Bounds
children.top_down_role: Linear lower bounds obtained through direct quadratic linearization.

assumptions_latex: Variables satisfy finite bounds \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\).
Every quadratic product is replaced by an auxiliary variable and valid linear envelopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting MILP relaxation has value \(L_{\mathrm{lin}}\le v^*\), where \(v^*\) is the original minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MILP-compatible McCormick linearization of bounded bilinear terms in a quadratic relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each product \(x_i x_j\), introduce \(w_{ij}\) and replace the product by \(w_{ij}\). Over \([l_i,u_i]\times[l_j,u_j]\), impose the four McCormick inequalities \[w_{ij}\ge l_i x_j+l_j x_i-l_i l_j,\quad w_{ij}\ge u_i x_j+u_j x_i-u_i u_j,\] \[w_{ij}\le u_i x_j+l_j x_i-u_i l_j,\quad w_{ij}\le l_i x_j+u_j x_i-l_i u_j.\] Substitution in every quadratic expression produces an MILP-compatible relaxation, whose minimization value \(L_{\mathrm{lin}}\) satisfies \(L_{\mathrm{lin}}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace bounded bilinear products by auxiliary variables and their McCormick envelopes. The resulting linear mixed-integer model supplies a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Quadratic Bounds

children.title: Lifted Linear Bounds
children.top_down_role: Linear lower bounds using auxiliary-variable lifted representations.

assumptions_latex: The original variables lie in a bounded polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ l\le x\le u\}\).
The lifted variables satisfy \(W_{ij}=x_i x_j\) at every original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing over any linear relaxation containing all pairs \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) yields a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear matrix-product lifting with valid linear relations derived from bounded base constraints.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce a symmetric matrix \(W\) intended to satisfy \(W=xx^{\mathsf T}\), so each quadratic form becomes linear: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\langle Q,W\rangle\). Construct a polyhedron \(R_L\) in \((x,W)\)-space using product envelopes and linear consequences obtained by multiplying valid bounded constraints by nonnegative bound factors and then replacing products by entries of \(W\). If \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\in R_L\) for every \(x\in P\), then minimizing the lifted linear objective over \(R_L\) gives a lower bound on the original quadratic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift products into a matrix and impose valid linear product relations. Any lifted polyhedron containing all exact product points yields a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Linear Bounds

children.title: MILP-Compatible Bound Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening mechanisms preserving compatibility with linear mixed-integer solvers.

assumptions_latex: Two MILP-compatible relaxations satisfy \(R_2\subseteq R_1\).
Both relaxations contain every lifted image of an original feasible point and use the same lifted objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Their minimization bounds satisfy \(L_1\le L_2\le v^*\).

notation.meaning: Weaker and strengthened MILP relaxation sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone strengthening by valid linear inequalities in a common lifted MILP space.

source_refs.locator: 9.4 Using Lift-and-Project to Choose the Best Mixed Integer Gomory Cut p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\) be a valid lifted MILP relaxation and let \(R_2=R_1\cap\{z:Dz\le d\}\), where every exact lifted feasible point satisfies \(Dz\le d\). With common linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}z\), define \(L_k:=\inf_{z\in R_k}c^{\mathsf T}z\). Since \(R_2\subseteq R_1\) and both sets contain the exact lifted feasible set, \[L_1\le L_2\le v^*.\] Thus valid RLT relations, disjunctive cuts, or tighter product envelopes cannot weaken a minimization bound, although they may leave it unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid linear inequalities to a lifted MILP relaxation can only raise its minimization lower bound, though the improvement may be zero.
knowledge_statements.title: MILP-Compatible Bound Strengthening

children.title: Semidefinite Bounds
children.top_down_role: Matrix-lifted lower bounds for mixed-integer quadratic models.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic problem is a minimization problem with bounded continuous relaxation.
Quadratic products are lifted to \(X\), and the rank-one identity is relaxed by a positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Shor relaxation value \(L_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) satisfies \(L_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order Shor matrix lift for a continuous quadratic relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Semidefinite and Lagrangian relaxations p. 55
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For quadratic functions \(q_i(x)=\langle Q_i,xx^{\mathsf T}\rangle+a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\), replace \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \(X\) and impose \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\] together with the lifted linear quadratic constraints \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\le0\) and any valid linear side constraints. The semidefinite bound \(L_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) is the minimum of \(\langle Q_0,X\rangle+a_0^{\mathsf T}x-b_0\) over this set. Every feasible \(x\) lifts with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), hence \(L_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Shor bound replaces the rank-one product matrix by a positive-semidefinite lift. Every original feasible point remains representable, so the optimum is a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Bounds

children.title: Lagrangian Quadratic Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quadratic lower bounds obtained through constraint dualization.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(v^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ x\in X\}\).
Multipliers for inequality constraints satisfy \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian quadratic bound \(L_{\mathrm{Lag}}=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(q_0(x)+\sum_i\lambda_iq_i(x)\bigr)\) satisfies \(L_{\mathrm{Lag}}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical inequality-constraint Lagrangian dual bound for quadratic minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Continuous bound versus Lagrangian bound p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda):=q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\), and the dual function \(\theta(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}\mathcal L(x,\lambda)\). The Lagrangian quadratic bound is \[L_{\mathrm{Lag}}:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}\theta(\lambda).\] For every primal-feasible \(x\) and every \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)\le q_0(x)\); consequently weak duality gives \(L_{\mathrm{Lag}}\le v^*\). Equality requires additional strong-duality hypotheses and is not part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualize quadratic inequalities with nonnegative multipliers, minimize the Lagrangian over the base domain, and maximize the result. Weak duality makes this a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Quadratic Bounds

children.title: Matrix-Lift versus Dualization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Strength, scalability, and reuse tradeoffs between the two bound families.

assumptions_latex: A matrix-lift relaxation and a Lagrangian dual bound are constructed from the same quadratic primal model.
Both constructions are closed and attain finite optimal values when an equality claim is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No unconditional dominance follows from the construction names alone; equality or dominance requires a model-specific dual correspondence or feasible-set containment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical strength comparison, separated from representation size and numerical solution cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix lift exposes products through a variable of order \(n^2\) and enforces global consistency by positive semidefiniteness; Lagrangian dualization instead optimizes multipliers and repeatedly evaluates an inner quadratic infimum. If conic dualization of the chosen SDP produces exactly the chosen Lagrangian dual, closedness and strong conic duality imply \(L_{\mathrm{SDP}}=L_{\mathrm{Lag}}\). Without that correspondence, neither equality nor a universal ordering is valid. Bound dominance must be established from an explicit dual derivation or containment, while computational preference depends separately on matrix dimension, sparsity, multiplier dimension, and inner-solve difficulty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix lifting and Lagrangian dualization may yield equal bounds under exact conic duality, but neither universally dominates; computational preference depends on size, sparsity, and inner solves.

children.title: Bound Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural strength relations among alternative relaxation bounds.

assumptions_latex: All compared formulations relax the same minimization problem and use objective-preserving embeddings.
Each bound is the infimum of the corresponding relaxation objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_2\subseteq R_1\) in a common representation, then \(L(R_2)\ge L(R_1)\); strict containment alone need not imply strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial order of minimization bounds induced by relaxation containment or pointwise dual-function comparison.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid relaxation \(R\), let \(L(R):=\inf_{z\in R}\widehat f(z)\), with \(L(R)\le v^*\). Bound \(L(R_2)\) dominates \(L(R_1)\) when \(L(R_2)\ge L(R_1)\) for every instance in the specified class. A sufficient condition is an objective-preserving common representation with \(R_2\subseteq R_1\), which gives \[L(R_1)\le L(R_2)\le v^*.\] Strict containment does not guarantee a strictly stronger bound because the removed region may contain no optimizer. Absent containment or a valid dual comparison, dominance cannot be inferred from formulation labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a contained relaxation gives at least as large a lower bound. Strict containment may tie, and formulation names alone establish no dominance.

children.title: Computational Cost Profiles
children.top_down_role: Solution effort, memory demand, and reuse characteristics of bound families.

knowledge_statements.title: Computational Cost Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource profile for comparing finite families of valid MINLP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation family \(\{R_k:k\in K\}\), dimension parameter \(n\), and solver tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define its computational cost profile by \[\mathcal C_k(n,\varepsilon)=\bigl(T_k(n,\varepsilon),M_k(n,\varepsilon),N_k(n,\varepsilon)\bigr),\] where \(T_k\) is elapsed work or time, \(M_k\) is peak memory, and \(N_k\) is the number of relaxation-oracle calls required to return a certified lower bound within tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Profiles are comparable only under the same instance class, computational model, stopping rule, and implementation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation's cost profile records time, memory, and oracle calls under a common instance class, solver model, and accuracy convention.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite relaxation index set.
All profiles use the same accuracy and computational conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_k=(T_k,M_k,N_k)\) provides a common resource representation.

children.title: Strength–Cost Routing
children.top_down_role: Model and search regimes favoring particular strength-to-cost balances.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Cost Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects a relaxation by balancing certified bound adequacy against predicted solution cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite set \(K\), certified lower bounds \(L_k\), predicted costs \(C_k\), incumbent value \(U\), and permitted absolute gap \(\tau\ge0\). Initialize \(S=\{k\in K:U-L_k\le\tau\}\). If \(S\ne\varnothing\), choose \[k^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in S}C_k.\] If \(S=\varnothing\), choose lexicographically by maximizing \(L_k\) and then minimizing \(C_k\). Solve the selected relaxation to its prescribed tolerance and output its certified lower bound; update the cost predictions after observing the solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the cheapest relaxation meeting the required bound gap; if none qualifies, choose the strongest bound and break ties by cost.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\le z^\star\le U\) for every \(k\in K\).
\(C_k\ge0\) uses a common resource metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \(k^\star\) satisfies the stated strength-first cost-routing rule.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound from relaxation k

children.title: LP Relaxation Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: LP Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound obtained from a polyhedral outer approximation and affine objective underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^\star=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F\) may contain integrality and nonlinear restrictions. An LP relaxation bound is \[L_{\mathrm{LP}}=\inf\{\ell(x):x\in P\},\] where \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedron satisfying \(F\subseteq P\), and \(\ell\) is affine with \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Consequently, \(L_{\mathrm{LP}}\le z^\star\), including when either value is attained only as an infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing an affine objective underestimator over a polyhedron containing every original feasible point yields an LP lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{LP}}\le z^\star\).

children.title: Convex NLP Relaxation Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Convex NLP Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous convex relaxation bound for a minimization-form MINLP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^\star=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). A convex NLP relaxation consists of a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and a convex function \(\phi:C\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) such that \(F\subseteq C\) and \(\phi(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Its bound is \[L_{\mathrm{CNLP}}=\inf_{x\in C}\phi(x).\] Every original feasible point is admissible in the relaxation with no larger objective value, so \(L_{\mathrm{CNLP}}\le z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex objective underestimator minimized over a convex superset of the MINLP feasible set gives a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(F\subseteq C\).
\(\phi\) is convex on \(C\) and underestimates \(f\) on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{CNLP}}\le z^\star\).

children.title: Polyhedral–Nonlinear Bound Comparison
children.top_down_role: Strength and computational tradeoffs between LP and convex NLP bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral–Nonlinear Bound Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance criterion for LP and convex nonlinear relaxations of the same minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a polyhedron, let \(C\subseteq P\) be convex, and let \(\ell:P\to\mathbb R\) be affine. If \(\phi:C\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfies \(\phi(x)\ge\ell(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), then \[\inf_{x\in P}\ell(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}\ell(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}\phi(x).\] Hence, when both relaxations are valid for the same MINLP, the convex nonlinear bound dominates the LP bound. Without set containment and objective ordering, no general dominance follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex nonlinear bound is at least the LP bound when its feasible region is tighter and its objective underestimator is pointwise stronger.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq P\).
\(\phi(x)\ge\ell(x)\) for all \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{LP}}\le L_{\mathrm{CNLP}}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-MINLP Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-subset relaxation that retains selected mixed-integer nonlinear structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^\star=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\text{ for all }i\in I\}\), where \(X\) contains the retained domain and integrality restrictions. For \(J\subseteq I\), define the restricted-constraint MINLP value \[L_J=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_j(x)\le0\text{ for all }j\in J\}.\] Since the original feasible set is contained in the restricted-constraint feasible set, \(L_J\le z^\star\). Thus dropping constraints, while retaining the chosen mixed-integer nonlinear structure, produces a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining only a subset of the original constraints enlarges the feasible set and yields a restricted-structure MINLP lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(J\subseteq I\).
The problem is in minimization form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_J\le z^\star\).

children.title: Decomposition Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds assembled through structured decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian decomposition of separable blocks coupled by linear equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^\star=\inf\{\sum_{s=1}^m f_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s,\ \sum_{s=1}^m A_sx_s=b\}\), allowing nonconvexity and integrality within each \(X_s\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), define \[d(\lambda)=-\lambda^\top b+\sum_{s=1}^m\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\lambda^\top A_sx_s\bigr).\] Then \(d(\lambda)\le z^\star\) for every \(\lambda\), and the decomposition bound is \(L_D=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}d(\lambda)\le z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing linear coupling constraints separates the MINLP into block subproblems; maximizing their Lagrangian value gives a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective and uncoupled feasible region are block separable.
The coupling constraints are \(\sum_s A_sx_s=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_D=\sup_{\lambda}d(\lambda)\le z^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Restriction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic hierarchy generated by retaining nested subsets of MINLP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the restricted-constraint values \(L_J\), let \(J_1\subseteq J_2\subseteq I\). Their feasible sets satisfy \(F_I\subseteq F_{J_2}\subseteq F_{J_1}\), and therefore \[L_{J_1}\le L_{J_2}\le L_I=z^\star.\] Thus progressively retaining constraints cannot weaken the lower bound in a minimization problem. Equality may occur despite strict inclusion, and computational cost need not be monotone because the retained constraints can alter problem structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested retained-constraint sets produce nondecreasing lower bounds, although their computational costs need not follow the same order.
assumptions_latex: \(J_1\subseteq J_2\subseteq I\).
All values use the same objective and retained domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{J_1}\le L_{J_2}\le z^\star\).

u)=\inf_{x\in X} igl(f(x)+\lambda^	op g(x)+
u^	op h(x) igr).\] Weak duality gives \(d(\lambda,

u}d(\lambda,

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Underestimator Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower bounds obtained by replacing nonconvex functions with convex underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0,\ i\in I\}\), and let \(C\supseteq X\) be convex. Suppose convex functions \(\underline f\) and \(\underline g_i\) satisfy \(\underline f(x)\le f(x)\) and \(\underline g_i(x)\le g_i(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then \[L_U=\inf\{\underline f(x):x\in C,\ \underline g_i(x)\le0\text{ for all }i\in I\}\] satisfies \(L_U\le z^\star\). Global underestimation on the domain containing original feasible points is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the objective and constraints by globally valid convex underestimators creates a convex relaxation whose optimum is a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and contains \(X\).
All displayed underestimator inequalities hold on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_U\le z^\star\).

children.title: Bound-Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural and numerical conditions limiting dual or underestimator validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies pointwise conditions whose violation destroys global lower-bound validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Outer containment, global objective underestimation, and correct multiplier signs are validity conditions, not optional regularity assumptions. For example, consider \(z^\star=\min\{x^2:x=0\}=0\). The surrogate set \(C=\{0\}\) contains every feasible point, but the surrogate objective \(\phi(0)=1\) is not an underestimator; its relaxation value is \(1>z^\star\). Likewise, a set excluding an original feasible minimizer or a Lagrangian inequality multiplier with the wrong sign has no general lower-bound guarantee. Local agreement away from all global minimizers is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation may overestimate the optimum if containment, global underestimation, or Lagrangian sign conditions fail; local accuracy does not restore validity.
assumptions_latex: The comparison uses minimization-form problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of a validity condition can produce \(L>z^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Lagrangian Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical linear multiplier augmentation for inequality- and equality-constrained MINLPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z^\star=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\), define the linear Lagrangian \[\mathcal L(x;\lambda,
u)=f(x)+\lambda^	op g(x)+
u^	op h(x),\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] Its relaxation value is \(d(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}\mathcal L(x;\lambda,
u)\). For every primal-feasible \(x\), \(\mathcal L(x;\lambda,
u)\le f(x)\); hence \(d(\lambda,
u)\le z^\star\). The best linear Lagrangian bound is \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0,
u}d(\lambda,
u)\), with no general zero-gap claim for MINLPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add constraints linearly to the objective with sign-feasible multipliers, minimize over the retained domain, and maximize the resulting lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization problem.
Inequalities are written as \(g(x)\le0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}d(\lambda,\nu)\le z^\star\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Nonlinear Lagrangian and Strong Duality p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contain the integrality restrictions, and consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho\ge0\), define
\[
L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert h(x)\rVert_2^2,
\qquad q_\rho(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L_\rho(x,\lambda).
\]
The augmented relaxation satisfies \(q_\rho(\lambda)\le p^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho\ge0\). Maximizing \(q_\rho\) over any chosen multiplier domain therefore yields a valid lower bound for the minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a quadratic equality-violation penalty to the Lagrangian preserves a valid lower bound when the resulting relaxation is minimized over the mixed-integer domain.

children.title: Penalty-Parameter Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and asymptotic exactness of quadratic equality penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(X\) is compact, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuous, and \(\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). For fixed \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), set
\[
q_\rho(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\left(f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert h(x)\rVert_2^2\right).
\]
If \(0\le\rho_1\le\rho_2\), then \(q_{\rho_1}(\lambda)\le q_{\rho_2}(\lambda)\le p^*\). Moreover,
\[
\lim_{\rho\to\infty}q_\rho(\lambda)=p^*,
\qquad p^*=\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, increasing the quadratic penalty monotonically improves the augmented lower bound, which converges to the equality-constrained optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and nonempty.
\(f\) and \(h\) are continuous on \(X\).
\(\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\rho_1}(\lambda)\le q_{\rho_2}(\lambda)\le p^*\) for \(\rho_1\le\rho_2\), and \(q_\rho(\lambda)\to p^*\).

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Nonlinear Surrogate Dual Method p. 104

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\), where inequalities are componentwise. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), define
\[
S(\lambda)=\{x\in X:\lambda^\top g(x)\le0\},
\qquad q_S(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in S(\lambda)}f(x).
\]
For every such \(\lambda\), the surrogate relaxation satisfies \(q_S(\lambda)\le p^*\) and \(S(\alpha\lambda)=S(\lambda)\) for every \(\alpha>0\). With \(\Delta_m=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m:\mathbf1^\top\lambda=1\}\), the surrogate dual value is
\[
d_S^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}q_S(\lambda)\le p^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted aggregation of all inequalities defines a relaxation; optimizing its value over normalized weights gives the surrogate-dual lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 5.4 Generalized Nonlinear Lagrangian Theory for Singly-Constrained Nonlinear Integer Programming Problems p. 137

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\), let \(\Phi\) be a family of functions \(\phi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\phi(z)\le0\) whenever \(z\le0\). Define
\[
L_\phi(x)=f(x)+\phi(g(x)),
\qquad q(\phi)=\inf_{x\in X}L_\phi(x),
\qquad d_\Phi^*=\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}q(\phi).
\]
Then \(q(\phi)\le p^*\) for every \(\phi\in\Phi\), and \(d_\Phi^*\le p^*\). The linear functions \(\phi(z)=\lambda^\top z\) with \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) form an admissible subfamily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear Lagrangian adds a constraint transformation that is nonpositive on feasible residuals; minimizing it produces a valid lower bound.

children.title: Strong-Duality Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent formulations designed to attain matching primal and dual values.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Duality Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically exact violation-penalty dual for compact mixed-integer domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f\), \(g\), and \(h\) be continuous, and assume \(F=\{x\in X:g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\). Define
\[
V(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\max\{g_i(x),0\}+\lVert h(x)\rVert_1,
\qquad q(\rho)=\min_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\rho V(x)\bigr).
\]
Then \(q(\rho)\le p^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\), \(q\) is nondecreasing on \(\mathbb R_+\), and
\[
\sup_{\rho\ge0}q(\rho)=\lim_{\rho\to\infty}q(\rho)=p^*.
\]
Thus the constrained problem has an exact strong-duality reformulation when the penalty parameter is itself dualized over an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, the supremum of continuous violation-penalty relaxations equals the constrained optimum, even if no finite exact penalty exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(f\), \(g\), and \(h\) are continuous on \(X\).
\(F=\{x\in X:g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup_{\rho\ge0}\min_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\rho V(x)\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{a,b,c\}\), with objective values and constraint residuals
\[
(f(a),g(a))=(1,(0,0)),\quad (f(b),g(b))=(0,(-1,1)),\quad (f(c),g(c))=(0,(1,-1)).
\]
For \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\), the primal feasible set is \(\{a\}\) and \(p^*=1\). The linear Lagrangian dual function and value are
\[
q(\lambda)=\min\{1,-\lambda_1+\lambda_2,\lambda_1-\lambda_2\},\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^2,

d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^2}q(\lambda)=0<p^*=1.

children.title: Duality-Gap Reduction
children.top_down_role: Convexification or augmentation mechanisms that improve dual bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(p^*\in\mathbb R\).
\(q_i(\theta)\le p^*\) for every \(\theta\in\mathcal D_i\).
\(\mathcal D_1\subseteq\mathcal D_2\) and \(q_2(\theta)=q_1(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathcal D_1\).
