notation.meaning: best bound from dual family i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone gap improvement under enlargement of a valid dual family.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Nonlinear Lagrangian and Strong Duality p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a minimization problem have finite primal value \(p^*\). For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal D_i\) be a dual-parameter family with function \(q_i\), and suppose
\[
q_i(\theta)\le p^*\quad\text{for every }\theta\in\mathcal D_i,
\]
\[
\mathcal D_1\subseteq\mathcal D_2,
\qquad q_2(\theta)=q_1(\theta)\quad\text{for every }\theta\in\mathcal D_1.
\]
Define \(d_i^*=\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal D_i}q_i(\theta)\in\mathbb R\) and \(G_i=p^*-d_i^*\). Then
\[
d_1^*\le d_2^*\le p^*,
\qquad 0\le G_2\le G_1,
\qquad G_1-G_2=d_2^*-d_1^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging a valid dual family cannot worsen its best finite lower bound and reduces the duality gap by exactly the bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Nonlinear Lagrangian and Strong Duality p. 113

children.title: Dual Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Relationships under which distinct dual constructions produce the same bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence under value-preserving reciprocal parameterizations of dual families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let two dual constructions have parameter sets \(\Theta_1,\Theta_2\) and dual functions \(q_1,q_2\). They are value-equivalent if maps \(T_{12}:\Theta_1\to\Theta_2\) and \(T_{21}:\Theta_2\to\Theta_1\) exist such that
\[
q_1(\theta)=q_2(T_{12}\theta)\quad\text{for all }\theta\in\Theta_1,
\qquad
q_2(\eta)=q_1(T_{21}\eta)\quad\text{for all }\eta\in\Theta_2.
\]
These reciprocal domination conditions imply
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_1}q_1(\theta)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_2}q_2(\eta).
\]
If both constructions obey weak duality for the same primal value, they therefore have identical duality gaps, although their parameter spaces and maximizers may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two dual families are value-equivalent when each parameterized bound can be reproduced by the other; their optimal bounds and duality gaps then coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are extended-real-valued dual functions for the same primal problem.
The displayed reciprocal value-preserving maps exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_1}q_1(\theta)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_2}q_2(\eta)\).

notation.meaning: parameter set of dual construction i

children.top_down_role: Structural settings where reformulations or augmentations yield different dual values.

assumptions_latex: \(g(x)\le0\) is interpreted componentwise.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_L^*=0<d_N^*=p^*=1\), proving nonequivalence of the two dual regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear and nonlinear penalty duals yield different bounds on one finite problem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Nonlinear Lagrangian and Strong Duality p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{a,b,c\}\), with
\[
(f(a),g(a))=(1,(0,0)),\quad (f(b),g(b))=(0,(-1,1)),\quad (f(c),g(c))=(0,(1,-1)).
\]
For the componentwise-constrained problem \(\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\), the primal value is \(p^*=1\), while the linear Lagrangian dual value is \(d_L^*=0\). Define
\[
V(x)=\max\{g_1(x),0\}+\max\{g_2(x),0\},
\qquad q_N(\rho)=\min_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\rho V(x)\bigr),
\qquad \rho\ge0.
\]
For this nonlinear family,
\[
q_N(\rho)=\min\{1,\rho\},
\qquad d_N^*=\sup_{\rho\ge0}q_N(\rho)=1=p^*.
\]
Thus \(d_L^*<d_N^*\), so the two dual regimes are not value-equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one finite integer problem, the linear Lagrangian dual has a unit gap while a nonlinear violation-penalty dual is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonequivalent Dual Regimes

children.title: Subgradient Dual Search
children.top_down_role: First-order search for nonsmooth dual bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Dual Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected supergradient ascent for a concave Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top g(x)\}\) on \(\mathbb R_+^m\), choose \(\lambda^0\ge0\), positive steps \(\alpha_k\), and an iteration limit \(K\). At iteration \(k\), compute
\[
x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top g(x)\},
\qquad s^k=g(x^k),
\]
then update
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda^k+\alpha_k s^k).
\]
The vector \(s^k\) is a supergradient of the concave function \(q\) at \(\lambda^k\). Stop at \(K\), or earlier under a prescribed bound or step tolerance, and return the sampled multiplier having the largest value \(q(\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the Lagrangian subproblem, use its constraint residual as a dual supergradient, project the ascent step, and retain the best bound.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed Lagrangian subproblem attains its infimum.
The multiplier domain is \(\mathbb R_+^m\).
Positive step sizes \(\alpha_k\) and a finite stopping rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^k=g(x^k)\) is a supergradient of \(q\), and the returned value \(\max_{0\le k\le K}q(\lambda^k)\) is a valid dual bound.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the nonnegative orthant

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top g(x)\}\), and let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) be compact. Given sampled subproblem solutions \(x^1,\ldots,x^k\), solve
\[
U_k=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda,\,t}\left\{t:t\le f(x^j)+\lambda^\top g(x^j),\ j=1,\ldots,k\right\}.
\]
For an optimal master multiplier \(\lambda^k\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top g(x)\}
\]
and append the cut generated by \(x^{k+1}\). At every iteration,
\[
q(\lambda^k)\le\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\le U_k.
\]
Stop when \(U_k-q(\lambda^k)\le\varepsilon\), and return \(\lambda^k\) together with the valid lower bound \(q(\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master maximizes a finite outer model of the dual function; each exact subproblem adds a cut until the master-oracle gap is small.

children.title: Outer Lagrangian Linearization
children.top_down_role: Linear outer models derived from Lagrangian value information.

assumptions_latex: Each sampled Lagrangian subproblem has a minimizer \(x^j\).
The dual function is finite at every sampled multiplier \(\lambda^j\).
The sampled index sets satisfy \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)\le\widehat q_{k+1}(\lambda)\le\widehat q_k(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\).

notation.meaning: supergradient induced by a Lagrangian minimizer
finite outer linearization of the dual function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite polyhedral outer model generated by Lagrangian minimizers.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.2 Outer Lagrangian linearization method p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^\top g(x)\}.
\]
For each \(j\in J_k\), suppose \(x^j\) attains this infimum at \(\lambda^j\), and set \(s^j=g(x^j)\). Then \(s^j\) is a supergradient of \(q\) at \(\lambda^j\), and
\[
q(\lambda)\le q(\lambda^j)+(s^j)^\top(\lambda-\lambda^j)
=f(x^j)+\lambda^\top g(x^j).
\]
Define the outer Lagrangian linearization by
\[
\widehat q_k(\lambda)=\min_{j\in J_k}\{f(x^j)+\lambda^\top g(x^j)\}.
\]
The function \(\widehat q_k\) is concave and polyhedral and satisfies \(q(\lambda)\le\widehat q_k(\lambda)\). If \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\), then
\[
q(\lambda)\le\widehat q_{k+1}(\lambda)\le\widehat q_k(\lambda)
\]
for every \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each Lagrangian minimizer supplies an affine upper support of the concave dual function; the pointwise minimum over nested sample sets is a refinable polyhedral outer model.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer Lagrangian Linearization

children.title: Dual Master Refinement Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Master Refinement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane refinement for maximizing a concave Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\}\) on a multiplier set \(\Lambda\). Given evaluated pairs \((\lambda^i,x^i)\), where \(x^i\) attains the defining infimum, form \(m_k(\lambda)=\min_{i\le k}\{f(x^i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x^i)\}\) and the unrestricted master bound \(U_k=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}m_k(\lambda)\). Select a trial multiplier by maximizing this model or by a trust-region or proximal stabilization, evaluate \(q\) there, and add the resulting affine cut. A valid global stopping test is \(U_k-\max_{i\le k}q(\lambda^i)\le\varepsilon\); a stabilized subproblem value may guide trial selection but must not replace \(U_k\) in this test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine a polyhedral upper model with evaluated dual cuts. Stabilization may select trial multipliers, but the global stopping certificate uses the unrestricted master bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\), and every requested Lagrangian subproblem attains a finite infimum.
\(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), the unrestricted master defining \(U_k\) is solvable, and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), \(q(\lambda)\le m_k(\lambda)\), and therefore \(U_k\) is an upper bound on \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral dual-master model after k oracle evaluations.

children.title: Proximal Bundle Dual Search
children.top_down_role: Stabilized nonsmooth dual optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Bundle Dual Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step proximal bundle method for concave dual maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a concave dual function \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\), retain bundle elements \((\lambda^i,q_i,g_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial^+q(\lambda^i)\), and define \(m_k(\lambda)=\min_{i\in B_k}\{q_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(\lambda-\lambda^i)\}\). From center \(\bar\lambda_k\), compute \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\{m_k(\lambda)-\|\lambda-\bar\lambda_k\|^2/(2t_k)\}\). Evaluate \(q(\lambda^{k+1})\) and a supergradient there. Declare a serious step and set \(\bar\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda^{k+1}\) when actual improvement is at least \(\gamma\) times predicted improvement; otherwise retain the center and take a null step. Stop when the predicted improvement is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle model proposes multipliers; sufficient actual improvement moves the center, while null steps refine the model without moving it.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is finite and concave on the closed convex set \(\Lambda\).
\(t_k>0\), \(0<\gamma<1\), and a dual-value/supergradient oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iteration either improves the serious center or enriches the polyhedral model at the rejected trial point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is plausible and fits the container, but serious-step tests, predicted improvement, stopping rules, and bundle management vary across proximal bundle methods. An authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Surrogate Multiplier Search

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Multiplier Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized multiplier formulation of the surrogate-dual search problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0\}\). For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), define \(S(\lambda)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le0\}\). Because \(S(\alpha\lambda)=S(\lambda)\) for every \(\alpha>0\), multiplier search may be restricted to \(\Delta_m=\{\lambda\ge0:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1\}\). The surrogate-dual search problem is \(d_S=\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}S(\lambda)\). Every evaluated multiplier supplies the valid lower bound \(S(\lambda)\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scale invariance reduces surrogate multiplier search to the simplex, where every evaluated surrogate relaxation yields a valid primal lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem with componentwise inequalities \(g(x)\le0\).
Every evaluated surrogate relaxation has a well-defined extended-real infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\Delta_m\), \(S(\lambda)\le d_S\le v^*\).

children.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Block separation through duplicated variables or relaxed coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-separable dualization of linear coupling equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v^*=\inf\{\sum_{b=1}^B f_b(x_b):x_b\in X_b,\ \sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b=b_0\}\), dualize only the coupling equation. The Lagrangian dual function separates as \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x_b\in X_b}\left\{\sum_{b=1}^B f_b(x_b)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}\left(\sum_{b=1}^B A_bx_b-b_0\right)\right\}=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b_0+\sum_{b=1}^B\inf_{x_b\in X_b}\{f_b(x_b)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_bx_b\}.\] Thus each evaluation of \(q\) consists of independent block subproblems, and the decomposed dual bound is \(d_L=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}q(\lambda)\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing the linking equations separates the Lagrangian evaluation into independent block problems whose optimized dual value is a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_b\) is nonempty; it may contain discrete and nonlinear restrictions.
The primal objective and coupling expression are well defined on \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)\le d_L\le v^*\), and \(q(\lambda)\) is computable by \(B\) independent block infima.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Value Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane cuts for a convex recourse value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be convex and let \(v:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex value function of a parameterized continuous subproblem. If \(v(\bar y)<+\infty\) and \(s\in\partial v(\bar y)\), then \[\eta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\] is valid for every \((y,\eta)\) with \(y\in Y\) and \(\eta\ge v(y)\). In a minimization master, this Benders value cut removes candidates that underestimate recourse while retaining the epigraph of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of a convex subproblem value function gives an affine lower estimator and therefore a valid Benders value cut.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is convex, and \(v:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
\(v(\bar y)\) is finite and \(s\in\partial v(\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}v\subseteq\{(y,\eta):\eta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\}\).

children.title: Benders Feasibility Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-ray feasibility cut for a linear parameterized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the finite-dimensional subproblem feasibility system \(Gx\ge h-Ty\), where \(x\) is unrestricted. If \(r\ge0\) satisfies \(r^{\mathsf T}G=0\), then every parameter \(y\) admitting a feasible \(x\) satisfies the Benders feasibility cut \[r^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\le0.\] If \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar y)>0\), then \(r\) certifies infeasibility of the subproblem at \(\bar y\), and the cut removes \(\bar y\) without removing any parameter whose subproblem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Farkas ray yields a master inequality satisfied by every feasible parameter and violated by the certified infeasible parameter.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is the finite-dimensional linear system \(Gx\ge h-Ty\) with unrestricted \(x\).
A vector \(r\ge0\) satisfying \(r^{\mathsf T}G=0\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\le0\) is valid for every parameter whose subproblem is feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Cutting-Plane Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order separation of a violated convex nonlinear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible region include \(g(x)\le0\), where \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex. At a relaxation point \(\bar x\) with \(g(\bar x)>0\), select \(s\in\partial g(\bar x)\) and add \[g(\bar x)+s^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le0.\] This affine inequality is valid for every point satisfying \(g(x)\le0\) and is violated by \(\bar x\). Reoptimize the master and repeat until no modeled convex constraint is violated beyond the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize each violated convex constraint at the relaxation point; the resulting valid inequality separates that point from the nonlinear feasible set.

\(g(\bar x)>0\), and a subgradient \(s\in\partial g(\bar x)\) is available.

children.title: Column Generation for Structured MINLP
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master methods with nonlinear or mixed-integer pricing subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation for Structured MINLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pricing loop for a block-pattern master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(b\), let \(P_b\) be the feasible pattern set, possibly defined by mixed-integer nonlinear constraints, and let \(c_b(p)\) and \(A_bp\) be a pattern's objective and linking coefficients. Initialize finite sets \(R_b\subset P_b\), solve the restricted linear master, and obtain linking dual multiplier \(\pi\). Solve each pricing problem \[\rho_b=\inf_{p\in P_b}\{c_b(p)-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_bp-\sigma_b\},\] where \(\sigma_b\) is the convexity-row multiplier. Add a minimizing pattern whenever \(\rho_b< -\varepsilon\), then reoptimize. If every exact pricing optimum satisfies \(\rho_b\ge-\varepsilon\), return the restricted-master solution as an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution of the full linear master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted pattern master, price block-feasible MINLP patterns by reduced cost, and add improving columns until exact pricing finds none.
assumptions_latex: The full master is the linear convexification over pattern sets \(P_b\).
Restricted masters and pricing problems are solved to the stated tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact nonnegative reduced costs certify optimality of the restricted-master solution for the full master relaxation.

notation.meaning: Feasible pattern set for block b.
Minimum reduced cost for block b.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The column-generation loop fits the container, but the stated reduced-cost tolerance does not generally imply an epsilon-optimal full-master solution without a bound translating per-block reduced-cost errors into a global objective gap. A precise structured-MINLP column-generation source and corrected tolerance theorem are required.

children.title: Branch-Cut-Price MINLP Interface

children.title: Branching Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of discrete or spatial branching with decomposition state.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition between branch disjunctions and pricing subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-price node with feasible set \(F_N\), a branching disjunction \(D_1,\ldots,D_r\) is pricing-compatible when \[F_N=\bigcup_{j=1}^r(F_N\cap D_j)\] and, for every child \(j\), membership in \(D_j\) can be enforced in each affected pricing problem or by an equivalent restriction on admissible columns. Generated columns at child \(j\) must belong to \(D_j\), while columns violating \(D_j\) must be fixed to zero there. This coverage and enforcement condition guarantees that branching removes the current fractional solution without eliminating any integral solution from all children and prevents pricing from regenerating forbidden columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch disjunction must cover the parent feasible set and be enforceable during pricing so forbidden columns cannot reappear in a child.
assumptions_latex: \(F_N\) is the represented feasible set at the parent node.
Every affected pricing oracle accepts the child restrictions or an equivalent column filter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each parent-feasible integral solution remains representable in at least one child, and every child-generated column respects that child's branch.

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented at the parent node.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Coverage and pricing enforceability are necessary compatibility conditions, but they do not alone guarantee that the disjunction removes the current fractional solution. A source-backed condition must additionally state that the current solution violates every child restriction, or weaken that claim.

children.title: Nonlinear Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Insertion of nonlinear separation results into the search framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving insertion of convex nonlinear cuts into a node master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\) denote the original-space vector represented by a branch-cut-price master, and suppose the global model requires \(g(z)\le0\) for a convex function \(g\). At a point \(\bar z\) with \(g(\bar z)>0\), any \(s\in\partial g(\bar z)\) yields the valid cut \[g(\bar z)+s^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)\le0.\] After expressing \(z\) through the master columns, the cut may be inserted globally if its validity is global, or only in the current subtree if its assumptions are node-local. It excludes \(\bar z\), preserves all feasible represented solutions in its validity domain, and strengthens the node lower bound after reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex nonlinear separation cut is translated into master-column coefficients and installed only where its assumptions make it valid.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex and subdifferentiable at \(\bar z\).
The master representation maps every column combination to its original-space vector \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integrated cut excludes \(\bar z\) without excluding any feasible solution in its declared validity domain.

notation.meaning: Original-space vector represented by master columns.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex cut and validity-domain distinction are plausible, but no source is supplied for branch-cut-price integration. Reoptimization can leave the node lower bound unchanged, so the claim should be nondecrease rather than unconditional strengthening.

children.title: Generated-Column Integration
children.top_down_role: Management of dynamically generated columns within MINLP search.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Column Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent insertion of priced columns into every applicable master row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a priced pattern \(p\) has negative reduced cost and represents original-space vector \(z(p)\). Add a master variable \(\lambda_p\) with objective coefficient \(c(p)\), linking coefficients \(Az(p)\), and coefficient \(1\) in its block convexity row. For every active original-space cut \(a_r^{\mathsf T}z\le b_r\), insert coefficient \(a_r^{\mathsf T}z(p)\) in row \(r\); also impose all node-local bounds and branching restrictions applicable to \(p\). Reoptimize the restricted master. A generated column is fully integrated only when every active row evaluates it exactly as the corresponding original-space pattern, ensuring equivalence between the extended master representation and its projected constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted pattern receives objective, linking, convexity, cut, and branching coefficients before the restricted master is reoptimized.
assumptions_latex: Each generated pattern has a well-defined original-space image \(z(p)\).
All active master rows expose a coefficient-evaluation rule for new patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After complete integration, every active original-space row has the same value on \(p\) as its master-column representation.

notation.meaning: Master weight assigned to pattern p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed coefficient-insertion protocol fits the leaf and is plausible, but its equivalence claim depends on the exact extended-master formulation and active-row semantics. A branch-cut-price source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: MIQP Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous convex-QP relaxation used to bound an MIQP search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization MIQP \(v^*=\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ \ell\le x\le u,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\). At branch-and-bound node \(N\), incorporate its bound changes and fixings into \(\ell^N,u^N\), then drop integrality to obtain \[L_N=\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ \ell^N\le x\le u^N\}.\] The feasible set of every integer descendant of \(N\) is contained in this convex-QP feasible set. Hence \(L_N\) is a valid node lower bound; infeasibility of the relaxation certifies that the node contains no feasible MIQP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply node bounds, relax integrality, and solve the resulting convex quadratic program to obtain a valid node lower bound or infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The MIQP is a minimization problem and \(Q\succeq0\).
Node restrictions are represented by valid bound changes or fixings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\le v_N^*\), where \(v_N^*\) is the optimal integer value in node \(N\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the node's continuous QP relaxation.
Optimal MIQP value within the node.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), suppose the MIQCP has quadratic inequalities \(q_i(x)\leq0\), integer-index set \(I\), and valid node box \([\ell^v,u^v]\). Let \(F_v\) denote its feasible set, including integrality. Drop integrality by allowing \(x_j\in[\ell_j^v,u_j^v]\) for \(j\in I\), and replace each nonconvex inequality function \(q_i\) by a convex underestimator \(\widehat q_i\leq q_i\) valid on the node box. Together with all unchanged convex constraints, these substitutions define a convex relaxation \(R_v\supseteq F_v\). If the objective is \(c^\top x+q_0(x)\) and \(\widehat q_0\leq q_0\) is a convex underestimator on the box, define \[L_v:=\inf\{c^\top x+\widehat q_0(x):x\in R_v\}.\] With \(z_v:=\inf\{c^\top x+q_0(x):x\in F_v\}\), the relaxation satisfies \(L_v\leq z_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic inequalities written with a less-than-or-equal-to-zero orientation, dropping integrality and replacing nonconvex quadratic functions by valid convex underestimators gives a convex node relaxation and a valid minimization lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Node-Bound Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance comparison for minimization relaxations on the same node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_v^a\) and \(R_v^b\) be valid relaxations of the same node feasible set \(F_v\), with the same relaxation objective \(\widehat f\), and define \(L_v^k:=\inf\{\widehat f(x):x\in R_v^k\}\) for \(k\in\{a,b\}\). If \(F_v\subseteq R_v^a\subseteq R_v^b\), then \[L_v^b\leq L_v^a\leq\inf\{\widehat f(x):x\in F_v\}.\] Thus retaining additional valid quadratic constraints or using tighter quadratic envelopes cannot weaken the node lower bound, provided the objective relaxation is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, the smaller of two valid node-relaxation feasible regions yields the stronger lower bound when both use the same relaxed objective.
assumptions_latex: Both relaxations contain the same original node feasible set.
The two relaxation values use the same objective function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v^a\subseteq R_v^b\Longrightarrow L_v^a\geq L_v^b\).

notation.meaning: two relaxation feasible regions at node v

children.title: Convex MINLP Node Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Convex nonlinear and polyhedral outer-approximation node bounds.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The continuous node domain \(C_v\) is a nonempty polyhedron containing every node-feasible point after integrality is ignored.
The functions \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are proper convex functions on \(C_v\), and the selected subgradients exist at their linearization points.
At least one objective linearization is included, and all relaxation values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v^{\mathrm{OA}}\leq L_v^{\mathrm{NLP}}\leq z_v\).

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let \(C_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the polyhedral continuous domain obtained from the node bounds and linear constraints after integrality is ignored. Define the continuous convex feasible region \(Q_v:=\{x\in C_v:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are convex. Its relaxation value is \(L_v^{\mathrm{NLP}}:=\inf\{f(x):x\in Q_v\}\). For finite sets of linearization points, select \(s_{i,y}\in\partial g_i(y)\) and \(r_y\in\partial f(y)\), and define \[P_v:=\{(x,t):x\in C_v,\ g_i(y)+s_{i,y}^\top(x-y)\leq0\text{ for every selected }(i,y),\ t\geq f(y)+r_y^\top(x-y)\text{ for every selected objective point }y\}.\] Then every \(x\in Q_v\) satisfies the constraint cuts, and \((x,f(x))\in P_v\). Consequently, with \(L_v^{\mathrm{OA}}:=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in P_v\}\) and original node optimum \(z_v\), one has \(L_v^{\mathrm{OA}}\leq L_v^{\mathrm{NLP}}\leq z_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ignoring integrality gives a convex NLP relaxation. Supporting-hyperplane cuts for both the constraints and the objective epigraph give a polyhedral outer approximation whose lower bound cannot exceed the convex NLP bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex MINLP Node-Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity contract between a nonconvex relaxation engine and global tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxation package delivered at node \(v\) is globally valid if it supplies a domain \(D_v\), relaxed feasible set \(R_v\), and relaxed objective \(\widehat f_v\) such that \[F\cap D_v\subseteq R_v,\qquad \widehat f_v(x)\leq f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in F\cap D_v.\] Cuts and tightened bounds must be valid on \(F\cap D_v\). If \(w\) is a child, its domain must satisfy \(D_w\subseteq D_v\), and its underestimators and partitions must be certified on \(D_w\). The returned value \(L_v:=\inf_{x\in R_v}\widehat f_v(x)\) is then a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxation engine must return supersets, underestimators, valid cuts and nested child domains; these conditions make its reported optimum a valid global-search lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
All domains, cuts, and underestimators are represented with exact validity semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D_v\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent Bound Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone lower-bound bookkeeping under node refinement and subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an incumbent upper bound \(U\) and a stored lower bound \(B_v\) for every active minimization node. Initialize \(B_v:=L_v\), where \(L_v\) is a valid relaxation bound. After any valid strengthening with value \(L_v'\), set \(B_v\leftarrow\max\{B_v,L_v'\}\). For a child \(w\) of \(v\), initialize \[B_w:=\max\{B_v,L_w\},\] where \(L_w\) is a valid relaxation bound on the child domain. Whenever a feasible solution of value \(z\) is found, set \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,z\}\). Prune node \(v\) only if it is infeasible or \(B_v\geq U\) under the prescribed numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower bounds increase by maxima under refinement and inherit the parent bound; the incumbent decreases by minima, preserving valid pruning decisions.
assumptions_latex: Every relaxation value used in an update is a valid lower bound.
Every recorded incumbent value comes from a feasible solution.
Parent and child problems share the same minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_w\geq B_v\), updated \(B_v\) never decreases, and updated \(U\) never increases.

notation.meaning: stored lower bound for node v

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branching on a fractional integer variable at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node relaxation solution \(\bar x\), choose \(j\in I\) with \(\bar x_j\notin\mathbb Z\). Create two children by adding, respectively, \[x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\qquad\text{and}\qquad x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil.\] Solve or relax each child and return them to the node-selection policy; fathom a child only by infeasibility, integrality with an accepted feasible solution, or a valid bound test. For every integer-feasible point in the parent, exactly one of the two branch inequalities holds, so the branching is exhaustive and does not discard an integer-feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional integer variable using floor and ceiling children; the two children exhaust all integer-feasible points of the parent node.
assumptions_latex: The selected variable is required to be integer in the original model.
Its relaxation value is finite and nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v\subseteq F_v^-\cup F_v^+\) and \(F_v^-\cap F_v^+=\varnothing\) for integer-feasible parent points.

notation.meaning: integer-feasible sets of the two child nodes

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Branching Requests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirements for requesting continuous-domain subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A spatial branching request at node \(v\) is an eligible tuple \((j,s)\) only if the current certified bounds satisfy \(-\infty<\ell_j^v<s<u_j^v<+\infty\), the variable or associated nonlinear expression participates in a relaxation gap, and both child domains can be represented. The request denotes the exhaustive disjunction \[x_j\in[\ell_j^v,s]\quad\lor\quad x_j\in[s,u_j^v].\] Any estimator, cut, or bound transferred to a child must remain valid on that child's domain or be recomputed there. A request failing the strict interior-split condition is ineligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spatial branch requires finite certified bounds, an interior split, and a relevant relaxation gap; all transferred relaxation objects must remain valid on each child domain.
assumptions_latex: The node domain includes certified interval bounds for the selected quantity.
The global search permits overlapping children on their common split boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((j,s)\text{ is eligible}\Rightarrow D_v=D_v^-\cup D_v^+\).

children.title: Rectangular Domain Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Axis-aligned subdivision of bounded continuous domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Domain Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary partition of a bounded rectangular node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=[\ell,u]:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\}\), choose \(j\) with \(\ell_j<u_j\), and select \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\). Define \[D^-:=D\cap\{x:x_j\leq s\},\qquad D^+:=D\cap\{x:x_j\geq s\}.\] Then \(D=D^-\cup D^+\), while \(\operatorname{int}(D^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(D^+)=\varnothing\). Both children are rectangles, their only overlap is contained in \(\{x:x_j=s\}\), and each has strictly smaller width than \(D\) in coordinate \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting one coordinate of a box at an interior point produces two rectangular children whose union is the parent and whose interiors are disjoint.
assumptions_latex: The parent domain is a nonempty bounded rectangle.
The split point lies strictly inside the selected coordinate interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=D^-\cup D^+\) and \(\operatorname{int}(D^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(D^+)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: interior split point in coordinate j

children.title: Subdivision Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing when domain subdivision is useful or prohibitively large.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdivision Selection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility boundary for numerically meaningful spatial subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given node widths \(w_j:=u_j^v-\ell_j^v\), tolerances \(\tau_j>0\), and nonnegative relaxation-gap scores \(g_j\\), a coordinate is eligible for spatial subdivision only if \[j\in E_v:=\{j:-\infty<\ell_j^v<u_j^v<+\infty,\ w_j>\tau_j,\ g_j>0\}.\] A selection rule may choose any \(j\in E_v\) and any split \(s\in(\ell_j^v,u_j^v)\) separated from both endpoints by the prescribed numerical margin. If \(E_v=\varnothing\), coordinate subdivision is unavailable at that node; branching must use another valid disjunction or terminate by a valid stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spatial subdivision is selectable only on finite intervals wider than tolerance and associated with a positive relaxation gap; otherwise another branch or stopping test is required.
assumptions_latex: Widths and relaxation-gap scores are computed from certified node information.
Every numerical margin is positive and no larger than half the eligible interval width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_v=\varnothing\Rightarrow\) no eligible coordinate subdivision exists at node \(v\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative score measuring a relaxation gap involving coordinate j
set of coordinates eligible for subdivision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has no citation, and the positive-gap and tolerance conditions define a solver-specific selection policy rather than a universal mathematical boundary. In addition, the statement contains malformed TeX after g_j. An authoritative source and exact intended policy are needed before a reliable replacement can be reviewed.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching for tightening a bilinear product relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bilinear relation \(w=xy\) on \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), select a factor with nonzero interval width, say \(x\), and choose \(s\in(\ell_x,u_x)\). Create children with \(x\in[\ell_x,s]\) and \(x\in[s,u_x]\), respectively, retain \(w=xy\) for feasible points, and rebuild the McCormick inequalities on each child rectangle. The children cover the parent feasible graph. Because each child uses a smaller factor interval, its McCormick relaxation is contained in the restriction of the parent envelope; repeated exhaustive subdivision drives the envelope error to zero as the rectangle diameters tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a factor interval of a bilinear product and rebuild each McCormick envelope; child graphs cover the parent and their relaxations tighten as boxes shrink.

The split is strictly interior to a factor interval of positive width.
McCormick inequalities are rebuilt using certified child bounds.

source_refs.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93
Disjunctive cuts for nonconvex MINLP p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) be the feasible set at node \(v\), and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) be a finite family satisfying \(F_v\subseteq\bigcup_{r=1}^kD_r\). Create child feasible sets \(F_{v,r}:=F_v\cap D_r\), and construct a valid relaxation \(R_{v,r}\supseteq F_{v,r}\) for each child. Then \[F_v=\bigcup_{r=1}^kF_{v,r}.\] For a minimization problem, if \(L_{v,r}\) is a valid lower bound for child \(r\), then \(\min_{1\leq r\leq k}L_{v,r}\) is a valid lower bound for the parent. The disjuncts may overlap; coverage of the parent feasible set, rather than pairwise disjointness, is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create one child for each member of a finite disjunction that covers the parent feasible set. The children cover the parent even when disjuncts overlap, and the minimum valid child lower bound is valid for the parent.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Branching

source_witnesses.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93
Disjunctive cuts for nonconvex MINLP p. 117

children.title: Hybrid Integer–Spatial Branching
children.top_down_role: Coordination of discrete and continuous branching candidates.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set and \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) is the current node box.
\(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) indexes variables that are integer-constrained at every point of \(F\).
A node relaxation supplies \(\bar x\in B\), and the algorithm supplies a finite, nonempty set of admissible integer and spatial branching candidates with finite real scores.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B\subseteq B^-\cup B^+\), so replacing \(B\) by the selected children preserves every feasible continuation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract globally valid coordination rule for a finite collection of integer and spatial branching candidates in a nonconvex MINLP tree.

source_refs.locator: Global optimization of mixed-integer signomial programming problems p. 349

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer candidate \(j\in I\) with \(\bar x_j\notin\mathbb{Z}\), form \(B^-:=B\cap\{x:x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\}\) and \(B^+:=B\cap\{x:x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\}\). For every selected spatial candidate \((k,\tau)\) with \(\ell_k<\tau<u_k\), form \(B^-:=B\cap\{x:x_k\leq\tau\}\) and \(B^+:=B\cap\{x:x_k\geq\tau\}\). Retain only candidates satisfying \(F\cap B\subseteq B^-\cup B^+\). Apply the prescribed common scoring rule to the finite retained candidate set and branch on a maximizer. Output its two children with all constraints restricted to their respective domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form a finite set of admissible integer splits and continuous spatial subdivisions, score them together, choose a maximizer, and create children whose union retains every feasible point in the current node.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Integer–Spatial Branching

source_witnesses.locator: Global optimization of mixed-integer signomial programming problems p. 349

children.title: Nonlinear Solver Extension Architecture
children.top_down_role: Solver integration of nonlinear separation, propagation, relaxation updates, and incumbent validation.

children.title: Separation Locality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Global and local quadratic or nonlinear cut generation during tree search.

children.title: Root Nonlinear Separation
children.top_down_role: Globally valid quadratic or nonlinear cuts generated at the root.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq D_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set inside the root domain.
\(R_0\supseteq F\) is the current root relaxation.
The separator can certify validity of every inequality it returns on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated halfspace contains \(F\), and hence remains valid at every descendant domain \(D_t\subseteq D_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root separation whose cuts are valid throughout the root domain, including all descendant nodes.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the root relaxation by \(R:=R_0\). Solve it to obtain \(y\in R\). If a nonlinear separator produces inequalities \(a_r^\top x\leq b_r\) satisfying \(a_r^\top x\leq b_r\) for every \(x\in F\) and violated by \(y\), replace \(R\) by \(R\cap\bigcap_r\{x:a_r^\top x\leq b_r\}\) and resolve. Stop when no accepted violated inequality is returned, the relaxation is infeasible, or a prescribed root limit is reached. Store every accepted inequality with root scope \(D_0\), making it eligible at all descendant nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the root, repeatedly add violated nonlinear cuts certified valid for the entire feasible set; these cuts may then be used throughout the search tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Root Nonlinear Separation

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Node-Local Nonlinear Separation
children.top_down_role: Locally valid nonlinear cuts generated within restricted search regions.

assumptions_latex: \(D_t\subseteq D_0\) is the domain of search node \(t\).
\(F_t:=F\cap D_t\) is the node-feasible set and \(R_t\supseteq F_t\) is its relaxation.
The separator certifies returned inequalities on \(F_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strengthened relaxation still contains \(F_t\), while a cut lacking global validity is confined to node \(t\) and its descendants.

notation.meaning: Feasible set restricted to the node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation using inequalities certified only over the current node domain.

source_refs.locator: Global optimization of mixed-integer signomial programming problems p. 349

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve \(R_t\) to obtain \(y_t\). For each returned inequality \(a^\top x\leq b\), accept it only after certifying \(a^\top x\leq b\) for every \(x\in F_t\). If \(a^\top y_t>b\), strengthen the node relaxation to \(R_t\cap\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\). Label the inequality with scope \(D_t\) unless validity has separately been established on \(F\). A cut scoped to \(D_t\) may be activated at node \(s\) only when \(D_s\subseteq D_t\); otherwise it must remain inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local separator adds cuts valid on the current node’s feasible region and restricts their later use to descendants contained in that node domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Nonlinear Separation

source_witnesses.locator: Global optimization of mixed-integer signomial programming problems p. 349

children.title: Separation Locality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity distinctions controlling global reuse or local retention of cuts.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq D_0\) is the root-feasible set and \(D_t\subseteq D_0\) is a node domain.
The proposed cut is the halfspace \(H:=\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A locally valid cut may be exported outside its scope exactly when validity is independently established on the destination feasible region.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between root-global and domain-restricted nonlinear cuts.

source_refs.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cut is root-valid precisely when \(F\subseteq H\), and it is valid at node \(t\) precisely when \(F\cap D_t\subseteq H\). Root validity implies node validity for every \(D_t\subseteq D_0\), but node validity alone does not imply root validity. Indeed, if there exists \(z\in F\setminus D_t\) with \(a^\top z>b\), then activating the cut at any node whose feasible region contains \(z\) deletes a feasible point. Thus a cut certified only on \(D_t\) must remain restricted to domains contained in \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global cuts must contain the whole root-feasible set. A cut valid only on one node domain cannot leave that subtree unless broader validity is separately certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Locality Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

children.title: Nonlinear Enforcement-Propagation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Modular enforcement, checking, propagation, and relaxation of nonlinear constraints.

children.title: Nonlinear Constraint Handlers
children.top_down_role: Modular checking, enforcement, and relaxation services for nonlinear constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set in the current domain, and the handled nonlinear constraint is \(g(x)\leq0\).
A candidate point \(y\in D\) and feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) are supplied.
Every generated relaxation inequality, branch, or infeasibility response is certified for its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A handler returns only \(\operatorname{FEASIBLE}\), \(\operatorname{CUT}\), \(\operatorname{BRANCH}\), or \(\operatorname{INFEASIBLE}\), with the corresponding validity condition.

notation.meaning: Feasible set in the current domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract enforcement contract for one nonlinear constraint or constraint family.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On input \((D,y,\varepsilon)\), evaluate or certify a bound on \(g(y)\). Return \(\operatorname{FEASIBLE}\) only if \(g(y)\leq\varepsilon\). Otherwise return one of: \(\operatorname{CUT}(a,b,S)\), where \(y\in S\), \(F\cap S\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\), and \(a^\top y>b\); \(\operatorname{BRANCH}(D^1,\ldots,D^q)\), where \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{r=1}^qD^r\); or \(\operatorname{INFEASIBLE}\), supported by \(F=\varnothing\). The handler may also request propagation, but it must not declare feasibility or prune the node without the corresponding validity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear constraint handler checks a candidate and responds with certified constraint feasibility, a separating cut valid on a scope containing the candidate, a covering branch, or a node-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Constraint Handlers

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Nonlinear Domain Propagators
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction services driven by nonlinear constraint structure.

assumptions_latex: \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) is the current variable box, and \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) indexes integer-constrained variables.
\(F_B\) is the set of points in \(B\) satisfying the propagated nonlinear constraints and \(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(i\in J\).
Each forward range evaluation, backward contraction, and integer-bound rounding is certified to preserve every point of \(F_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned box \(P(B)\) satisfies \(F_B\subseteq P(B)\subseteq B\), or emptiness certifies \(F_B=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Constraint-feasible points in the box, including declared integrality restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound box contraction for nonlinear constraint domains with explicit treatment of integer-variable bounds.

source_refs.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B^{(0)}:=B\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), apply certified forward range evaluation and backward contraction to obtain \(B^{(k+1)}:=P(B^{(k)})\) with \(F_B\subseteq B^{(k+1)}\subseteq B^{(k)}\). For every \(i\in J\), replace a contracted interval \([\ell_i^{(k+1)},u_i^{(k+1)}]\) by \([\lceil\ell_i^{(k+1)}\rceil,\lfloor u_i^{(k+1)}\rfloor]\). If any component interval becomes empty, return \(\operatorname{INFEASIBLE}\). Otherwise stop when \(B^{(k+1)}=B^{(k)}\), a prescribed contraction tolerance is met, or a work limit is reached, and return \(B^{(k+1)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear propagator repeatedly contracts variable bounds using certified range reasoning and rounds declared integer-variable bounds. It preserves every feasible point and certifies infeasibility when a component interval becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Domain Propagators

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

children.title: Handler–Propagator Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information exchange between constraint enforcement and domain reduction services.

assumptions_latex: Each propagator \(P_r\) is sound: \(F\cap B\subseteq P_r(B)\subseteq B\).
Each handler cut or branch is valid on its declared domain.
The coordination loop uses a finite work limit or a termination tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every intermediate domain and relaxation contains all feasible points remaining in the current node.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound event-driven coupling between nonlinear enforcement and domain propagation.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Begin with node state \((B,R)\). Apply queued propagators until no material bound change occurs or a limit is reached. Rebuild or update \(R\) after bound changes, solve it for a candidate \(y\), and invoke handlers for violated or undecided nonlinear constraints. Valid handler cuts strengthen \(R\); valid branches create covering child domains; new cuts or bounds enqueue affected propagators. Repeat until a handler certifies feasibility, the node is certified infeasible, branching is selected, or the work limit is reached. Because every contraction, cut, and branch preserves \(F\cap B\), coordination cannot remove a feasible node solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation tightens domains before enforcement; handler cuts and bound changes trigger further propagation. Sound component contracts ensure the coordinated loop never deletes feasible node solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Handler–Propagator Coordination

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Relaxator-Cut-Pool Interface
children.top_down_role: Integration of alternative dual bounds and managed nonlinear cut collections.

children.title: Relaxator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Integration points for alternative relaxations and dual bounds.

assumptions_latex: At node domain \(D\), the true feasible set is \(F_D:=F\cap D\).
The objective \(f\) is minimized and the relaxator uses a set \(R(D)\supseteq F_D\).
Any finite lower bound returned by the relaxator is certified for \(R(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns \(L(D)\leq\inf_{x\in F_D}f(x)\), or a valid certificate that \(F_D=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-oriented contract between a nonlinear relaxator and branch-and-bound.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On input \(D\), active valid cuts, and a stopping tolerance, construct \(R(D)\supseteq F_D\) and solve \(L(D):=\inf\{f(x):x\in R(D)\}\) to the declared certification accuracy. Return one of: a certified lower bound \(L(D)\) and a relaxation point \(y\in R(D)\); \(\operatorname{INFEASIBLE}\) with a certificate that \(R(D)=\varnothing\); or \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) without permitting bound-based pruning. The interface must report the cut and domain versions used, so stale results are discarded after either version changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxator builds a node relaxation, returns a certified lower bound and candidate point, or certifies relaxation infeasibility; uncertified failures cannot justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Cut-Pool Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Storage, selection, aging, and reuse of nonlinear cuts.

assumptions_latex: Each stored cut has form \(a^\top x\leq b\) and a declared validity scope \(S\).
The cut is admitted only after certifying \(F\cap S\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\).
A node with domain \(D\) activates only cuts whose scopes contain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cut returned for node \(D\) is valid on \(F\cap D\).

notation.meaning: Validity scope attached to a cut.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving storage and retrieval contract for global and local nonlinear cuts.

source_refs.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut-pool entry is a tuple \((a,b,S,m)\), where \(a^\top x\leq b\) is valid for \(F\cap S\) and \(m\) contains nonmathematical management data. For a node domain \(D\), the pool's eligible set is \(\mathcal{C}(D):=\{(a,b,S,m):D\subseteq S\}\). Retrieval may rank, age, or omit eligible cuts, but it must never return an entry with \(D\nsubseteq S\). Duplicate removal or aggregation is admissible only when the replacement inequalities remain valid on every scope to which they are assigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut pool stores each inequality with its validity scope and returns it only to nodes contained in that scope; management policies cannot weaken validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 6.3.2 Domain cut p. 170

children.title: Relaxator–Cut-Pool Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of valid inequalities and bound information between solver services.

assumptions_latex: The relaxator treats a minimization problem at node domain \(D\), with feasible set \(F_D\), and uses relaxations \(R_k\supseteq F_D\).
Every exchanged cut is valid on \(F_D\) and violated by the current relaxation point.
Every raw lower bound returned by a relaxation solve is certified for \(F_D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_D\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), and the reported certified bounds satisfy \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\).

notation.meaning: Monotone certified lower bound reported at round k.
Raw certified lower bound obtained at round k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative exchange of scoped cuts and relaxation solutions at one node, with explicit monotone aggregation of certified lower bounds.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Retrieve eligible pool cuts for \(D\), form \(R_0\), solve it for a relaxation point \(y_0\) and a raw certified lower bound \(\widehat L_0\), and set \(L_0:=\widehat L_0\). At round \(k\), separate \(y_k\); validate and insert every accepted cut into the pool with its certified scope. Let \(C_k\) be the accepted cuts eligible for \(D\), and set \(R_{k+1}:=R_k\cap\bigcap_{(a,b)\in C_k}\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\). Resolve for \(y_{k+1}\) and a raw certified lower bound \(\widehat L_{k+1}\), then report \(L_{k+1}:=\max\{L_k,\widehat L_{k+1}\}\). Stop when \(C_k=\varnothing\), infeasibility is certified, or an exchange limit is reached. Version both the relaxation and pool so results computed from obsolete cuts are not used for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxator consumes eligible pool cuts and receives newly separated cuts. Valid additions shrink the relaxation, while taking the maximum of the previous and newly certified lower bounds makes the reported minimization bound monotone.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator–Cut-Pool Exchange

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Deferred Feasibility-Validation Interface
children.top_down_role: Deferred nonlinear enforcement and independent incumbent validation.

children.title: Lazy Nonlinear Feasibility Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Deferred enforcement of nonlinear constraints during candidate processing.

assumptions_latex: Candidates satisfy the explicitly enforced relaxation and all integrality conditions.
Deferred nonlinear constraints have form \(g_i(x)\leq0\).
A rejected candidate is accompanied by a valid separating or exclusion response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate is installed as an incumbent only if \(g_i(y)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for every deferred constraint \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred nonlinear checking at integer-feasible incumbent candidates.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever the search proposes an integer-feasible candidate \(y\), evaluate every deferred constraint. If \(g_i(y)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\), accept \(y\) as nonlinearly feasible. Otherwise select a violated index \(j\) and reject \(y\). Before continuing, add either a cut \(a^\top x\leq b\) valid on its declared feasible scope with \(a^\top y>b\), a valid disjunctive branch excluding \(y\), or a no-good constraint that excludes only a discrete assignment proved incapable of nonlinear completion. Never update the incumbent bound with a rejected candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deferred nonlinear constraints are checked only when an integer-feasible candidate appears. A violating candidate is rejected and receives a valid cut, branch, or justified no-good exclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Nonlinear Feasibility Enforcement

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Incumbent Validation Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Independent nonlinear feasibility checks for prospective incumbents.

assumptions_latex: The callback receives a candidate \(y\) and a finite family of deferred constraints \(g_i(x)\leq0\), indexed by \(i\in I\), with tolerances \(\varepsilon_i\geq0\).
All integrality conditions and explicitly enforced constraints have already been checked.
Constraint evaluations or residual bounds used by the callback are certified to the declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(\operatorname{ACCEPT}\) response certifies all deferred inequalities within tolerance; every \(\operatorname{REJECT}\) response identifies a certified violation and a valid search response.

notation.meaning: Finite index set of deferred constraints.
Deferred constraint function indexed by i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound acceptance, rejection, and unresolved responses produced by an incumbent-validation callback.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(i\in I\), the callback computes certified residual bounds \([\underline r_i,\overline r_i]\ni g_i(y)\). It returns \(\operatorname{ACCEPT}\) only when \(\overline r_i\leq\varepsilon_i\) for every \(i\in I\). It returns \(\operatorname{REJECT}(j,W)\) only when \(j\in I\) and \(\underline r_j>\varepsilon_j\), where \(W\) records the violated index, residual bound, evaluation tolerance, and a valid cut, branch, or exclusion request. If neither conclusion is certified, it returns \(\operatorname{UNRESOLVED}\), triggering tighter evaluation rather than acceptance or permanent exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback accepts only when certified residual bounds satisfy every deferred constraint, rejects only with a certified violation and valid search response, and reports unresolved numerical cases without deciding.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Validation Callbacks

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Rejected-Incumbent Responses
children.top_down_role: Solver responses when callback validation rejects a candidate solution.

assumptions_latex: The candidate \(\bar x\in\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\) satisfies all currently enforced constraints and violates a deferred constraint \(g_j(\bar x)\le 0\).
A rejection function \(c_j:\mathbb R^{p+q}\to\mathbb R\) is available such that \(c_j(x)\le 0\) for every feasible point \(x\) of the original MINLP and \(c_j(\bar x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding \(c_j(x)\le 0\) rejects \(\bar x\) without removing any feasible point, after which the discrete search may resume. A no-good constraint excluding the entire integer assignment of \(\bar x\) is valid only if that assignment has independently been shown to admit no feasible continuous completion.

notation.meaning: Incumbent candidate returned by the discrete solver.
Globally valid rejection or separation function.

review_flags: source locator requires a section or page
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract valid-separation response to a deferred nonlinear-feasibility rejection; assignment-wide exclusion requires a separate infeasibility justification.

source_refs.locator: Part VI. Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar x\), identify a deferred constraint with \(g_j(\bar x)>0\). Add a globally valid rejection constraint \(c_j(x)\le 0\) satisfying \(c_j(\bar x)>0\), and then continue the search. If no such constraint or other solver-supported valid rejection action is available, report that the response cannot safely exclude the candidate. Do not exclude the entire integer assignment merely because the particular mixed point \(\bar x\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject the incumbent with a globally valid separating constraint and resume the search; exclude its entire integer assignment only when every continuous completion of that assignment has been shown infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Rejected-Incumbent Responses

source_witnesses.locator: Part VI. Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Optimization

children.top_down_role: Candidate-generation and improvement families that complement exact global certification.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Candidate Repair Calculus
children.top_down_role: Conversion of relaxation solutions into nonlinear-feasible mixed-integer candidates.

children.title: Relaxation-Solution Rounding
children.top_down_role: Discrete candidate construction from fractional relaxation solutions.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation solution is \(x^R=(z^R,y^R)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^q\), with bounded integer domain \(Z\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\).
A deterministic tie-breaking rule and a projection metric are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a mixed-integer candidate \(\hat x=(\hat z,y^R)\) with \(\hat z\in Z\). It guarantees integrality and respect for discrete bounds, but it does not by itself guarantee nonlinear feasibility or objective improvement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearest-domain rounding of the integer block; nonlinear feasibility is delegated to a subsequent repair step.

source_refs.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^R=(z^R,y^R)\), compute \(\hat z\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}\|z-z^R\|\), using the prescribed tie-breaking rule. For separable box domains this reduces to componentwise nearest-integer rounding followed by bound projection. Form \(\hat x=(\hat z,y^R)\), evaluate all original constraints, and pass \(\hat x\) to nonlinear feasibility repair if any violation exceeds tolerance. Output \(\hat x\) only as an integral candidate, not as a certified feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the relaxation's integer coordinates onto their admissible lattice, retain the continuous coordinates, and send any nonlinear violations to a repair procedure.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Solution Rounding

source_witnesses.locator: Algorithms and software for convex mixed integer nonlinear programs p. 1

children.title: Variable Partitioning Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction through restricted discrete or continuous partitions.

assumptions_latex: The discrete index set \(I\) is finite and the relaxation point \(x^R\) is available.
Each \(i\in I\) has a nonnegative priority score \(s_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule produces a disjoint partition \(I=F\mathbin{\dot\cup}R\), where variables in \(F\) are fixed to admissible integer values and variables in \(R\) remain available for repair or neighborhood search.

notation.meaning: Indices retained for repair or local search.

review_flags: priority score is heuristic and problem dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic score-based partition used to balance discrete commitment against remaining repair freedom.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a threshold \(\tau\ge 0\) or a cardinality budget \(k\). Set \(F=\{i\in I:s_i\ge\tau\}\) or select the \(k\) largest-score indices, and let \(R=I\setminus F\). Fix every \(i\in F\) to an admissible rounding of \(x_i^R\); retain variables indexed by \(R\) in the subsequent mixed-integer repair neighborhood. Ties are resolved by a fixed index order. The partition is recomputed only when the relaxation point or the scores change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank discrete variables, fix a selected high-priority subset, and leave the remainder free for repair or neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Partitioning Heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited introductory section does not specifically support the proposed score threshold, top-k partition, or update rule. Moreover, fixing each coordinate to an individually admissible rounding need not produce values extendable to a coupled discrete domain. A source and a precise domain-aware fixing rule are required.

children.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration of nonlinear feasibility after discrete candidate construction.

assumptions_latex: Finite index sets \(J\) and \(K\), an integral assignment \(\hat z\in Z\), an initial continuous vector \(y^0\in Y\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) are given.
For every \(j\in J\) and \(k\in K\), the functions \(g_j(\hat z,\cdot)\) and \(h_k(\hat z,\cdot)\) are evaluable on the closed continuous domain \(Y\).
The violation weights satisfy \(\rho_j\ge 1\) for \(j\in J\) and \(\rho_k\ge 1\) for \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned point \((\hat z,y^*)\) satisfying \(V_{\rho}(y^*)\le\varepsilon\) has \(g_j(\hat z,y^*)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(|h_k(\hat z,y^*)|\le\varepsilon\) for every \(k\in K\). Otherwise the procedure reports repair failure without claiming that the fixed assignment \(\hat z\) has no feasible continuous completion.

notation.meaning: Finite inequality and equality index sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local continuous feasibility restoration after fixing or rounding the discrete variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\hat z\), define \(V_{\rho}(y)=\sum_{j\in J}\rho_j\max\{0,g_j(\hat z,y)\}+\sum_{k\in K}\rho_k|h_k(\hat z,y)|\). Starting from \(y^0\), apply a constrained local method to reduce \(V_{\rho}\) over \(Y\), increasing selected weights when violations stagnate. Stop successfully at \(y^*\) only when \(V_{\rho}(y^*)\le\varepsilon\); otherwise stop at the prescribed iteration limit or a stationary point and report repair failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the integer variables fixed, locally reduce a weighted aggregate of nonlinear violations and accept only when the aggregate is small enough to imply that every individual residual is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Repair

children.title: Fixed-Integer Local NLP
children.top_down_role: Continuous local optimization after fixing discrete decisions.

assumptions_latex: The MINLP has variables \((z,y)\in Z\times Y\), objective \(f:Z\times Y\to\mathbb R\), a finite inequality index set \(J\), functions \(g_j:Z\times Y\to\mathbb R\) for \(j\in J\), a finite equality index set \(K\), and functions \(h_k:Z\times Y\to\mathbb R\) for \(k\in K\).
A discrete assignment \(\bar z\in Z\) and an initial continuous point \(y^0\in Y\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated local solution \(y^*\) of the reduced NLP yields the mixed-integer candidate \((\bar z,y^*)\). It is an admissible incumbent only if all original constraints pass the required numerical feasibility test. Failure of the local NLP solver is not a certificate that the fixed assignment \(\bar z\) has no feasible continuous completion.

notation.meaning: Finite inequality and equality index sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced continuous nonlinear program induced by one fixed discrete assignment.

source_refs.locator: Using interior-point methods within an outer approximation framework for mixed integer nonlinear programming p. 225

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed discrete assignment \(\bar z\in Z\), the fixed-integer local NLP is
\[
\min_{y\in Y} f(\bar z,y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_j(\bar z,y)\le 0\ \text{for every }j\in J,\qquad h_k(\bar z,y)=0\ \text{for every }k\in K.
\]
Initialized at \(y^0\), a local NLP solver seeks a stationary or locally optimal feasible point \(y^*\) and may instead return a failure status. Any computed point must be validated against the original constraints before it is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix the discrete assignment and locally solve the resulting continuous nonlinear program; validate any computed mixed-integer point, and do not interpret local solver failure as an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Integer Local NLP

If the transition procedure returns a candidate \(\tilde x^k\) that passes all integrality and nonlinear-feasibility tests and satisfies \(f(\tilde x^k)\le f(x^k)-\eta_k\), set \(x^{k+1}=\tilde x^k\). Otherwise set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\), revise the transition neighborhood or restoration parameters, and continue. assumptions_latex: The binary-continuous feasible set is \(F=\{(z,y):z\in\{0,1\},\ y\in\mathbb R,\ y^2\le z,\ (y-2)^2\le 1-z\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both discrete slices are empty, although a continuous relaxation may contain points satisfying weakened constraints. Thus rounding or deforming a relaxed point cannot guarantee a feasible discrete transition; restoration can fail for every integer assignment.

If \(z=1\), the constraint \((y-2)^2\le 0\) forces \(y=2\), while \(y^2\le 1\) is violated. Hence \(F=\varnothing\). assumptions_latex: A candidate \(\bar x\in\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_h,\varepsilon_b,\varepsilon_I\ge 0\) are given.
All original nonlinear functions and variable bounds are evaluated at \(\bar x\) using the designated validation precision.

children.title: Global Bound Validation

knowledge_statements.title: Global Bound Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically guarded certificate for a minimization problem with a validated incumbent and relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). Suppose an incumbent has reported value \(\widehat U\), with independently validated feasibility and objective-error bound \(\eta_U\ge 0\), and a global relaxation supplies \(\widehat L\), with certified bound error \(\eta_L\ge 0\). If every \(x\in F\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge \widehat L-\eta_L\), then \[\widehat L-\eta_L\le p^*\le \widehat U+\eta_U.\] For prescribed \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), global optimality within tolerance is certified when \[(\widehat U+\eta_U)-(\widehat L-\eta_L)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|\widehat U+\eta_U|\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated error margins turn a relaxation bound and feasible incumbent into an enclosing interval for the global optimum and an explicit optimality-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and the problem is a minimization problem.
The incumbent is independently feasible under the stated validation tolerances.
The relaxation bound is valid for every point of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*\in[\widehat L-\eta_L,\widehat U+\eta_U]\), with tolerance-global optimality when the displayed gap test holds.

eg V_F\wedge
